item.title: [TEST DRIVE] Lexus RX500h packs punch with refined ride
item.description: The Lexus RX500h F Sport Performance quickly dispels the conventional notion that a Lexus hybrid is built only for quiet, comfortable cruising. When pressing the accelerator hard, the large SUV responds with surprising force, building speed with a steady surge, as the turbocharged engine and electric motors work together. The power delivery is smooth rather than abrupt, retaining the refinement expected of a Lexus. But underneath that composure is a powertrain capable of making the 2-ton-plus SUV move with authority. The RX500h F Sport Performance combines a 2.4-liter four-cylinder turbocharged gasoline engine with electric motors to produce a combined 371 horsepower. It is the most powerful version of the RX, Lexus' flagship midsize luxury SUV, adding a distinctly sportier character to a model long associated with quietness and comfort. The fifth-generation RX, launched in Korea in 2023, traces its roots to the original RX introduced globally in 1999. The performance-oriented character is visible before the engine is started. item.title: Enduring legacy of 'hanji,' Korea's traditional paper
item.description: MUNGYEONG, North Gyeongsang Province — With a history spanning more than 1,000 years, "hanji," traditional Korean paper, has played a vital role in the Korean Peninsula's cultural and intellectual development. First produced during the Three Kingdoms period (57 B.C. – A.D. 668), hanji became essential to the spread of Buddhism, the growth of publishing and the development of printing technology. During the Silla and Goryeo dynasties, Korean paper gained recognition throughout Asia for its exceptional whiteness, smooth texture and durability, becoming a sought-after export in China and Japan. Production expanded further during the 1392-1910 Joseon Dynasty to meet growing demand for books and scholarly publications. Next week, hanji is poised for a major moment on the international stage, as centuries of papermaking knowledge and practices are expected to be inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. The final decision is expected at a UNESCO committee meeting in Xiamen, China, slated for Nov. 30 to Dec. 5. Keeping heritage At a time when industrial machinery and chemical

item.title: Your guide to 'hanji' experiences in Korea
item.description: There is a quiet resilience woven into every sheet of hanji, Korea’s traditional mulberry paper. Said to last a thousand years, hanji is far more than a historical artifact — it is a living, breathing medium that bridges ancient craftsmanship and contemporary design. For those looking to escape digital noise and the business of city life, a journey into the world of hanji offers a tactile connection to Korea's cultural roots. While there are many places in Seoul to experience the versatility of hanji, options within the capital are tailored toward crafting rather than raw manufacturing. Jong Ie Nara Paper Art Museum in central Seoul's Jung District stands out as Korea’s first paper culture museum and specialize institution, offering rich exhibitions and ustomized experience programs that draw large numbers of visitors. Meanwhile, artisan-centered spaces like Jonginamoo Gallery are tucked into the charming alleyways of Bukchon Hanok Village in Jongno District, where many workshops specialize in small-group experiences for crafting traditional items like jewelry boxes and lamps. Beca

item.title: Why do celebrities keep driving drunk despite having so much to lose?
item.description: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. They can afford chauffeurs and have people willing to help them. An arrest for drunk driving can cost them their public image and force them to suspend their careers. Yet news of celebrities driving under the influence continues to surface, with some getting behind the wheel again even after being punished. Why do they keep making the same choice despite having so much to lose? The question has long been raised overseas, too. CNN's former entertainment program “Showbiz Tonight” once examined cases involving Lindsay Lohan, Nicole Richie and Paris Hilton, asking, “Why don't they hire a driver when they have the money and the means?” The program looked beyond the cost, pointing to attitudes shaped by special treatment, environments in which risky behavior goes unchecked and persistent drinking problems. Paris Hilton explained her drunk driving case in a 2007 interview on CNN's “Larry King Live.” She said she had had one drink and was on her way to a restaurant a few blocks away. She acknowledged that she should not have been driving.

item.title: When celebrities play poor, viewers see privilege, not relatability
item.description: “Wow, look at that expression," said a man watching a barista at Blank Street Coffee in London in March 2024. The barista captivating customers was Sabrina Carpenter, a famous American singer-songwriter and actress. She took orders and handed out drinks just like an ordinary coffee shop worker. The event was part of a promotional campaign for her new song “Espresso.” The coffee shop posted a photo of Carpenter on social media, captioning it, “Working late because she’s a barista.” For fans, it was a special opportunity to receive coffee directly from their favorite star. But when attention shifted from the celebrity to the workplace, the same scene took on a different meaning. Carpenter was working in a low-wage service job while wearing a luxury outfit by Fendi. The promotional caption about “working late” stood in stark contrast to the reality of workers who must stay behind the counter until late to make ends meet. Some criticized the event as “playing ordinary people.” The idea of having the singer of “Espresso” serve coffee was clever, but an event that borrow

item.title: A Tribute to Blacklisted Lyricist Yip Harburg: The Man Who Put the Rainbow in The Wizard of Oz
item.description: His name might not be familiar to many, but his songs are sung by millions around the world. Today, we take a journey through the life and work of Yip Harburg, the Broadway lyricist who wrote such hits as “Brother, Can You Spare a Dime?” and who put the music into The Wizard of Oz, the movie that inspired the hit Broadway musical and now Hollywood blockbuster, Wicked. Born into poverty on the Lower East Side of Manhattan, Harburg always included a strong social and political component to his work, fighting racism and poverty. A lifelong socialist, Harburg was blacklisted and hounded throughout much of his life. We speak with Harburg’s son, Ernie Harburg, about the music and politics of his father. Then we take an in-depth look at The Wizard of Oz, and hear a medley of Harburg’s Broadway songs and the politics of the times in which they were created.

item.title: Focker-In-Law isn't terrible. It's just a sitcom
item.description: Focker-In-Law is nothing compared to 2000's Meet the Parents. item.title: Nearly $4.7M in drugs, cash seized in months-long investigation in northern Ontario
item.description: Canada’s largest Indigenous police service has seized nearly $4.7 million in drugs and cash across several remote First Nations in northern Ontario. In all, 172 charges were laid against 68 people, the majority from northern Ontario, with some from Toronto, Winnipeg, Fort St. James, B.C., and Chezzetcook, N.S. The news comes after the launch of a new border control pilot program.

item.title: US Army detonates toxic explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Army detonated a massive cache of toxic explosives stored in a tiny Iowa farming town on Wednesday, saying the materials were too unstable to move to a safer area and warning residents to shelter from the blast and a potential cloud of lead dust. Officials said the 68 drums of lead azide — the entire U.S. stockpile of the degraded material — were at risk of spontaneous explosion, requiring their destruction at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, where they had been stored for more than 15 years. Measures were put in place to curb potential contamination from the destruction of the nearly five tons of explosive material, but the Army encouraged residents of Middletown, Iowa and other nearby areas to leave prior to the blast "out of an abundance of caution." Locals taped up windows to guard against flying glass and were urged to stay indoors to avoid possible toxic dust. The controled explosion sent debris flying into the air and a large cloud of smoke over a tree line, while a New York Times reporter said the blast could be heard some 10 miles (15 kil

item.title: US proposes tariffs over excess production, retains 15% cap for Korea, Japan, EU
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in U.S. midterm elections. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20 percent to 40 percent to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting. But the U.S. Trade Representative's office said it intends to cap new tariffs at lower levels agreed under trade deals that are completed or still under negotiation. In unveiling the results of an eight-month unfair trade practices investigation into excess industrial capacity, USTR aims to more fully rebuild Trump's tariff leverage after the Supreme Court in February struck down his broad global duties under a national emergencies law. The effort also seeks to put Trump's tariffs and associated trade agreements on more solid legal and political grounds by backing them with a court-tested trade law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, and addressing foreign subs

item.title: From 6 days to 5: Busan subway cleaners finally find time for life beyond work
item.description: “Back then, there were no machines. You had to wring it out by hand. You step on this bar with your foot, grab the two strands of the mop and twist them tightly with your rubber-gloved hands.” Han Kyung-sun, 66, demonstrated how to wring out a mop, springing to her feet as she explained the evolution of cleaning equipment at Minam Station on Busan Metro Line 3 on Nov. 10. Wearing red rubber gloves, she gripped the mop strands and twisted them, sending dirty water dripping to the floor. Han is a 16-year veteran cleaner employed by Busan Transportation Operation & Service. She is currently responsible for the station's restrooms, escalators, platform screens and station office. When she first started cleaning, she had to wring out heavy, water-soaked mops with both hands. Later, a foot-operated mop wringer, nicknamed “squeezer,” made the work easier. This year, the introduction of wet vacuums further reduced her workload. Han, who used to carry buckets, mops and a wringer, now heads into the station with just a vacuum cleaner and a damp mop. item.title: Mathmatician-turned-Buddhist monk leans into inner cultivation for AI era
item.description: “Inner cultivation to manage alienation and depression will become increasingly important in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). We need ‘metacognition’ — the ability to objectively observe our own mental state — to regulate and overcome our emotions.” Ven. Ilmuk, a 61-year-old Buddhist monk who has practiced meditation in Korea and abroad for 30 years and taught meditation, has published his first book in five years, "Buddha’s Breathing Meditation" (Bulkwang Publishing). Based on the early Buddhist scripture "Anapanasati Sutta" (Mindfulness of Breathing), the book offers a detailed guide to the principles and practice of breathing meditation. It covers everything from the basic steps of observing one’s breath to obstacles that hinder meditation and ways to overcome them, as well as the process of cultivating concentration and wisdom to end suffering. The book presents breathing meditation as a path that leads beyond mental tranquility to liberation. item.title: Inflation remains uncomfortably high despite retreat in gas prices as challenges mount for the Fed
item.description: WASHINGTON — A key inflation gauge remained high last month even as gas prices cooled in a sign that elevated costs remain a challenge for the Federal Reserve and elected officials in Washington. The Commerce Department said Wednesday that consumer prices rose 3.8 percent in October from a year earlier, up from 3.6 percent in September. On a monthly basis, consumer prices climbed 0.3 percent from September to October, down from a 0.6 percent increase the previous month. The stubbornly elevated price figures come as the economy is expanding at a healthy pace, driven by strong consumer spending and surging business investment as large tech firms splurge on building out AI infrastructure. Consumer spending has been resilient even as persistent inflation raises the costs of many necessities and has soured most Americans on the economy. Yet much of the spending is driven by upper-income households, and there are signs poorer Americans are relying more on credit to sustain their spending. item.title: US finds no evidence China directed executive to spy on Nvidia CEO, WSJ reports
item.description: U.S. officials found no evidence that tech executive Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with a classified briefing. The briefing comes after U.S. President Donald Trump cleared the way for Jensen Huang's reinstatement earlier this week, assuring Nvidia that its CEO posed no national-security threat. The controversy began with concerns over Alice Huang's alleged Chinese intelligence links and whether her relationship with Jensen Huang affected suspected diversions of Nvidia chips to China. Officials from the CIA, FBI, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and National Security Agency briefed staff from congressional intelligence committees and chamber leaders, the Journal reported. The officials said Alice Huang contacted China's spy agency during the affair but found no indication that she provided significant intelligence, the Journal reported. item.title: US Justice Dept did not open probe into Huang before reinstatement, sources say
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Jensen Huang before U.S. President Donald Trump pushed for his return as Nvidia chief executive this week, despite active probes into the chipmaker's customers and allegations he conducted an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence, according to three people familiar with the matter. Instead, Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that there was no evidence the tech titan had broken any laws based on the Justice Department's ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity. That determination, which is subject to change as the probes continue, was crucial to Blanche's decision to tell Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the weekend that he possessed no evidence that Huang posed a risk to national security, said two of the people. Jensen Huang's reinstatement has angered members of Congress — both Republicans and Democrats

item.title: Iran says Israel trying to deceive US into war with chemical weapons claim
item.description: TEHRAN — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Israel was trying to drag the United States into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons. "This warmonger shamelessly accuses Iran... of developing and concealing such heinous weapons in pharmaceutical factories. The objective is audacious: to deceive the U.S. into fighting yet another war on its behalf," he wrote in a statement posted on X. Israel has for years accused Iran of trying to acquire nuclear weapons, but Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz on Tuesday alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons and vowed to stop the Islamic republic from obtaining them. "Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons but has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them," said Katz in a statement published by his Likud party on Telegram. "We must not allow this to proceed." But a key ally of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said Wednesday there was no need to attack Iran immediately and questioned the caretaker government's intentions. Avigdor Liberm

item.title: Gold falls 3% to more than one-year low after data shows US inflation rose further
item.description: Gold fell more than 3 percent to its lowest level in more than a year after strong U.S. inflation data failed to assuage concerns surrounding the Federal Reserve's rate-hike path. Spot gold was down 3 percent to $3,445.89 per ounce by 11:13 a.m. ET (1613 GMT), hitting its lowest level since August 2025. The metal fell below the key $3,500 level for the first time since September 2025. U.S. gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.3 percent to $3,445.10. U.S. inflation rose further in October, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index rising 0.3 percent after an unrevised 0.5 percent gain in September, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said on Wednesday. "With inflationary pressures remaining significantly above the Fed target, the likelihood continues that the Fed will raise interest rates moving forward, which adds pressure to gold," David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, said. "That's been one of the main themes that remains a headwind for the gold market, and today's PCE data did nothing to allay those concerns." Elevated rates

item.title: N. Korea expels Swiss diplomat over sanctions weeks after office reopening
item.description: North Korea has expelled the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered the envoy to leave within 48 hours, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, in a spat over sanctions less than a month after Bern reopened the office. The ministry said the move was in response to the Swiss decision to put sanctions on North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp, calling it an overtly hostile act in a statement carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency. Pyongyang's Foreign Ministry summoned the head of the diplomatic office, Sylvain Astier, and handed him a memorandum urging him to close the office, the news agency said. "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours," it said, using the country's official name. "Any act of violating the sovereign rights of the DPRK and the interests of its citizens can never be welcomed by us." item.title: Anthropic's slide tests Wall Street's lofty bets on future AI profits
item.description: Anthropic's slide below its initial public offering price has sharpened investor scrutiny of lofty technology valuations, as markets increasingly question whether even the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom can generate enough profit to justify their price tags. Shares of the Claude developer were trading around $80.50, well below their $83 offer price and nearly 30 percent below their opening price on November 19. The swift reversal highlights growing unease over how much investors are willing to pay for future growth, even as earnings prospects improve for many companies benefiting from artificial intelligence. Of the 86 Nasdaq-100 companies with positive earnings multiples and available earnings revision data, 60 saw their forward 12-month earnings forecasts rise over the past three months, a Reuters analysis of LSEG data showed. Yet, shares in 37 of those companies declined over the same period. Nvidia shares have fallen about 25 percent over the past three months despite a nearly 20 percent increase in its earnings forecasts, partly driven by the volatile swings around CEO Jensen

item.title: EU leaders divided over budget spending as they weigh $49 bil. loan to Ukraine
item.description: BRUSSELS — European Union leaders struggled on Thursday to bridge major differences over the bloc’s long-term budget and agree a new $49 billion loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year. At a summit in Brussels, some leaders called for belts to be tightened, while others defended traditional policies that consume large parts of the budget. Most want extra funds for important new priorities, and to help Ukraine almost five years into the war. “Europe needs solid finances. We can’t and we mustn’t take on more debt,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said, in remarks that highlighted some of the contradictions. “At the same time there is a series of tasks we must fulfill reliably.” “The priorities must be a flourishing economy, the internal market must be able to develop its full potential, and we need better defense,” he told reporters. item.title: Olive Young reports data breach affecting 790 people
item.description: CJ Olive Young said Thursday that personal information belonging to some of its employees and customers was compromised after its internal business system was hit by a cyberattack. The country's leading health and beauty retailer said it confirmed unauthorized external access to its internal business system on Monday, resulting in the exposure of personal information contained in some company records. Membership numbers belonging to 790 people were exposed. In some cases, the leaked data also included names, IP addresses, member IDs, phone numbers, dates of birth and email addresses. The affected individuals include 639 employees, 106 employees of partner companies and 45 customers. No payment information or passwords were compromised, the company said. Upon detecting the breach, Olive Young said it immediately isolated the affected system from the network, blocked unauthorized access routes and deactivated the attacker's account. It also notified the relevant authorities.

item.title: Temu commits to changing some of its commercial practices in EU, Commission says
item.description: BRUSSELS — Chinese e-commerce platform Temu has committed to bringing several of its commercial practices in line with EU consumer protection laws, the European Commission said on Thursday. "Temu's commitments concern a broad range of commercial practices that mislead consumers or unduly influence their purchasing decisions, including fake discounts, fake reviews, pressure selling, forced gamification, and missing and misleading information," the Commission said in a statement. Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it would provide clearer and more accessible information for customer support, prices, environmental claims and checkout, and would make refunds easier. Temu also committed to ending forced gamification features, like spinning the wheel to access the marketplace, and pressure-selling messages, the Commission said. A Temu spokesperson said the company was pleased to have reached a resolution. "We appreciate the constructive engagement throughout the process and will continue to strengthen transparency and improve the shopping experience for consumers across Europe." Count

item.title: Lee approves confirmation hearing requests for ministerial, spy chief nominees
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung has approved requests for parliamentary confirmation hearings for four ministerial nominees and his pick to lead the state intelligence agency, the presidential office said Thursday. The move comes three days after Lee announced a Cabinet reshuffle and nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service (NIS). Lee also tapped former lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister, ruling Democratic Party Rep. Han Jun-ho as interior minister and senior presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung as culture minister, presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a press notice. Under the Personnel Hearing Act, the National Assembly must complete the confirmation hearing process within 20 days of receiving the requests. If the Assembly fails to submit the hearing reports by the deadline, Lee may set a new deadline of up to 10 days for their submission. If the Assembly fails to meet the extended deadline, Lee may proceed with the appointments without the reports.

item.title: Police seek arrest warrant for top scorer of tax accountant exam accused of AI-assisted cheating
item.description: Police on Thursday filed for an arrest warrant for the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam accused of cheating on the test using artificial intelligence (AI) technology. Earlier this month, the man, surnamed Han, admitted to using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative AI to score top marks on the exam, sparking public outcry and concerns over cheating in national exams. Police sought Han's warrant on charges that include obstruction of official duties. The move reportedly reflected the magnitude of the incident involving a state exam and concerns over the suspect possibly fleeing or destroying evidence. Han, who scored a near-perfect score in the first round of the exam, made the admission after facing scrutiny over what many saw as unrealistically high scores.

item.title: Int'l legal body urges extreme caution over push to impeach Korea's chief justice
item.description: An international legal association voiced concern over the ruling party's push to impeach the chief justice, urging extreme caution to safeguard judicial independence. In a statement released Thursday, the Law Association for Asia and the Pacific (LAWASIA), acknowledged the constitutional legitimacy of impeachment but stressed the need to uphold fundamental democratic principles. "LAWASIA acknowledges that impeachment is a remedy recognized by the Constitution of the Republic of Korea, and that no person or institution is above the law," the statement read. "LAWASIA emphasises, however, that any action taken by government against the courts must be exercised with extreme caution." LAWASIA represents legal professionals and leading legal associations across some 40 jurisdictions in the Asia-Pacific region. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) plans to seek the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae as early as next week. item.title: Lee touts new deposit system as effective in curbing illegal fishing by Chinese vessels
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday touted a tightened deposit system introduced by the Coast Guard, saying it has been significantly effective in curbing illegal fishing by Chinese vessels. Lee made the remarks in a post on his X account, sharing a news report that an increasing number of Chinese fishermen have given up their boats and abandoned illegal operations due to the financial burden since the Coast Guard began requiring deposits of up to 1.5 billion won ($1.1 million) in May from Chinese vessels caught fishing illegally. The Coast Guard requires the deposits in exchange for the release of Chinese vessels caught fishing illegally and their crew members. Previously, the maximum deposit was capped at 300 million won. "The significant increase in the deposit for illegal fishing has been very effective," Lee wrote, adding that the government will "strongly safeguard South Korea's fishing rights." item.title: Defense minister calls for easing tension with Russia after air defense zone entry
item.description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Thursday called for efforts to ease tensions with Russia, after Russian warplanes flew into Korea's air defense zone and almost breached its territorial airspace earlier this week. Two Russian Tu-160 supersonic strategic bombers and two other fighter jets entered Korea's air defense identification zone (KADIZ) in the East Sea early Tuesday. They came within about 1 kilometer of the airspace over Ulleung Island off the east coast, prompting the Korean Air Force to scramble fighter jets in response. Seoul has lodged a strong protest with the Russians over their repeated unannounced and unauthorized entry into KADIZ. "I believe we need to make efforts to ease tensions at this point," Kang said during a parliamentary session. "While we maintain communication channels with Russia, I believe we should do more." Kang said Seoul clearly conveyed to the Russian side the need for an advance notice and coordination in case of flying any military plane near the Korean territory so as to avoid any accidental clash. item.title: Korea secures final victory in ISDS case brought by Iran's Dayyani family
item.description: The Korean government has secured a final victory in the second investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) arbitration brought by six members of Iran's Dayyani family, the justice ministry said Thursday. The ministry said the dismissal of the entire 770 billion won ($573 million) claim has become final, as the Dayyani family did not file a challenge with a British court to set aside the second ISDS arbitral award within the statutory deadline. As a result, the Korean government is not only free from any obligation to pay the claimed amount but will also recover 4.8 billion won in legal costs, it said. The case traces back to 2015, when the Dayyanis, a major shareholder of Entekhab Industrial Group, filed for arbitration after Korea's state-run Korea Asset Management canceled a contract to sell a major stake in Daewoo Electronics to Entekhab in 2011. In a 2018 arbitration, Seoul was ordered to pay 73 billion won plus interest in compensation to the Dayyanis over the failed takeover of Daewoo Electronics. The ruling was finalized in December 2019, with Seoul making a payment in April 2022. Th

item.description: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo said Thursday that Seoul should break the deadlock with Pyongyang through small, practical steps rather than a push for high-level talks. “Given the current state of inter-Korean relations and the situation on the Korean Peninsula, I think it might be better to start with smaller and more practical steps rather than pursue high-level talks,” Hong said during a doorstep interview in Seoul. item.title: Exhibition in Seoul explores cultural roots of Gwangcheon 'gim'
item.description: As Korean food gains fans worldwide, "gim," or dried seaweed, has moved from everyday Korean tables to fine dining menus, becoming one of the country’s hottest exports. To highlight the history and culinary versatility behind one of the country’s most recognized seaweed-producing regions, Hongseong County in South Chungcheong Province recently opened a pop-up exhibition titled “Hongseong Seafood Market, Do You Know Gim?” in Seoul. The exhibition focuses on Gwangcheon, a town in Hongseong where more than 40 companies produce hundreds of varieties of seasoned gim. While “Gwangcheon gim” is widely known among consumers, organizers said many people mistakenly view it as a single commercial brand rather than a regional industry built over decades. "This exhibition focuses on gim produced in Gwangcheon to raise awareness of Hongseong’s rich local resources, showing that the region has much more to offer beyond well-known specialties like strawberries," an official from the event organizer said. Displays at the venue trace how Gwangcheon developed into a center for seaweed producti

item.title: Samsung reorganizes memory, system LSI units to boost AI chip competitiveness
item.description: Samsung Electronics has consolidated its memory development operations under the direct supervision of the head of its memory business division, industry sources said Thursday. The latest organizational shuffle also expanded the sales and marketing organization of its system LSI division, which oversees chip design, they said. The changes are aimed at accelerating the development of next-generation memory technologies to strengthen the company's position in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market, the sources said. Yoon Ha-ryong, who previously headed the memory marketing team at Samsung's Device Solutions America (DSA), which oversees Samsung's semiconductor production in the United States, has been tapped to lead the company's U.S. operations. Hwang Sang-joon, who previously headed both the memory development division and the DRAM development team, was promoted to head of the memory business division.

item.title: PPP refuses to recommend special counsel candidate to probe alleged fabricated indictments
item.description: Two candidates were recommended by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) and a minor opposition party Thursday to lead a special counsel probe into allegations of fabricated indictments against President Lee Jae Myung, while the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) refused to make a recommendation. A special counsel bill was passed by the National Assembly earlier this month and approved by the Cabinet last week, calling for an independent counsel to investigate suspicions that the prosecution under former President Yoon Suk Yeol fabricated evidence or induced false testimonies to build cases against then opposition leader Lee and others. The new special prosecutor is to be chosen by President Lee from among three candidates recommended by the DPK, the PPP and the minor Rebuilding Korea Party. item.title: FM Cho reaffirms Korea's non-involvement stance on US-Iran war in call with Iranian counterpart
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Thursday explained Korea's plans to expand the operational area of its naval unit near the Strait of Hormuz and reaffirmed its non-involvement stance on the U.S.-Iran war during phone talks with his Iranian counterpart, the foreign ministry said. Cho held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East, bilateral relations and the protection of Korean nationals abroad, according to the ministry. item.title: Real household income falls despite chip export boom
item.description: Real household income in Korea fell for the first time in 10 quarters in the third quarter, according to data released Thursday by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The decline came even as the economy grew 3.4 percent in the quarter, buoyed by a semiconductor boom, and was expected to expand in the high 3 percent range this year. The benefits of economic growth were uneven across households. Lower-income families earned less from work and received less in transfers while facing higher interest payments, further widening the income gap. Average monthly household income rose 0.8 percent from a year earlier to 5.48 million won ($4,080), the data showed. Adjusted for inflation, however, it fell 2.1 percent, the first decline since the first quarter of 2024, when real household income fell 1.6 percent. The decline stands in contrast to the rise in real gross domestic product (GDP), which grew 3.4 percent over the same period. item.title: KOSPI edges up despite BOK rate hike
item.description: The benchmark KOSPI edged up 0.29 percent Thursday despite the central bank’s rate hike, with chipmakers leading the rebound. The index recouped only a fraction of its loss of more than 6 percent in the previous session. The benchmark KOSPI closed at 4,711.21 after opening 1.01 percent higher at 4,745.10. The index briefly climbed above the 4,800-mark but gave up most of its gains toward the close. Institutional investors led the buying, purchasing a net 750.9 billion won ($560 million), while foreign investors and retail investors recorded net sales of 113.6 billion won and 1.04 trillion won, respectively. Samsung Electronics rose 0.35 percent to close at 171,300 won, while SK hynix gained 2.23 percent to finish at 1,053,000 won. The widely anticipated rate hike appeared to have little effect on investor sentiment. The Bank of Korea (BOK) raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage point to 3.25 percent, citing persistent inflationary pressures and stronger-than-expected economic growth driven by the semiconductor export boom. item.title: Real estate developer-led consortium expresses intent to acquire troubled retailer Homeplus: sources
item.description: A consortium led by a real estate developer is reportedly pursuing the acquisition of the troubled discount store chain Homeplus, industry sources said Thursday. The consortium, comprised of a real estate developer and a logistics company, has submitted a letter of intent (LOI) to purchase the entire retail chain, according to sources. The lead underwriter is said to be monitoring the market situation while being open to non-binding offers from other bidders, they added. In September, the Seoul Bankruptcy Court approved a corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus, wholly owned by private equity firm MBK Partners. But the discount store chain has been struggling to repay its debts amounting to 1.3 trillion won ($968.3 million) due to a liquidity crunch. Homeplus has suspended online delivery services as of Thursday morning. It will also temporarily close 67 stores that were in operation starting Friday.

item.title: Korea challenges US claims of state-led manufacturing overcapacity
item.description: Korea is pushing back against Washington's claim that its industrial policies are contributing to structural excess capacity in manufacturing, as a new U.S. tariff investigation raises concerns over whether support for domestic semiconductor production could face further trade pressure. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said Thursday that it disagrees with much of the evidence cited by the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), arguing that Korea's industrial policies are driven by market demand and companies' investment decisions rather than government efforts to expand production beyond actual demand. It emphasized that it would seek to preserve the 15 percent tariff ceiling agreed under last year’s bilateral trade deal. “There are substantial parts of the report cited by the USTR that we cannot agree with. Korea’s industrial policies are based on a market economy and driven by companies’ investment demand. A minister-counselor-level diplomat from the Russian Embassy visited the ministry's headquarters earlier in the day, where the two sides discussed the entry of Russian military aircraft into the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) and other pending issues, according to the diplomatic sources. item.title: Interior ministry to train local officials to prevent erroneous disaster alerts
item.description: The interior ministry said Thursday it will provide special training for local government officials responsible for issuing civil defense alerts to prevent the erroneous transmission of emergency disaster messages. The special training will take place for two days next week for about 170 officials from 16 metropolitan and provincial governments nationwide, the ministry said. The measure follows an incident on Tuesday, in which North Gyeongsang Province authorities sent an emergency alert to the East Sea island of Ulleung containing incorrect information, causing confusion among residents. At that time, several Russian warplanes briefly entered South Korea's air defense zone over the East Sea but the province's civil defense warning control center described them as aerial objects presumed to be North Korean aircraft in its emergency message sent to the island. item.title: Lee calls for accelerating '7 Seeds' project to gain edge in future industries
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung called for efforts Thursday to accelerate the government's "Seven Seeds" initiative aimed at fostering growth in seven key future industries, including renewable energy and quantum technology. Lee made the call during a meeting with his key aides at Cheong Wa Dae, referring to the initiative announced in August, alongside the administration's "three megaprojects," which aim to secure global leadership in the manufacturing of artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors, data centers and physical AI. The Seven Seeds initiative identifies seven future-oriented sectors as potential engines of economic growth and aims to support their sustainable development. The designated sectors are small modular reactors (SMRs), nuclear fusion, renewable energy, quantum technology, aerospace, advanced biology and supply chains for advanced materials and components. item.title: Starbucks opens hanok-inspired store at N Seoul Tower
item.description: The main entrance of Starbucks's N Seoul Tower branch, set to open Friday, is seen in this handout photo. The company's 15th special store in Korea is located on the fourth and fifth floors of the Seoul landmark on Mount Nam and incorporates key elements inspired by traditional Korean hanok architecture. The store offers exclusive drinks, including a latte made with scorched rice, a traditional Korean ingredient, and a cocktail inspired by makgeolli, a traditional Korean rice alcohol. item.title: [COVER STORY] Gov't weighs banning part-time work for int'l students lacking Korean proficiency
item.description: International students who fall short on Korean language requirements could face a complete ban on part-time work, even if when they were enrolled in English-taught programs. The Ministry of Justice is reviewing the measure, along with plans to shorten post-graduation stays for those with limited Korean proficiency. If implemented, the measures would make Korean language skills a key determinant of international students' ability to work and stay in the country. The proposed changes come as Korea reassesses its international student policy amid growing concerns that aggressive recruitment by universities — sometimes involving inducement of guaranteeing part-time work — may come at the expense of educational quality. The number of international students in Korea stood at 307,464 as of April, surpassing the government's 2027 target of 300,000 ahead of schedule. The figure rises to nearly 400,000 when including some 30,000 graduates seeking employment. item.title: PPP files complaint against special counsel for 'legal distortion' following Daegu mayor's acquittal
item.description: The main opposition People Power Party (PPP) on Thursday filed a complaint against a special counsel team for allegedly distorting the law in indicting Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho, who was recently acquitted of charges related to the 2024 martial law declaration. The PPP's legal advisory committee submitted the complaint to police against special counsel Cho Eun-suk and members of his team, accusing them of deliberately hiding key evidence and treating allegations as established facts without sufficient evidence. "Concealing key evidence for political purposes and distorting facts to apply the law forcibly, even though the requirements for establishing the crime were not met, undermines the fairness of the criminal justice system and the foundations of the rule of law," PPP Rep. Kim "stressed the importance of consolidating all the Party cells into the ones of single ideology and will, steadfast in their revolutionary faith and obligation," according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). item.title: Korean-British YouTube couple with 10 mil. subscribers announce divorce
item.description: Jin and Hattie, a Korean-British couple who rose to fame through their YouTube channel with 10.1 million subscribers, have announced their divorce, saying they will continue to manage their social media platforms separately. Heo Jin-woo and Harriet Emily shared a lengthy statement Wednesday on their YouTube community page and social media accounts announcing their separation. "After much thought and many conversations behind the scenes, we have made the decision to end our marriage and move forward separately," they said. item.title: PM expresses gratitude to CSAT supervisors, promises to look for ways to lessen burden next year
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook expressed gratitude Thursday to test supervisors at last week's annual college entrance exam, saying they must have remained on edge throughout the test due to a series of measures added to prevent cheating and that the government will look for ways to minimize their burden next year. Thousands of additional personnel, usually school teachers, were mobilized to supervise the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), known as Suneung in Korean, to enforce a series of anti-cheating measures, including checking test-takers' glasses and clothing. "This year's Suneung was an unfamiliar experience for both students and teachers," Han said on X. "As teachers checked the students' glasses and clothing, they likely remained on edge until the very end, anxious about whether anything had been overlooked, yet equally concerned that an unnecessary suspicion might hurt a student's feelings." item.title: Hoban's Hanjin KAL investment turns into exit dilemma
item.description: With Delta Air Lines throwing its weight behind Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae, Hoban Group is left with few viable options to challenge the incumbent leadership at Hanjin KAL, potentially prompting the construction group to consider an exit from its investment. Delta holds a 14.9 percent stake in Hanjin KAL, bringing its combined shareholding with Cho and his related parties, who own 20.58 percent, to 35.48 percent. Hoban and its affiliates hold 20.69 percent, making them the airline group's largest shareholder bloc by a narrow margin. The gap could widen further if Cho completes his planned purchase of an additional 325,000 shares, equivalent to 0.49 percent, lifting his bloc's stake to approximately 21.07 percent and putting him back ahead of Hoban as the largest shareholder by Jan. 1. Hoban's options for building a rival shareholder coalition also appear limited. The state-run Korea Development Bank (KDB), which holds a 10.58 percent stake, recently reiterated that it has no immediate plans to sell its shares. item.title: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
item.description: WASHINGTON — Chinese consumer rights advocate Wang Hai has spent three decades exposing counterfeit goods and seeking compensation for buyers. In recent months, he left China fearing he was a target of the authorities, but now he is stranded in South Korea with his family, facing possible deportation home. Wang, a well-known campaigner against counterfeit goods, said China invalidated his passport and South Korean authorities rejected his asylum. The United States also revoked his tourist visa, narrowing his options for leaving South Korea and deepening his fears of being sent back to China. Chinese authorities launched a campaign against organized crime in July, saying they would target “malicious compensation claims.” Since then, authorities have arrested at least 100 people for allegedly extorting businesses through anti-counterfeiting work or consumer compensation claims, according to official statements reviewed by The Associated Press. Wang said the arrests made him fear he could be next, prompting him to leave a country where official Chinese media had once praised him for

item.title: New bills target stealth recording with AI glasses
item.description: Lawmakers of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea have proposed bills to stop people from secretly filming others with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered smart glasses, amid growing concern that wearable cameras are making illegal filming harder to detect. Rep. Lee Ju-hee and 18 DPK colleagues have submitted an amendment to the Information and Communications Network Act to require makers and importers of wearable cameras to include a recording indicator that people nearby can easily recognize. It is one of two bills in what the lawmaker calls the “Smart Glasses Illegal Filming Prevention Act,” introduced earlier this week. The other bill would also require individuals who film others with such devices to signal that they are recording. Existing rules cover only the stage when footage is distributed, according to the lawmakers. Moreover, the Personal Information Protection Act's requirements apply only to operators who film for business purposes; they don’t apply when individuals wear a device and film for private reasons. item.title: LG Chem plans $11 bil. R&D push to go beyond petrochemicals
item.description: LG Chem plans to invest 15 trillion won ($11.2 billion) in research and development by 2035 as it seeks growth beyond petrochemicals in which persistent global oversupply has squeezed profitability. The company said it will direct 70 percent of that investment to priority businesses, including materials for semiconductors, mobility and robotics, as well as new cancer drugs. LG Chem aims to double its electronic materials business to 2 trillion won by 2030 from the current 1 trillion won, driven by advanced semiconductor packaging materials. To support this growth, the company has established new R&D teams dedicated to semiconductors and automotive electronics, as well as a business development unit that reports directly to the CEO. As artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing drives demand for denser, multilayer chip packages, LG Chem is expanding beyond memory chips into packaging materials for AI and other nonmemory chips. item.title: Integrated LCC headquarters to be based in Busan
item.description: The headquarters of the integrated low-cost carrier (LCC) formed through the merger of Air Busan, Jin Air and Air Seoul will be based in Busan, the city government said Thursday. Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo and Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae reached the agreement during a meeting in Busan, paving the way for the launch of the integrated airline in March next year. The agreement follows close consultations between the city and Korean Air, with Hanjin Group making the decision in consideration of Busan's growth potential and the importance of balanced national development, according to the city government. The integration follows Korean Air's acquisition of Asiana Airlines, scheduled to be completed on Dec. 17. Under the broader restructuring, Korean Air's Jin Air will be integrated with Asiana Airlines' Air Busan and Air Seoul to form a single low-cost carrier. The integrated LCC will operate a fleet of 60 aircraft, comprising 33 from Jin Air, 21 from Air Busan and six from Air Seoul, all under the Jin Air brand. item.title: Law banning foreigners' political activity ruled unconstitutional
item.description: The Constitutional Court ruled Thursday that a provision of the Immigration Act imposing a general ban on political activity by foreign residents does not conform to the Constitution, with six of the nine judges agreeing. To prevent a legal vacuum, however, the court kept the clause in effect until it can be revised, no later than Dec. 31, 2028. The provision was introduced in 1977. A 2005 amendment added an exception for political activities permitted under other laws, but the general ban stayed in place. Violators can be ordered to halt the activity or leave the country and those without permanent resident status may face deportation. In 2021, two Mongolian international students planned to request preliminary candidates in the 20th presidential election present policies to address discrimination against foreign nationals living in Korea. They filed a constitutional complaint that July after learning the law barred them from political activity. The court found that freedom of expression, unlike voting and other political rights, is a constitutional right that applies to both citizens a

item.title: FM nominee says Korea-US alliance 'strong enough to overcome any difficulty'
item.description: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon dismissed concerns about recent friction with Washington, Thursday, saying the alliance is resilient enough to weather any challenge. "The alliance has evolved over more than 70 years. Given that long history and the values and interests our two countries share, I believe the two can overcome any difficulty," Lim said during a doorstep interview in Seoul. "I don't think the Korea-U.S. alliance is so fragile that any particular issue could shake it." He also struck a balanced tone on relations with Beijing. “I believe both our alliance with the U.S. and our relationship with China are important to us. I don't think there is a single country that doesn't matter to South Korea.” His remarks came amid a strain in Seoul-Washington ties. item.title: HS Hyosung promotes 2 CEOs to presidents
item.description: HS Hyosung said Thursday it promoted Ahn Sung-hoon, CEO of HS Hyosung, and Seong Nak-yang, CEO of HS Hyosung Advanced Materials, from executive vice presidents to presidents in its 2027 executive reshuffle. Born in 1971, Ahn joined Hyosung Group in 2000 after a stint at global consulting firm Bain & Company. He spent nearly two decades at Hyosung Heavy Industries, serving as executive vice president overseeing its power systems business, before becoming HS Hyosung's inaugural CEO in 2024. The group credited him with stabilizing the organization and strengthening its business competitiveness following its launch. Seong previously served as CEO of Yahoo Korea and Doosan Glonet, as well as a global partner at McKinsey and Accenture and head of management innovation at Hyosung Group. He became CEO of HS Hyosung Advanced Materials following the group's launch. He was recognized for leading the company's entry into silicon anode materials, a key next-generation battery component, and securing new growth opportunities. item.title: US military confirms inactivation of Apache helicopter squadron in South Korea
item.description: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) confirmed Thursday that an Army aviation unit in South Korea has been inactivated, noting that the move does not change the United States' military force posture or commitment to the defense of the Asian ally. The inactivation of the 5th Air Cavalry Squadron, 17th Cavalry Regiment (5-17 ACS) at Camp Humphreys, a key U.S. base in Pyeongtaek, some 60 kilometers south of Seoul, came amid lingering speculation that the U.S. could consider a troop realignment to better address broader regional security challenges, including from China. "The inactivation of the 5-17 Air Cavalry Squadron is part of the U.S. Army's broader force structure and aviation transformation efforts to modernize capabilities and optimize formations for future operational requirements," the USFK said in response to a question from Yonhap News Agency. "This action does not change U.S. Forces Korea's mission, posture, or commitment to the defense of the Republic of Korea," it added, referring to South Korea by its official name. item.title: Gov't considering inspection of official discipline at KEPCO over repeated data breaches
item.description: The government is considering conducting an inspection of official discipline at Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) following repeated personal information leaks from the state-run power utility, officials said Thursday. The Office for Government Policy Coordination released the statement, saying it "takes seriously the recent series of incidents where significant harm to the people is feared due to large-scale personal information leaks at public institutions." "In particular, we are considering conducting an inspection of official discipline and conduct at Korea Electric Power where personal data breaches occurred back to back in November and October," the office said, adding that violations will be dealt with sternly to heighten awareness regarding the protection of personal information. KEPCO said Sunday that personal information belonging to 650,487 users of its KEPCO ON customer service platform and 869,761 users of its electronic procurement system, known as SRM, had been leaked, a month after a separate leak affecting tens of thousands of people.

item.title: Hana Financial chief cleared in final ruling on bank hiring case
item.description: Hana Financial Group Chairman Ham Young-joo’s acquittal on an obstruction of business charge became final, Thursday, eight years after he was indicted in a case involving hiring at Hana Bank. The Seoul Western District Court upheld the original acquittal on remand, saying the lower court’s decision “appears justified.” The prosecution had sought a three-year prison sentence at an earlier hearing. Speaking to reporters outside the courthouse after the ruling, Ham apologized for the concern the case had caused and pledged to “do my utmost to run Hana Financial Group more fairly and transparently.” Ham was indicted in June 2018 for allegedly manipulating a job applicant’s scores at an acquaintance’s request during Hana Bank’s 2015 recruitment of entry-level employees, when he headed the lender. He was also accused of instructing the human resources department to favor male applicants in the lender’s open recruitment, setting a hiring ratio of four men for every woman, in violation of the Equal Employment Opportunity Act. item.title: Food alleys, seasonal dishes tapped to turn K-food fans into repeat Seoul visitors
item.description: Seoul is looking to turn its signature food alleys, seasonal dishes and late-night street dining into major draws for repeat international visitors, the head of the Seoul Tourism Organization said at a forum on Wednesday. Speaking on a panel titled "The Power of Gastronomy Captivating the World: K-Food and Global Culinary Tourism" hosted by Kyung Hee University’s College of Hotel and Tourism Management, Seoul Tourism Organization CEO Kim Byung-min joined Josun Palace executive chef Son Jong-won and Dean Suh Won-seok to map out how Korea's capital can convert global fascination with Korean cuisine into long-term tourism growth. Kim described tourism as a "comprehensive art industry" linking lodging, transit, cultural experiences and dining, arguing that culinary strategy must be tied to broader urban competitiveness rather than treated as a standalone sector. item.title: Japan's data center boom faces growing revolt from urban residents
item.description: KASHIWA — Until a few years ago, Susumu Goto’s house in Kashiwa, northeast of Tokyo, looked out on a grassy field where neighbors played baseball and soccer. Today, a couple of 31-meter-tall (102-foot) data centers owned by Hong Kong-based asset manager PAG loom in front of it. At least once a month, tests of backup generators send black fumes into the sky and the smell of burning fuel hangs in the air. “Every morning when I step outside, my whole view is swallowed up by the buildings," said the retired auto mechanic. “It feels oppressive. Seeing that day after day takes a real mental toll.” Each building is the size of a large warehouse but as tall as a 10-story apartment block. Loose regulation and political stability have made Japan a magnet for data center investment even as other countries have put administrative brakes on the industry. But about 60 percent of data centers are in and around the densely populated Tokyo metropolitan area, home to about 37 million people, and growing opposition from residents has prompted a review of an industry the government is counting on

item.title: Hyundai Motor Group names new CEOs at 4 affiliates
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group has appointed new CEOs at four affiliates in a reshuffle aimed at strengthening core businesses and accelerating its shift toward electrification and software-defined vehicles (SDVs). The group announced the appointments Thursday and said they would boost competitiveness and synergies across its affiliates. Baek Cheol-seung, currently CEO of Hyundai Transys, has been promoted to president and appointed CEO of Hyundai Mobis. Baek has extensive experience in the automotive and auto parts industries, with a track record of improving profitability and operational efficiency. He will focus on optimizing Hyundai Mobis' business portfolio and strengthening its competitiveness in electrification and automotive electronics. Park Chan-young, executive vice president and head of Hyundai Motor Group's procurement division, has been named CEO of Hyundai Transys. He has played a key role in strengthening the group's electrification supply chain and expanding parts localization. item.title: Korean Air to expand flight, cargo networks after Asiana merger
item.description: Korean Air plans to increase flight frequencies, spread out departure times and expand its cargo network following its integration with Asiana Airlines on Dec. 17. Asiana flights will use Korean Air flight numbers, increasing the number of flights operated under the Korean Air brand by 50 percent. The carrier will also take over 11 international routes previously operated exclusively by Asiana, including to Barcelona Airport in Spain and Clark Airport in the Philippines, and launch new services to Melbourne, Australia and Hiroshima, Japan. Flights from Incheon to New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport will increase from three to four a day, with departures in both the morning and afternoon. item.title: Images of Seoul landmarks meet vintage travel gear in Kodak collab
item.description: Images of Gwanghwamun, N Seoul Tower and Sungnyemun are being reimagined as vintage-inspired clothing and travel accessories in a new Seoul-themed merchandise line. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday it is launching five fashion items in collaboration with Kodak Apparel on Friday, blending the city's official brand, Seoul My Soul, with the American photography brand's signature analog-film aesthetic. The collection draws on Kodak's 138-year history and explores Seoul's daily transformation from bustling daytime streets to atmospheric nighttime scenery, translating familiar city landmarks into retro-style graphics. The designs feature faded colors and textures reminiscent of film photography, alongside the Seoul My Soul logo, highlighting the city's blend of past and present. The collection comprises three T-shirt designs, one cap and one travel bag. The shirts feature photographs and typography inspired by Seoul's landscape, with relaxed silhouettes and understated colors. item.title: New late-night Seoul bus connects Gangnam, Hongdae with major downtown tourist hubs
item.description: Seoul is making late-night travel easier for visitors and night owls by launching the Firefly Bus, a late-night route that connects major tourist and entertainment hubs across both sides of the Han River, linking the upscale Gangnam business and shopping district south of the river with the central shopping hub of Myeong-dong, eastern landmark Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) and the western nightlife district of Hongdae. The Seoul Metropolitan Government will begin operating the bus on Friday night, offering residents and international visitors a way to travel between major destinations after regular public transportation services have ended. The route, designated Firefly 01, starts at Gangnam Station, passes Banpo Hangang Park, Seoul Station, Myeong-dong, DDP and Gwanghwamun, and turns around at Hongik University Station before returning to Gangnam. Covering 50 kilometers and 62 stops, the service will operate daily, including weekends and public holidays, with eight buses running at intervals of 20 to 30 minutes. item.title: Rescene, aespa, BTS most popular K-pop stars in Korea, China, Japan: Melon
item.description: Girl groups Rescene and aespa, and boy group BTS were the most popular K-pop acts this year in Korea, China and Japan, respectively, a local music platform said Thursday. Melon released its first report based on data from the Global-K Chart, a joint chart launched in June by the Korean platform, China's Tencent Music and Japan's Line Music, and various metrics tracking K-pop fan engagement worldwide. After analyzing respective daily charts of each platform from May 11, when tracking for the global chart began, through Sept. 30, Melon said Rescene had the most No. 1 rankings on its chart, while aespa and BTS topped the Tencent Music and Line Music charts, respectively. "While BTS proved to be a 'living legend' anywhere in the world, Rescene's hit 'Love Attack' began its chart resurgence in earnest in July in Korea, revealing distinct K-pop consumption landscapes in each country," Melon said. Seven acts reached No. 1 at least once on the integrated chart during the tracking period: BTS, aespa, BIGBANG, Le Sserafim, Riize, Stray Kids and Itzy. BTS and aespa stayed in the Top 10 the longest

item.title: SK Chemicals' bio-based plastic used in specialty coffee drippers
item.description: SK Chemicals' high-performance copolyester has been used in specialty coffee drippers developed by Korean brand Hello World, highlighting the material's potential in premium kitchenware. The company said Thursday that its Ecozen material has been applied to Hello World's V3 01 Neon Green and V3 02 Black drippers, which are exported to 15 countries. Hello World CEO and product developer Jay Kim selected Ecozen for its heat resistance and low thermal conductivity, which help maintain water temperature during coffee extraction. Partially made from plant-based biomass, Ecozen can withstand boiling water at up to 100 degrees Celsius while retaining the low thermal conductivity of conventional plastics. This combination makes it suitable for pour-over coffee brewing, where stable water temperatures are essential to extracting desired flavors and aromas. Unlike metal, which transfers heat quickly, Ecozen helps minimize heat loss during brewing. "In pour-over coffee, a range of factors, including water temperature, extraction time and flow rate, shape the flavor and aroma of the coffee," Kim said

item.title: Too charming to hate: Lee Se-young steals the show in 'The Remarried Empress'
item.description: Playing a villain audiences cannot quite bring themselves to hate, actress Lee Se-young has delivered a career-defining performance as Rashta in the Disney+ fantasy romance series "The Remarried Empress," which concluded its 10-episode run Wednesday. From her striking transformation into a Western-style fantasy character to her nuanced portrayal of an increasingly desperate antagonist, Lee emerged as one of the most talked-about stars of the series, with even her character's downfall becoming a highly anticipated moment among viewers. When the emperor demands a divorce, Navier agrees on one condition: that she be allowed to remarry Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk), a prince of the Western Kingdom. item.title: Trade commission proposes antidumping tariffs on PVC suspension from China
item.description: Korea's trade watchdog on Thursday made a preliminary decision to impose antidumping tariffs on polyvinyl chloride (PVC) suspension resin imports from China after its initial investigation identified potential damage to the domestic industry. Under the decision, the Korea Trade Commission (KTC) will ask the Ministry of Economy and Finance to impose an antidumping tariff of between 23.47 and 26.02 percent on the product used in pipes and industrial materials. The KTC launched its investigation into alleged dumping by two Chinese companies, in April following a complaint filed by Hanwha Solutions Corp., a Korean chemical producer. Separately, the commission also recommended an antidumping tariff on Chinese tin plates at between 8.05 percent and 8.36 percent. Tin plates are steel coated with tin to resist corrosion.

item.title: Vietnam seeks US trade deal as tariffs threaten clothing, footwear exports
item.description: HANOI — Vietnam said on Thursday it was working with the United States to complete a trade deal as soon as possible hours after the Trump administration threatened new tariffs that could hurt key export industries, from clothing and footwear and electronics. The manufacturing hub, which runs the largest trade surplus of any U.S. partner, faces potential rates of 35% on grounds of excessive industrial capacity, exceeding those of Southeast Asian peers and second only to China's among the 14 targeted. Shortly after the tariffs were unveiled, Vietnam's trade ministry said the two countries were working to seal a trade deal "as soon as possible, " adding that it would cooperate with the U.S. investigation on excessive capacity. Vietnam, home to major export operations of multinationals including Samsung Electronics and Apple, has spent more than a year hammering out a trade deal with Washington. item.title: FM Cho calls for bipartisan support for foreign policy ahead of departure
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Thursday called for bipartisan support for the government's foreign policy, as he made what could be his final appearance before a parliamentary committee ahead of his scheduled departure. Cho made the remarks during a plenary session of the National Assembly's foreign affairs and unification committee, as Lim Woong-soon, second deputy director of the National Security Office, has been nominated as his successor. "I feel greatly honored to have been able to contribute to the development of Korea's diplomacy as the first foreign minister of the (Lee Jae Myung) administration," Cho said. Noting the increasingly challenging international environment, Cho called on committee members to continue providing bipartisan support for the administration, particularly its summit diplomacy, which he said had recently been delivering significant results. Cho took office in July last year and has served as the country's top diplomat. Lim was scheduled to begin work at a designated office Thursday to prepare for his confirmation hearing, the date of which has yet to be set.

item.title: Search for trapped miners increases after flooding kills 13 at Indonesia illegal gold mine
item.description: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Rescuers battled high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain Thursday searching for 13 more miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine where 13 bodies were recovered earlier. The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. Several people managed to escape from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters (330 feet) deep, in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta. Authorities said they were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, and local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable. Police first received reports of trapped miners about 16 hours after the flooding occurred, and nearby state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight Wednesday, triggering a full-scale rescue operati

item.title: Lotte opens themed plaza, giant media screen in Myeong-dong
item.description: Lotte Department Store will open a themed underground plaza and a giant outdoor media screen at its flagship store in central Seoul’s Myeong-dong shopping district as part of a push to draw more tourists. The retailer said Thursday that Lumiere Seoul, an area of about 840 square meters in the first basement floor of the main store, will open Friday. The space connects to Euljiro 1-ga Station, which handles more than 30 million passengers a year. "Lumiere," the French word for light, was also used for the Lumiere Boutique, a small store Lotte opened before the main store officially launched in 1979. At the center of the plaza is the Lumiere Sphere, a 4.5-meter-wide globe made of about 21,000 acrylic crystals. It was created by a Korean installation artist and reflects both natural light from the domed glass ceiling and artificial lighting. The plaza also houses Lumiere House, a two-story gift shop with about 2,000 items, including Korean souvenirs and goods featuring Charlotte, the heroine of Goethe's novel "The Sorrows of Young Werther," and the inspiration for the Lotte company name.

item.title: Lotte holds investor briefing at Lotte Biologics' new Songdo plant
item.description: Lotte Corp., the holding company of Lotte Group, held an investor relations event Wednesday at Lotte Biologics' Songdo Bio Campus in Incheon to present its performance and growth strategy for its biopharmaceutical subsidiary. Securities analysts and institutional investors attended the briefing, along with Lotte Corp.'s chief financial officer and senior Lotte Biologics executives, the company said Thursday. After the session, participants toured the campus's first plant, which was completed Nov. 18. Lotte Corp. is the largest shareholder of Lotte Biologics with a 61 percent stake and has invested a total of 883 billion won ($601 million) in the company. item.title: Minister nominee says investigative independence must meet public expectations
item.description: Interior Minister nominee Han Jun-ho said Thursday that if appointed, he would address the issue of investigative agencies' independence in a way that meets public expectations. Han, a two-term lawmaker of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea, made the remarks to reporters as he arrived at an office in downtown Seoul to prepare for his parliamentary confirmation hearing. "The way powerful state institutions exercise their authority can lead to incidents like the Dec. 3, 2024, martial law declaration. item.description: Incheon International Airport Corp. said Thursday it has won the best airport innovation leader award at the 2026 ACI World Airport Innovation Awards. It is the first time an Asian airport has won the award. The award was presented Wednesday (local time) at Airports Innovate 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. item.title: Lee vows to ease financial burden on patients with rare diseases
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday vowed to ease the financial burden on seriously ill patients and those with rare diseases, giving them greater hope of receiving treatment. Lee made the pledge in a post on his X account, citing a news report on the Cabinet's approval of a plan to reduce the health insurance copayment rate for seriously ill patients and those with rare or incurable diseases from the current 10 percent to 7 percent starting next month. "Around 370,000 people are expected to benefit (from the measure) which will reduce their annual costs by an average 220,000 won ($164.2) per person," he noted. "This would help ease concerns over treatment costs among patients with rare diseases and those who are seriously ill, giving them greater hope of receiving treatment," the president said. He said the government has been working on measures to ease the financial burden on patients and will continue efforts to further reduce their treatment costs.

item.title: Seoul science museum turns humble snacks into hands-on lessons in science
item.description: From the crunch of a potato chip to the technology that keeps cookies fresh, an ordinary snack can reveal a surprising amount about science — and Seoul Science Center is inviting visitors to explore what goes into every bite. The museum will open a special exhibition, "Crispy on Outside, Science on Inside," on Friday, which will run through May 30, 2027. It offers an interactive look at the science behind snack development, manufacturing, packaging and distribution. Designed around familiar foods, the exhibition takes visitors through a series of settings modeled on a snack research laboratory, manufacturing plant and supermarket, tracing how products make their way from the first stages of development all the way to consumers' stomachs. The first section, "Memories and Records of Snacks," explores how snacks have changed over generations, encouraging visitors to share memories associated with familiar products. item.title: Canada pushing controversial bill on personal data access
item.description: TORONTO — Canada is advancing legislation that would give law enforcement new powers to access personal digital information, a proposal facing international criticism over concerns that it undermines privacy and cybersecurity. A joint letter last week from more than 20 civil society groups, including Amnesty International, called the legislation "an impending catastrophe" and asked Prime Minister Mark Carney to step in before the bill becomes law. Leading tech companies had warned that if the bill passed unchanged they might be forced to withdraw certain services from Canada to avoid complying with rules they claim would weaken encryption protections. The bill had been approved by the House of Commons, but Canada's Senate on Wednesday proposed several amendments aimed at assuring tech companies can maintain robust defenses against cyberattacks. item.title: Police raid home of late LEET top scorer in cheating probe
item.description: Police on Thursday raided the home of the late top scorer on this year's law school entrance exam as part of a probe into his alleged cheating on the test. Investigators searched the home of Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student who was found dead last week amid mounting suspicions about his possible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in getting a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Police also raided Younghoon High School in Seoul, where Lee's college entrance exam papers from last year have been stored. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's financial crime unit launched the probe after receiving multiple complaints accusing Lee of cheating. Despite initial expectations they would close the case following Lee's death, the police have pressed ahead in the public interest, with the nation still grappling with the recent admission of AI-assisted cheating by the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam. The admission sent authorities scrambling to draw up and enforce anti-cheating measures during the annual college entrance exam last week.

item.title: Lee's approval rating falls for 2nd straight time: poll
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating fell for the second consecutive time to 43 percent, with negative assessments of his performance continuing to outnumber positive ones, a biweekly poll showed Thursday. In a survey of 1,000 adults nationwide conducted Monday through Wednesday, positive assessments of Lee's job performance fell 1 percentage point from two weeks earlier, according to the National Barometer Survey (NBS). Negative assessments also fell 2 percentage points to 45 percent, while 12 percent said they were undecided. Lee's approval rating has seen a downward trend from early this year in NBS polls, hovering below 70 percent from March to May before falling below 60 percent in June and remaining in the low-to-mid 40 percent range since September. When asked about the direction of state affairs, 42 percent said the Lee administration was heading in the right direction, while 46 percent said it was going in the wrong direction.
