item.title: Apple Korea faces potential $50 mil. fine over 'deceptive' iPhone AI ads
item.description: Apple Korea could face a fine of up to 67 billion won ($50 million) after the nation's antitrust regulator accused the company of misleading consumers over the availability of key Apple Intelligence features advertised with the iPhone 16, the Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said Thursday. The watchdog estimated sales related to the alleged violation at about 3.35 trillion won ($2.5 billion). Under the Act on Fair Labeling and Advertising, companies can be fined up to 2 percent of sales related to a violation. The FTC said its investigators had recommended corrective measures and a fine against Apple Inc. and Apple Korea for allegedly violating the law by advertising Apple Intelligence features without adequately disclosing uncertainty over their availability and release schedules. The case centers on nine Apple Intelligence features advertised on Apple's iPhone 16 website between September 2024 and March 2025. item.title: AIcLude builds AI agents for everyday business tasks
item.description: An artificial intelligence (AI) avatar greeted passersby outside two telecom stores in Takamatsu, a city in Japan’s Kagawa Prefecture. Of the 3,709 greetings it initiated, 66.4 percent drew a spoken response. Those who responded exchanged an average of 7.3 messages with the avatar per conversation. The figures came from a four-month pilot conducted by AIcLude, a Seoul-based agentic AI company, and STNet, a telecommunications and information technology affiliate of Japan’s Shikoku Electric Power Group. During the pilot, which ran from December last year through March this year, AIcLude operated kiosks at two of STNet’s Pikara Shop outlets. The company wanted to see whether the avatars could greet passersby and invite them inside, as store staff already do, and whether the stores could afford to run them. “Telecom stores in Japan hire part-time workers to approach people walking by and invite them in. item.title: US military confirms inactivation of Apache helicopter squadron in S. Korea
item.description: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) confirmed Thursday that an Army aviation unit in South Korea has been inactivated, noting that the move does not change the United States' military force posture or commitment to the defense of the Asian ally. The inactivation of the 5th Air Cavalry Squadron, 17th Cavalry Regiment (5-17 ACS) at Camp Humphreys, a key U.S. base in Pyeongtaek, some 60 kilometers south of Seoul, came amid lingering speculation that the U.S. could consider a troop realignment to better address broader regional security challenges, including from China. "The inactivation of the 5-17 Air Cavalry Squadron is part of the U.S. Army's broader force structure and aviation transformation efforts to modernize capabilities and optimize formations for future operational requirements," the USFK said in response to a question from Yonhap News Agency. item.title: Korea to ban ads on food, drugs, cosmetics featuring AI-generated experts
item.description: Korea will ban advertisements using experts generated by artificial intelligence (AI) to promote food, drugs and cosmetics starting this week, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety said Thursday. The ministry said it has revised enforcement regulations of related laws, which will take effect sequentially starting Friday, the ministry said. Violators will be forced to suspend their businesses, or mandated to suspend advertising and sales activities. "We will protect the people from unfair advertisements abusing new technologies, while fostering an environment where customers can feel safe," an official from the drug ministry said.

item.title: Kookmin University professor named among World's Top 2% Scientists for 6 straight years
item.description: Nam Ki-hyun, a professor at Kookmin University’s College of General Education, has been named to the 2026 World’s Top 2% Scientists list for the sixth consecutive year. The list, jointly released by Stanford University and global academic publisher Elsevier, identifies the top 2 percent of researchers in their respective fields based on a comprehensive analysis of citation metrics and other indicators of research impact drawn from Elsevier’s Scopus database. Nam ranked in the top 0.52 percent of researchers in the field of biochemistry and molecular biology when self-citations were excluded, and in the top 0.25 percent when they were included, the university said. “I am deeply honored to have been named among the World’s Top 2% Scientists for six consecutive years,” Nam said. “This achievement would not have been possible without the collaboration and dedication of the researchers in Korea and abroad with whom I have worked, and I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all of them." item.title: Jeonbuk National University climbs to 22nd in Korean university rankings
item.description: Jeonbuk National University ranked 22nd nationwide in the JoongAng University Rankings 2026, up four places from last year. The university placed third among regional flagship national universities, behind Kyungpook National University and Pusan National University, which tied for 19th overall. The results underscore Jeonbuk National University’s competitiveness in education and research, the university said. The rankings, released Tuesday by the JoongAng Ilbo, a Korean daily newspaper, evaluated 55 universities this year across four categories: faculty research, educational environment, student outcomes and reputation. “These results are significant because they lay the groundwork for strengthening our competitiveness as we work toward joining the global Top 100,” said Yang Oh-bong, president of the university. “We will continue to fulfill our role as a regional flagship national university by ensuring that our research achievements benefit local businesses and communities." item.description: HD Hyundai Marine Solution has earned top international recognition for its sustainability disclosures, winning the highest distinction in a global communications competition and securing a place among the world's 20 best entries. item.title: Virtual boy band WINKX looks beyond K-pop with fantasy universe
item.description: The growing market for virtual K-pop idols is set to welcome another contender Friday, as four-member band WINKX makes its debut with the digital single "HALO." But the group's agency, Titan Content, has ambitions that extend well beyond music. The company, also home to girl group AtHeart, is developing WINKX as an intellectual property (IP) that spans music, comics, animation and video games, betting on the crossover appeal between K-pop and subculture fandoms. During a press conference held Wednesday at a hotel in western Seoul's Mapo District, Titan Content Chairman Han Se-min laid out the company's vision for the group. "I have announced the launch of so many idols, but today is the day I'm most excited," said Han, a former CEO of SM Entertainment who co-founded the Los Angeles-based entertainment company in 2023. item.title: RIIZE set as sole K-pop act on Tecate Pa'l Norte 2027 lineup in Mexico
item.description: Boy group RIIZE will be the sole K-pop act at Tecate Pa'l Norte 2027, Mexico's largest music festival, its agency SM Entertainment said. The festival announced its lineup Tuesday (local time). The six-member group will join the three-day event, which runs March 26-28 at Parque Fundidora in Monterrey. Monterrey is an industrial hub and the capital of Nuevo Leon in northeastern Mexico. The venue, Parque Fundidora, is a large public park built on the site of a former steelworks. RIIZE will take the stage on the opening day. Launched in 2012, Tecate Pa'l Norte has become one of Latin America's leading music festivals and drew approximately 300,000 people last year. The 2027 edition marks the festival's 15th anniversary. RIIZE is also set to appear in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York on Thursday (local time), where it is the only K-pop group in this year's lineup. The parade is held annually for the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday and is broadcast nationwide. item.title: Korea, Turkey discuss expanding cooperation in infrastructure, nuclear energy
item.description: Senior officials of Korea and Turkey have discussed ways to expand bilateral cooperation in infrastructure, nuclear energy and various other strategic sectors following a summit between their leaders earlier this month, the foreign ministry said Thursday. Park Hyung-chul, director-general for European affairs at the ministry, visited Turkey earlier this week and held separate meetings with officials from the foreign, transport and energy ministries, according to the ministry. In his meeting with Korkut Gungen, director-general for Asia-Pacific affairs at Turkey's foreign ministry, Park called for close consultations ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties next year and deeper cooperation in energy, science and technology, infrastructure, and defense. Park also raised difficulties faced by Korean companies and nationals in Turkey, and sought the government's attention and support. item.title: PM vows to protect teachers from false accusations of child abuse
item.description: The government will take steps to protect teachers from false accusations of child abuse to help them concentrate on educating children without worrying about such malicious complaints, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Thursday. The concept of emotional abuse will be defined more specifically to distinguish it from legitimate teaching, while unnecessary investigations into legitimate educational acts will be minimized, Han said during a government policy coordination meeting. "Protecting students from child abuse is more important than anything else. But at the same time, an educational environment should be guaranteed where legitimate educational activities are not discouraged and teachers can focus on guiding students according to their principles," she said. The government will also have schools and regional education offices take responsibility for responding to malicious complaints directed at individual educators so as to better protect teachers' rights, Han said. item.title: Assembly speaker proposes reviving parliamentary dialogue channel between Korea, Japan
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik has formally proposed resuming a long-stalled parliamentary dialogue forum between Korea and Japan in a meeting with his Japanese counterpart, his office said Thursday. Cho, who is on an official trip to Japan, also proposed hosting the forum in Korea next year as he met with Eisuke Mori, speaker of Japan's House of Representatives, in Tokyo on Wednesday (local time). "The Future Dialogue between the Parliaments of Korea and Japan holds special significance as a high-level dialogue channel led by the heads of the two countries' legislatures," Cho said, adding that he would begin preparations to hold the forum next year if Mori agrees. Mori supported Cho's proposal, saying the forum is central to exchanges between the two parliaments and that its importance is growing amid the challenging international situation. Mori added that he would positively consider leading a delegation to visit Korea next year. Launched in 2016, the dialogue forum was last held in 2018 and was suspended the following year amid strained bilateral ties after then Assembly Spea

item.title: Unionized rail workers launch work-to-rule campaign, 4 train services canceled
item.description: Unionized workers of Korea Railroad Corp. (KORAIL) launched a work-to-rule action Thursday, forcing the rail operator to cancel services of three passenger trains. Under the action, which began at 9 a.m. and is set to last through Dec. 4, the workers plan to strictly adhere to safety and other regulations, such as not driving trains faster to make up for lost time, refusing to work overtime and responding to passenger complaints in line with manuals, according to the Korean Railway Workers' Union. Through the campaign, the union is demanding improvements to the employee promotion system, extra allowances and additional personnel. It has threatened to launch an indefinite general strike on Dec. 10, if the needs are not addressed. KORAIL said it canceled operations of four regular trains scheduled Thursday due to the collective action as of 5p.m., including two ITX-Saemaul services. It also canceled a Mugunghwa train scheduled to depart from Yongsan Station in Seoul to the southern city of Yeosu at 3:10 p.m., after more than an hourlong delay, forcing 431 passengers to turn back. item.title: CORTIS to mark fandom's 1st anniversary with 6-day Seoul pop-up
item.description: K-pop boy band CORTIS is marking its fandom’s first anniversary with a six-day pop-up in Seoul next month, featuring member-designed merchandise, interactive photo zones and a collaboration with animated icon Pororo, its agency BigHit Music said Thursday. The five-member act will host the "COER 1st Anniversary POP-UP" from Dec. 1-6 on the first floor of HYBE’s headquarters in Seoul’s Yongsan District to celebrate the first milestone of its official fan club, COER, and thank supporters for a breakout year. Designed around a first-birthday party theme, the venue will display T-shirts featuring hand-drawn illustrations by the members alongside a message board for fans to leave celebratory notes. A large media wall will screen CORTIS music videos and behind-the-scenes clips, while a colorful ball pit inspired by the group's signature CORTIS Ball characters and an oversized balloon cake will anchor the space. item.title: S. Korea's spy agency denies report about China's alleged proposal for anti-US operations
item.description: South Korea's spy agency has denied a media report that Beijing had proposed covert operations against the United States when the agency sought to secure the release of two informants detained by China early this year. The Kukmin Daily reported Wednesday that China made the proposal to the National Intelligence Service (NIS) for the anti-U.S. operations, and that Washington strongly protested it, apparently leading to a chasm in the South Korea-U.S. intelligence partnership. "The NIS has never received any such proposal from the Chinese authorities," it said in a press notice. The agency also said intelligence cooperation between Seoul and Washington is proceeding in a "two-way" and "mutually beneficial" manner across various fields, including counterintelligence. Concerns about bilateral intelligence collaboration have continued following reports earlier this year that the U.S. partially limited Seoul's access to its satellite-based intelligence on North Korea after Unification Minister Chung Dong-young referred to the North's Kusong area as one of the uranium enrichment sites. item.title: North Korea's Kim urges wider tactical nuclear weapons deployment on facility tour, KCNA says
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un said his country should focus on deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and that its nuclear material production capacity was being systematically expanded, state media KCNA reported on Thursday. Kim, who spoke during an inspection on Wednesday of nuclear material production and weapons research facilities, also said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "absolutely inviolable." KCNA did not identify the facilities or their locations. "Our nuclear capability is now a reality," KCNA quoted Kim as saying. Kim said North Korea should "focus on utilizing tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains for different missions" and called recent achievements in nuclear weapons production a major success for the country's nuclear force policy. item.title: Korea's foreign tourist arrivals top 2 mil. in October for 4th straight month
item.description: Korea’s inbound tourism boom powered through October with 2.16 million foreign visitors, extending a four-month streak above the 2 million mark as traveler spending and travel beyond the capital hit major milestones, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism announced Thursday. The October tally marks a 24 percent jump from the 1.74 million arrivals registered a year earlier. Cumulative arrivals from January through October reached 19.27 million — up 21.8 percent over the same 10-month span last year — keeping monthly figures consistently above 2 million since July (2.09 million), peaking in August (2.25 million), and holding steady through September (2.06 million). This sustained surge builds on a multiyear rebound following the lifting of pandemic-era travel restrictions, propelled by the global wave of Korean pop culture — from K-pop and dramas to beauty and cuisine — alongside expanded international flight routes and streamlined electronic visa policies. item.title: JD Vance says Jensen Huang won't need pardon as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington
item.description: WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE, Ohio — U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday played down the possibility that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could need a presidential pardon just days before the executive of the AI giant is expected to appear before a congressional committee. Vance told reporters that Justice Department officials and “multiple officials in our national security apparatus” have confirmed that Huang is “under no investigation.” The vice president made the remarks after having a Thanksgiving Eve meal with troops at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. The Nvidia CEO resigned earlier this month after acknowledging extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. He was reinstated 11 days later at the urging of President Donald Trump. “I don’t think he needs a pardon at all,” Vance said. “I haven’t seen any evidence again that he committed a crime. item.title: BOK sharply upgrades 2027 growth forecast to 4.1% from 2.9% on chip boom
item.description: The Bank of Korea (BOK) sharply upgraded its 2027 growth forecast for Korea to 4.1 percent from 2.9 percent on Thursday, expecting the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom to continue fueling semiconductor exports and investment. In its revised economic outlook, the central bank also raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.9 percent from the 3.3 percent projected in August. The 1.2-percentage-point upgrade to the 2027 forecast marks the largest upward revision since the BOK began issuing growth projections for the following year in 2008. If realized, the 4.1 percent expansion would mark the first time for the Korean economy to grow by more than 4 percent since 2021, when it expanded 4.7 percent. The same day, the central bank's Monetary Policy Board raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25 percent, citing persistent inflationary pressures and stronger-than-expected economic growth. item.title: Seoul shares up late Thursday morning on tech gains
item.description: Korean shares traded higher late Thursday morning after the previous session's sharp decline, with chipmakers leading a rebound as the central bank sharply upgraded its economic growth forecasts. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) gained 60.24 points, or 1.28 percent, to 4,757.75 as of 11:20 a.m. The Bank of Korea sharply raised its growth forecast for the Korean economy to 4.1 percent for 2027 and 3.9 percent for this year, as strong exports of semiconductors connected to artificial intelligence (AI) bolstered the growth momentum. Chipmakers led the gains. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics gained 1.93 percent, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix added 4.47 percent. Among other index heavyweights, SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, went up 4.41 percent, while power equipment manufacturer Samsung Electro-Mechanics jumped 6.36 percent. The Korean won was quoted at 1,340 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., up 4.3 won from the previous session's close.

item.title: Supreme Court confirms ex-President Yoon's acquittal in perjury case
item.description: The Supreme Court on Thursday confirmed former President Yoon Suk Yeol's acquittal on charges that he perjured himself during the martial law trial of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo. Yoon was indicted on charges of making false claims during Han's trial in November last year that he had planned to call a Cabinet meeting for his martial law declaration on Dec. 3, 2024, even before Han proposed such a session. Special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team viewed the testimony as false, arguing that Yoon had initially called in six Cabinet members without planning a formal session but later summoned additional members at Han's suggestion to meet the quorum that would legitimatize his martial law declaration. An appellate court in September upheld a lower court's acquittal of Yoon, ruling that the unusual circumstances of the Cabinet meeting alone are not enough to find Yoon guilty. The Supreme Court did not find issues with the appellate ruling, noting that a conviction requires evidence strong enough to substantiate the charges as true. item.title: Trump heads to Arizona next week for high-stakes expansion of TSMC's computer chip factories
item.description: WEST PALM BEACH, Florida — U.S. President Donald Trump , who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based company. The trip will come at the end of a week where AI comes under the microscope in Washington in the aftermath of Trump intervening to get his ally Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia. Huang is slated to testify at a Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3 and will face questions about how his company has been selling its chips abroad — and his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Beijing has denied it. TSMC has expanded aggressively in the Phoenix, Arizona, area, using its U.S. facilities to manufacture chips for tech companies such as Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, and Qualcomm. item.title: World stocks tumble as Trump tariffs rattle markets, AI rally fades
item.description: NEW YORK/LONDON — Global markets retreated on Wednesday with riskier assets under pressure after the Trump administration proposed sweeping new tariffs on 14 trading partners. U.S. stocks, hammered in the morning, partially recovered in the afternoon from early losses as investors bought the dip ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The Dow closed higher and the Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended slightly lower. U.S. technology shares led declines amid concerns about inflation and a hawkish Federal Reserve, while investors assessed the implications of the tariffs for global supply chains and economic growth. Treasury prices rose as investors sought safe-haven assets. MSCI's global stocks index fell 0.60 percent and Nvidia shed more than 8 percent during the day before closing down 3.91 percent. Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors, said bargain hunters were stepping in ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, adding that "investors are taking advantage of some of those discrepancies." The Nasdaq was down more than 4 percent earlier in the session before closing down 0.62 percent,

item.title: US proposes excess capacity tariffs on Korean goods within agreed 15% ceiling
item.description: WASHINGTON — The United States proposed Wednesday imposing tariffs of up to 15 percent on Korean goods over alleged excess manufacturing capacity, taking into account a bilateral trade agreement and existing tariffs. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed measures as it determined that the acts, policies and practices of Korea and 13 other economies, including China, Japan and the European Union (EU), relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors were unreasonable and burdened or restricted U.S. commerce. The USTR proposed applying tariffs of up to 15 percent on all Korean goods, net of most-favored-nation (MFN) tariff rates and existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods. item.title: President extends hands-on approach by chairing overseas envoy meeting
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung is looking to expand his hands-on approach to governing by chairing a briefing with heads of overseas missions — a move that would put him in charge of diplomatic discussions previously led by the foreign minister. A former Seongnam mayor and Gyeonggi Province governor, Lee has paid close attention to how ministries and other government bodies implement policies at the decision-making level and has taken over some meetings once run by other senior officials. In February, Lee began presiding over the National Tourism Strategy Council, traditionally chaired by the prime minister. Two months later, he led the Regulatory Rationalization Committee’s first plenary session after its chairmanship shifted from the prime minister to the president. Cheong Wa Dae said Tuesday that the president may hear directly from ambassadors and other chiefs of overseas missions on key diplomatic issues at a briefing on Dec. 2. item.title: AI music tops local chart: What you need to know
item.description: A song written with assistance from artificial intelligence (AI) has topped Korea's most closely watched music chart for the first time, raising questions about how the country's music industry should handle songs created with AI. MEOMURU's rock ballad "The Adult I Dreamed Of" reached No. 1 on Melon's Top 100 on Nov. 13, months after Joseon HipHop's AI-assisted "Forest of the Heart" peaked at No. 89 on the chart. Released June 23, the ballad gained traction through Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts before topping YouTube's daily popular music video chart in Korea in September. With no established fandom or television promotion behind it, the song won over listeners in their 30s and 40s in particular with lyrics reflecting on the gap between childhood aspirations and adult reality. Its success has exposed gaps in Korea's music industry standards, from the disclosure of AI use to the distribution of royalties. Q: Who is behind the song? item.title: Blue Elephant bets on landmark stores to build global eyewear brand
item.description: Blue Elephant is accelerating its global expansion, starting with the United States and Japan, by opening brand-inspired stores in strategic locations to raise its profile among local consumers. The budget eyewear company, drawing on its experience operating 32 directly managed stores in Korea since 2019, including in tourist hotspots such as Seongsu, Myeong-dong and Jeju Island, has opened outlets in California and Tokyo. Fueled by a growing number of foreign customers, the Seoul-based company is seeing international consumers account for an increasing share of its sales both at home and abroad. In August, Blue Elephant opened its first U.S. flagship store in Beverly Hills, within the Golden Triangle, a local retail district home to global luxury fashion and beauty brands as well as restaurants. The 650-square-meter store incorporates the company's SPACE 2.0 design principles, an approach to store interiors that draws on architectural and cultural elements inspired by each location. Under this concept, Blue Elephant Beverly Hills preserves the building's original 1940s structure, inclu

item.title: Korean War veteran still carries bullet near his heart 73 years after battle
item.description: PYEONGTAEK, Gyeonggi Province — On July 20, 1953, just a week before the Korean War armistice was signed, Ryu Jae-sik and a Chinese soldier stood with their guns pointed at each other. Both fired. The Chinese soldier’s bullet struck Ryu’s shoulder, broke eight of his ribs and lodged near his heart. It is still there, 73 years later. Ryu, who now heads the Seoul branch of the Korean War Veterans Association, recalled his days on the battlefield during a visit to the U.S. Eighth Army headquarters at Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, Nov. 5. A native of Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, Ryu was an 18-year-old student when the war broke out in 1950. He and his friends hid in the mountains to avoid being conscripted by North Korean forces, catching frogs and grasshoppers to eat when they ran out of food. When he saw South Korean soldiers entering Chuncheon with South Korean flags attached to their rifles, he ran down the mountain, cheering. Ryu volunteered for a reconnaissance unit of the Army’s 6th Infantry Division and went into battle in his school uniform. The following y

item.title: Tunisia Embassy celebrates 2026 World Olive Tree Day in Seoul
item.description: Since ancient times, the olive tree has served as a symbol of peace, wisdom and harmony. To honor the 3,000-year heritage of the olive tree and its cultural, environmental and economic significance across the Mediterranean region, the Embassy of Tunisia in Korea hosted an event marking the upcoming World Olive Tree Day at the ambassador’s residence in northeastern Seoul’s Seongbuk District, Friday. UNESCO officially established the annual observance on Nov. 26 during the 40th session of its General Conference in 2019, following an initiative by Tunisia and Lebanon. This year's event, A Taste of Tunisia, was aimed at bringing together Korean importers, distributors, food industry professionals and media, combining a celebration of Tunisia's olive-growing heritage with an opportunity to explore new commercial partnerships in Korea's fast-growing market. item.title: Building a community for Black creatives in Seoul
item.description: When Marie Noel moved to Korea in 2024, the plan was simple: find a way to continue her filmmaking career as a writer and actor. Her profession had given her opportunities to travel across Austria, Germany and the U.K. In all these places she went, she found herself in spaces where representation and access were not always guaranteed. As soon as she began reconnecting with filmmaking in Korea, she was confronted with a similar reality about visibility and representation. Identifying and connecting Black creatives specifically required time and deliberate effort. The reality was further compounded by the fact that Black creatives were living and working across Korea and pursuing their own artistic interests, yet many were doing so independently, oblivious of each other, in the same industry. It was this revelation that sparked her to establish Black Seoul Creatives, a community connecting Black creatives and members of the Black diaspora across Korea. To other people, the idea seemed new, but it wasn't to her. It was an extension of something she had already experienced, built and learned

item.title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 ease, but off lows of the day as investors seek bargains
item.description: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday amid a tech selloff, but sharply pared earlier losses as bargain hunters stepped in ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. The Dow traded higher. The Nasdaq had been more than 4 percent lower earlier in the session as a selloff in AI-related stocks and new U.S. tariff proposals hit sentiment. "There are all these potential headwinds, but then there's also a certain amount of conditioning of buying on the dip, and that's part of what we're seeing," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president and adviser for Wealthspire Advisors in Westport, Connecticut. "The broad selloffs tend to kind of throw the baby out with the bathwater. Investors are taking advantage of some of those discrepancies," he said. While technology was down more than 1 percent, materials and real estate led S&P 500 sector gainers. Wall Street has been roiled this month, partly because of worries about AI leader Nvidia. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month, but the company's board reinstated him on Monday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 346.96 points, or 0.69

item.title: 'Hope' wins top Blue Dragon award; Sul, Jeon take acting honors for 'Possible Love'
item.description: Director Na Hong-jin's sci-fi thriller "Hope" won best picture at the 47th Blue Dragon Film Awards on Wednesday, while Lee Chang-dong's "Possible Love" emerged as the night's biggest winner with four awards, including both top acting honors. "Hope," which competed at this year's Cannes Film Festival, entered the ceremony at KBS Hall in Seoul with 10 nominations. In addition to best picture, it also won awards for cinematography and lighting. Accepting the best picture trophy, Na drew laughter from the audience by joking that he should have won the award at Cannes. "They should have given me this at Cannes. Why here instead?" he said. Na then credited the cast and crew, describing the experience of making the film as one of the happiest and most memorable times of his life. Lee's "Possible Love," which won the Grand Jury Prize at this year's Venice International Film Festival, dominated the acting categories. Sul Kyung-gu and Jeon Do-yeon, who play a married couple in the drama exploring class divisions, won best actor and best actress, respectively. Their co-star Cho Yeo-jeong took home be

item.title: "I'm Not Going to Give Up": Leonard Peltier on Indigenous Rights, His Half-Century in Prison & Coming Home
item.description:
In September 2025, Democracy Now! host Amy Goodman sat down with longtime political prisoner and Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier for his first extended television and radio broadcast interview since his release to home confinement in February 2025. Before his commutation by former President Joe Biden, the 82-year-old Peltier spent nearly 50 years behind bars. Peltier has always maintained his innocence for the 1975 killing of two FBI officers. He is expected to serve the remainder of his life sentences under house arrest at the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Nation in Belcourt, North Dakota. In a wide-ranging conversation, we spoke to Peltier about his case, his time in prison, his childhood spent at an American Indian boarding school and his later involvement in the American Indian Movement (AIM) and more.

“We still have to live under that, that fear of losing our identity, losing our culture, our religion,” Peltier says about his continued commitment to Indigenous rights. “The struggle still goes on for me. I’m not going to give up.”

item.description: The Marines have a new minimum fleet requirement for water survival, according to a policy released earlier this month. item.title: Nasdaq sinks about 4% as AI rout, fresh Trump tariffs spook Wall St
item.description: The main U.S. indexes fell on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq plunging about 4 percent, as a deepening selloff in AI-related stocks and new U.S. tariff proposals hit sentiment amid mounting doubt over whether the debt-fueled AI boom can deliver sufficient returns. Wall Street has been roiled this month, with fears of increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector following the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections adding to the pressure. "The fundamental support for a year-end rally simply isn't there," Chris Brigati, chief investment officer at SWBC, said in a note. "The AI-inspired rally continues to run out of steam, and without evidence that massive capex spending will deliver the profit and revenue goals the market expects, there is little incentive for a rebound." Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO after his removal earlier this month provided a temporary reprieve at the start of the week. Broader concerns lingered, however, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the S&P 500 remained on track for their worst November since 2008. Chipmakers led the declines, with Nvidia falling 8.7 percent an

item.title: 'Hope' wins top Blue Dragon award; Sul, Jeon take acting honors for 'Possible Love'
item.description: Director Na Hong-jin's sci-fi thriller "Hope" won best picture at the 47th Blue Dragon Film Awards on Wednesday, while Lee Chang-dong's "Possible Love" emerged as the night's biggest winner with four awards, including both top acting honors. "Hope," which competed at this year's Cannes Film Festival, entered the ceremony at KBS Hall in Seoul with a leading 10 nominations and also won the cinematography and lighting award. Accepting the best picture trophy, Na drew laughter from the audience by joking that he should have won the award at Cannes. "They should have given me this at Cannes. Why here instead?" he said. Na then credited the cast and crew, describing the experience of making the film as one of the happiest and most memorable times of his life. Meanwhile, Lee's "Possible Love," which won the Grand Jury Prize at this year's Venice International Film Festival, dominated the acting categories. Sul Kyung-gu and Jeon Do-yeon, who play a married couple in the drama exploring class divisions, won best actor and best actress, respectively. Their co-star Cho Yeo-jeong took home best suppor

item.title: FM Cho asks Omani counterpart to keep backing Cheonghae unit
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met his Omani counterpart, Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, on Wednesday and asked Oman to keep backing the Cheonghae naval unit, which operates in waters off the Gulf state, the ministry said. Cho thanked Oman, a key port of call for the unit, for helping it run its missions smoothly. Al Busaidi, for his part, vowed to continue that support, according to the ministry. Earlier in the day, the defense committee of Korea's National Assembly approved a revised motion to extend the unit's operational zone from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman. The motion also widens its role in securing safe maritime passage. Cho stressed that Oman is one of Korea's key energy partners and called on the Gulf country to support Korean businesses working in its renewable energy and energy infrastructure sectors. Al Busaidi's trip marked the first visit by an Omani foreign minister since July 2000.

item.title: 6 dead, 20 believed trapped after flood hits unauthorized gold mine in Indonesia
item.description: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Rescuers in Indonesia recovered three more bodies from an unauthorized gold mine Wednesday and searched for 20 other miners believed trapped inside by flooding, raising the confirmed number of deaths to six. The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. The shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters deep, is located in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta. Eleven miners escaped from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan said. Local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable. Authorities were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, officials said. “The problem was that nobody reported it and nobody wanted to report it because the activity was illegal,” said Muhammad Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor disaster mitigation age

item.title: UN warns of growing risk of atrocities by Israel against Palestinians
item.description: GENEVA, Switzerland — The United Nations warned Wednesday of a growing risk of atrocity crimes being committed by Israel against the Palestinians, and urged all states to take immediate preventative action. U.N. rights chief Volker Turk said ongoing Israeli attacks, policies and violations against Palestinians indicated a "widening risk of further atrocity crimes" in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. "Israeli government representatives at highest levels have time and again spelled out policies of annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment in the West Bank," he said in a statement. "Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes — war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide — has been appalling." Turk said his office had repeatedly warned about the risk of Israel's actions in Gaza posing a "real threat to the continued existence" of the Palestinians as a group. item.title: Hanwha Ocean loses preferred bidder status for Thai frigate project
item.description: Hanwha Ocean has lost its preferred bidder status for a next-generation Thai frigate project after the Royal Thai Navy canceled the procurement process, sending the Korean shipbuilder’s entry into the Thai naval market back to square one, the company said Wednesday. “Hanwha Ocean was selected as the preferred bidder for the frigate project ordered by the Royal Thai Navy on Sept. 8, but lost its preferred bidder status following the Royal Thai Navy’s announcement, Wednesday, canceling the procurement process,” Hanwha Ocean said in a regulatory filing. The Royal Thai Navy selected Hanwha Ocean as its preferred bidder in September, beating defense companies from Spain, Singapore and Turkey. The project involved building one frigate and providing integrated logistics support, with the proposed contract valued at around 680 billion won ($505 million). The Royal Thai Navy canceled the procurement after concerns emerged that performance requirements specified in the tender documents did not comply with Thailand’s public procurement regulations. item.description: Korean actor Son Suk-ku has opened up about the deep psychological and physical preparation behind his latest role in the Netflix mystery thriller series "The Blue Road," a gripping cross-border crime drama featuring an unprecedented investigative partnership between top representative actors from Korea and Japan. item.title: President reaffirms Cheonghae unit will widen role, but stay out of war
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday reaffirmed that Korea's Cheonghae naval unit will take on a wider role in securing safe maritime passage, but will not intervene in any war. His remarks followed a vote earlier in the day by the National Assembly's defense committee approving a revised motion to widen the unit's operational zone. The unit would move from the waters off Somalia to the Arabian Sea south of Oman, about 650 kilometers from the Strait of Hormuz. "As I said in September, the dispatch of the unit will neither involve us in a war nor intervene in one," Lee wrote on his X account. "We will use this extension of the unit's mission period to broaden its role and strengthen its combat capabilities," he said. On the specifics, he said, "We will add maritime patrol aircraft and mine-clearing support to the destroyer's existing role and extend its operation area from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman." item.title: Additional personal info leaked from Bithumb in cyberattacks
item.description: More personal information than initially reported had been leaked from Bithumb in a recent cyberattack, the cryptocurrency exchange said Wednesday. Bithumb reported a data breach late last month affecting some 7,100 customers and employees, but the exchange said more personal information has been compromised. The leaked personal information includes names, phone numbers, passport numbers and account numbers. Financial firms, such as Mirae Asset Securities and Daishin Securities, have suffered a series of cyberattacks.

item.title: Hahm Sung-deuk named acting president of Kyonggi University
item.description: Kyonggi University has appointed Hahm Sung-deuk, a political science professor and vice president of its Seoul campus, as acting president, the university said Monday. The appointment followed the succession order stipulated in the university's bylaws and organizational regulations, according to the university. The position has been vacant since late July, when Ko Gi-bok was removed from office over allegations of sexual assault involving a former student. Hahm received his doctorate in political economy from Carnegie Mellon University in the United States. He previously taught at Georgetown University and Korea University before joining Kyonggi University in 2021 as dean of its Graduate School of Political Studies. As acting president, he will oversee the university's academic and administrative affairs until a new president is appointed. The timeline for selecting a permanent president has yet to be determined. item.title: Delta sides with Korean Air leadership in Hanjin KAL ownership battle
item.description: Delta Air Lines has dealt a setback to Hoban Group's push for control of Hanjin KAL by reaffirming its backing for Korean Air Chairman Cho Won-tae, bolstering the incumbent leadership's position in the escalating ownership battle, a Delta executive said Wednesday. "Delta is committed to the success of our leading trans-Pacific joint venture with Korean Air," Jeff Moomaw, Delta's vice president for Asia-Pacific, told The Korea Times in an interview. Cho is also chairman of Hanjin Group. "Delta owns 14.9 percent of Hanjin KAL equity. As a long-term shareholder, Delta is highly confident in Cho and the existing management team at Hanjin Group and at Korean Air." This strengthens Cho's position as Hoban Group seeks to expand its influence over the airline conglomerate. Hoban has so far expanded its stake in Hanjin KAL to 20.69 percent, rising to become the largest shareholder of the company. Cho and his related parties hold 20.58 percent. item.title: Lee calls for swift public housing supply to help stabilize market
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday called for the swift supply of public housing in a bid to stabilize the housing market. The president made the call during a meeting to promote public housing in Seoul's northwestern district of Eunpyeong, stressing the importance of speeding up housing supply and curbing real estate speculation. The remarks came as housing prices in Seoul remain prohibitively high following years of runaway price growth. The president said sluggish construction activity and a decline in construction permits between 2022 and 2025 led to a housing shortage, destabilizing the housing market. "It is important to expand housing supply and provide housing as quickly as possible," he stressed. To this end, the government plans to annually supply 240,000 public housing units through 2030, which he said would mark the highest level of home supplies on record. The president also stressed the importance of improving the quality of public housing, noting that it should serve as a stepping stone for people seeking to buy their own homes.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz bets on core models in EV strategy shift away from EQ lineup
item.description: Long associated with traditional luxury and prestige, Mercedes-Benz is reshaping its brand identity and electrification strategy to regain ground in Korea's fast-changing imported vehicle market, where technology and competitive pricing increasingly drive consumer choices. The German luxury automaker is moving away from its standalone EQ lineup toward electric versions of its established models, betting on familiar nameplates and next-generation technology to broaden its appeal without sacrificing its luxury heritage. Mercedes-Benz Korea begins customer deliveries of the all-new electric GLB on Wednesday, marking its third next-generation electric vehicle (EV) to debut in Korea this year, following the launch of the electric CLA and GLC in October. "Both of them are marking a very important chapter in our electrification journey here in Korea," Mercedes-Benz Korea CEO Shirin Emira said of the CLA and GLC during a test-drive event on the southern resort island of Jeju on Monday. Emira also described the launch of the electric GLB as "another vital milestone" in the brand's electrification

item.title: Samsung Display invests 210 mil. euros in ams OSRAM, becomes largest shareholder
item.description: Samsung Display, a Korean display maker, said Wednesday it has signed an agreement to become the largest shareholder in European chipmaker ams OSRAM. Under the agreement, Samsung Display will acquire 9.98 million newly issued shares of ams OSRAM at 21 euros ($23) apiece, for a total investment of 210 million euros. Upon completion of the deal, Samsung Display will hold a 9.1 percent stake in the company, making it the No. 1 shareholder. The investment will be accompanied by a strategic partnership between the two display makers to jointly develop and commercialize next-generation "ultra-small" microLED technology. "Ultra-small microLED is a next-generation inorganic self-emissive technology with the potential to overcome the limitations of existing technologies in areas such as brightness and lifetime," said Yi Chung, President and chief executive officer (CEO) of Samsung Display. Samsung Display said the partnership aims to secure core microLED component technologies, which are drawing attention as a next-generation display technology following organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displa

item.title: Colombia security forces storm site of supermarket hostage siege
item.description: CARTAGENA, Colombia — Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena early Wednesday in a bid to end a day-long hostage siege, AFP reporters said. Several explosions were heard before security forces moved into the building, where about 20 people were believed to be held by armed men. Authorities said 10 of the roughly 30 hostages initially held had been released after hours of negotiations, including several elderly women. AFP reporters earlier saw a police helicopter hovering low over the building, before the assault began. President Abelardo de la Espriella traveled to Cartagena as the crisis unfolded and met security commanders at the scene. Authorities have said the siege began after an attempted armored vehicle robbery.

item.description: A promotional video produced by Dalsung County, Daegu won the grand prize in the historical and cultural category at the third Korea Local Government Promotional Awards. According to Dalsung County on Tuesday, the Korea Local Government Promotional Awards, hosted and organized by the Korea Media and Video Promotion Institute and sponsored by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, and the Korea Communications Commission, evaluates promotional videos produced by local governments nationwide. “The Man Who Lives at Yuksinsa” was created to promote Yuksinsa, one of Dalsung County's representative historical sites. item.title: Foreign ministry discusses support for Korean firms facing challenges in India
item.description: The foreign ministry said Wednesday it held a meeting with Korean companies operating in India to discuss their business activities and ways to address difficulties they face in the country. The meeting, chaired by Lee Min-kyung, director-general for Asian and Pacific affairs, brought together representatives from major companies, including Hyundai Motor, Samsung Electronics and POSCO, as well as experts on India, according to the ministry. Participants exchanged views on business conditions in India and raised difficulties and requests for government support. The director-general said President Lee Jae Myung's summit with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in April served as an opportunity to take bilateral cooperation to a new level, adding that the ministry will further expand ties with India through high-level exchanges. item.title: Alice Huang-linked firms listed $270 mil. in AI servers in China, records show
item.description: BEIJING — Companies linked to Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman whose affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his short-lived exit, raised financing against powerful computing equipment for major AI data centers in China, previously unreported records reviewed by Reuters show. The central-bank documents identify up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million, along with $31 million in equipment used to connect them into large computing networks. Much of the hardware was listed as located at a sprawling Shanghai data center originally developed under a partnership with Chinese technology giant Tencent. The records show businesses connected to Alice Huang's family and associates helped finance and equip China's AI industry, even as U.S. authorities investigated whether her Singapore-based company Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain restricted Nvidia technology. item.title: Unionized rail workers to launch work-to-rule campaign Thursday
item.description: Unionized workers of Korea Railroad (KORAIL) said Wednesday they will launch a work-to-rule action this week as planned, making disruptions to train services likely. The Korean Railway Workers' Union said the action will begin at 9 a.m. Thursday and last through Dec. 4, with rail workers strictly adhering to safety and other regulations, such as not driving trains faster to make up for lost time, refusing to work overtime and responding to passenger complaints in line with manuals. The union has demanded improvements to the employee promotion system, extra allowances and additional personnel, threatening to launch an indefinite general strike Dec. 10 if the needs are not addressed. It has said rail workers have operated train services on time through endless overtime and holiday work, as well as by working solo in dangerous environments, and that if working to rule leads to delays or suspensions, the effort will prove the lack of personnel. item.title: [COVER STORY] Why spy agency chief nominee is under scrutiny
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung’s nomination of former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as chief of the nation's top spy agency is drawing mixed reactions over whether she is fit for the position. Supporters say Kang is an apolitical pick with experience in leading a government organization and is suitable for a time of strained ties with Washington. Critics, however, cite her lack of intelligence experience and her alleged closeness to China. If confirmed by the National Assembly, Kang, 69, would lead the National Intelligence Service (NIS), an agency central to national security, at a time when Seoul’s ties with Washington are strained over several issues, including Coupang and intelligence sharing. The U.S. has been limiting intelligence sharing with Seoul, a move that is believed to stem from Washington’s suspicion that Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly disclosed intelligence on North Korea that Washington had shared with Seoul. item.title: KOSPI sinks 6% as chip outlook, US tariff concerns weigh
item.description: The benchmark KOSPI plunged more than 6 percent Wednesday, erasing the previous session’s rally sparked by the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, which had surged on the news a day earlier, gave up all of their previous day’s gains, tumbling 9.87 percent and 11.05 percent, respectively. The sharp sell-off came as global investment banks cut their price targets for the country’s two semiconductor heavyweights, adding to concerns over the longer-term earnings outlook for companies that together account for nearly half of the index’s market capitalization. KOSPI opened at 4,809, down 3.94 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. A sell-sidecar was triggered at 9:08 a.m., shortly after the market opened, temporarily suspending program sell orders for five minutes amid heightened volatility. This brought the number of sidecars activated on KOSPI this year to 62, more than double the 26 recorded during the global financial crisis in 2008. item.title: KEPCO offers up to $6,800 in fraud coverage after data breach
item.description: Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO), the state-run power utility, announced Wednesday a three-pronged customer protection package offering free identity theft prevention services and financial fraud insurance worth up to 10 million won ($6,800) to prevent further damage from a massive personal data breach disclosed last week. Under the measures, KEPCO is providing all notified victims with free one-year subscriptions to NICE Information Service's Jikimi Careship program. The service blocks unauthorized credit inquiries and identity verification attempts and provides compensation of up to 10 million won for financial losses caused by identity theft. Registration codes are being sent in phases via KakaoTalk, text messages and email on Wednesday and Thursday. Customers can redeem the vouchers through Dec. 31, 2027. The service automatically expires after one year, with no additional charges. KEPCO is also directing affected customers to AccountInfo, an integrated account management service operated by the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute, and Msafer, a free identit

item.title: Who is Kang Kum-sil?
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's pick for spy agency chief, former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil, is drawing attention as she is returning to the main venue of politics after a decade out of the political spotlight. If the National Assembly confirms her for the post, Kang would become the first woman to lead the National Intelligence Service since the agency's predecessor was founded in 1961. Kang, 69, became the first justice minister under President Roh Moo-hyun in 2003. At 46, she was the youngest person and the first woman to hold the post. She remained the only woman to serve as justice minister until Choo Mi-ae, now governor of Gyeonggi Province, was appointed in 2020. Born on Jeju Island in 1957, Kang attended Kyunggi Girls’ High School and studied law at Seoul National University, long seen as the classic path into Korea's legal elite. She passed the bar exam in 1981 and served as a judge from 1983 to 1995. She was one of the judiciary’s leading progressive judges, co-founding the Uri Law Research Society in 1988 and helping lead major court reforms in 1993. After leaving the bench

item.title: 'Hanwha Group's spirit of challenge, Ourhome's expertise to fuel K-food growth'
item.description: Hanwha Group Chairman Kim Seung-youn has called for combining the group’s spirit of challenge with Ourhome’s food expertise during his first visit to the company’s research center since it became a Hanwha affiliate last year. “Let’s bring together Hanwha’s spirit of challenge and Ourhome’s strengths to create a bright future for K-food,” Kim wrote in the center’s guestbook during his visit Wednesday. Kim toured laboratories for food safety, flavors, home meal replacements and ice cream, reviewing product development and quality-control processes. He spent particular time at the food safety laboratory, where employees conduct tests for heavy metals, antibiotics and foodborne pathogens. “Ensuring food safety for customers is more important than developing differentiated flavors,” Kim said, urging employees to uphold strict safety standards throughout production and logistics. item.title: AI could shorten CSAT's lifespan: Seoul education chief
item.description: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help hasten the end of Korea’s college entrance exam, with its heavy reliance on multiple-choice questions? Seoul education superintendent Jung Geun-sik sees that possibility, but teachers experimenting with the technology offer a more cautious picture of what it takes to change how students are taught and tested. Speaking at Tuesday’s forum on the future of assessment, Jung recalled his earlier proposal to abolish the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by 2040. Recent AI developments and high-profile cheating incidents, he said, had led him to question whether the CSAT could even last that long. “At this pace, I wonder whether the CSAT will be viable next year or the year after. I had proposed abolishing it in 14 or 15 years, but the incidents surrounding this year’s exam have left me feeling that its lifespan may be much shorter,” he said. item.title: Finda to launch 'AI native' bank in Chuncheon
item.description: Fintech company Finda has chosen Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, as the base for its planned artificial intelligence (AI)-driven banking business, as it seeks to transform the operations of a savings bank it acquired earlier this year. Finda said Wednesday that it will relocate Daewon Savings Bank's headquarters from Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, to Chuncheon following a shareholder meeting next month, when the lender will officially be renamed Finda Savings Bank. Finda completed the acquisition of Daewon Savings Bank in October, becoming the first Korean fintech company to acquire a savings bank. The move comes as the fintech firm seeks to integrate AI into the bank's core operations, including customer services, loan assessments and credit management. The company plans to launch a new service early next year, with AI agents handling routine tasks while employees focus on decision-making and oversight. Finda, a loan comparison platform, said the technology would help the lender assess borrowers' repayment capacity and creditworthiness, while allowing it to develop more digital-focus

item.title: Korea's crypto exchanges face ownership shake-up under new Digital Asset Basic Act
item.description: Korea's biggest cryptocurrency exchanges face a potential ownership shake-up as regulators move to cap major shareholders' stakes at 20 percent, or up to 34 percent with regulatory approval, industry officials said Wednesday. The limits were among the draft provisions of the Digital Asset Basic Act unveiled Tuesday by the Financial Services Commission (FSC). The proposal seeks to ensure that crypto exchanges serve the public interest, bringing them in line with capital market standards. Even shareholders cleared to own as much as 34 percent would face restrictions on voting rights above the 20 percent threshold. Most Korean crypto exchanges would fail to meet the proposed ownership requirements and would have three to six years to comply once the legislation is enacted. The proposal comes as Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, pursues a merger with Naver Financial through a comprehensive share swap. Dunamu Chairman Song Chi-hyung is currently the exchange's largest shareholder, with a 25.51 percent stake. Under the deal, which is subject to review by the Fair Trade Commission, Naver Financial

item.title: AMCHAM, AI policy chief discuss ways to deepen US-Korea cooperation
item.description: The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) held a roundtable with a senior presidential adviser on artificial intelligence (AI) Wednesday to discuss ways to strengthen U.S.-Korea cooperation in AI and advance Korea's ambition to become one of the world's top three AI powers. Ha Jung-woo, vice chair of the Presidential Council on National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, met with AMCHAM Chairman James Kim and representatives of member companies at the chamber's office in Seoul. Ha outlined the government's national AI strategy and key policy priorities, while participants discussed ways to strengthen the country's AI ecosystem through expanded infrastructure, including data centers, and advances in semiconductors, AI models and software. The discussions also focused on the role of global technology companies and public-private partnerships in enhancing Korea's AI competitiveness and accelerating AI transformation across manufacturing and other key industries. Participants explored opportunities to leverage the complementary strengths of Korea and the United States in AI technolog

item.title: First lady Kim watches performance by orchestra of visually impaired musicians
item.description: First lady Kim Hea Kyung on Wednesday attended a concert by an orchestra composed of visually impaired musicians, along with this year's college entrance exam takers. The concert, held in Incheon, west of Seoul, featured the Hyegwang Blind Orchestra, a group of around 50 visually impaired musicians, and was intended to encourage high school seniors who took the grueling college entrance exam earlier this month. The first lady attended the concert at the invitation of a student from Hyegwang School, an educational institution for visually impaired students in Incheon, whom she met last month at an event marking the 100th anniversary of the Korean braille system. Kim praised the orchestra's "enthusiasm and efforts" in creating harmony, while commending the high school seniors in attendance and expressing her hope that they would go on to make their mark in the wider world.

item.title: N. Korea closes Swiss office in Pyongyang over sanctions on children's camp
item.description: North Korea on Wednesday shut down Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang, calling on its head to leave "within 48 hours" over the European nation's sanctions on a children's camp in North Korea. The move came a day after Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of the North's leader Kim Jong-un, threatened to shut down the Swiss diplomatic office, which opened in October, over its sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp, which is accused of involvement in the forced deportation of Ukrainian children. Pak Hyon-su, director general of the North's foreign ministry in charge of the European department, summoned Astier Sylvain, head of the Swiss diplomatic office, and handed him a memorandum of North Korea's foreign ministry urging the closure of the office, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). North Korea's foreign ministry "declared head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours," the report read, using the acronym of North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. item.title: Korean firms eye foreign government, UN contracts at record procurement event
item.description: Korean small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are pitching their products to overseas buyers in one-on-one meetings in Seoul as they seek contracts with foreign governments, U.N. agencies and other public institutions, the Public Procurement Service (PPS) said Wednesday. The agency opened its largest-ever export matchmaking event, the Global Public Procurement Marketplace (GPPM), at Grand Walkerhill Seoul on Wednesday. Now in its 11th edition, the event runs through Thursday and brings together a record 378 Korean companies, up about 16 percent from last year, and 95 overseas buyers. The PPS is co-hosting the event with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and KEPCO Plant Service & Engineering. This year, the agency is helping exporters diversify their markets by pursuing contracts with international organizations. Representatives from the United Nations Development Programme, the U.N. refugee agency and the International Organization for Migration are meeting one-on-one with Korean suppliers. item.title: Top court to deliver ruling on ex-first lady's bribery case next week
item.description: The Supreme Court will deliver its verdict on former first lady Kim Keon Hee's bribery case next week, legal sources said Wednesday. The top court scheduled her sentencing for next Thursday after Kim and a special counsel team both appealed an appellate ruling that sentenced her to a five-year prison term on bribery-related charges, according to the sources. Special counsel Min Joong-ki's team earlier indicted Kim, the wife of former President Yoon Suk Yeol, on charges of receiving expensive gifts from multiple people in return for job appointments and business favors. The alleged gifts include jewelry worth over 100 million won ($74,400) from a construction company chairman in exchange for a government job for his son-in-law in 2022. A district court sentenced Kim to seven years in prison in June after finding her guilty on all counts but the appellate court reduced her sentence in September, acquitting her of some of the charges. item.title: Popular military comedy 'New Recruit' to hit big screen with horror twist
item.description: Popular military comedy series "New Recruit" is heading to the big screen as a horror comedy featuring its original cast alongside K-pop girl group TWICE member Jeongyeon, who makes her acting debut. "While the TV series focused on sitcom-style humor centered on barracks life, I felt it was important to give audiences a clear reason to come to theaters for the movie," Min Jin-ki, director of the movie “New Recruit: Haunted Military Hospital” said during a press conference at a theater in Seoul. "To appeal even to viewers who have not served in the military, I focused on the keyword of military ghost stories." "I thought a horror comedy works best in a dark theater with surround sound, where both the scares and the laughs are doubled," he added. "Approaching a story set in a military hospital felt like something truly worth making into a film." Based on a popular web animation of the same title, the hit ENA drama series "New Recruit" has aired four seasons since 2022, following the daily lives of quirky soldiers at a military unit. item.title: Industry minister hints at exit strategy for fuel price cap
item.description: Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said Wednesday the government was considering a gradual exit from its fuel price cap introduced in response to the Middle East conflict, amid concerns over market distortions and the difficulties of compensating refiners for their losses. "When conditions allow, we intend to return gradually to normal pricing, potentially taking into account the differences between fuel products," Kim said at a press briefing Wednesday. However, he stressed that the government had yet to decide on any specific measures, adding that the price cap will remain in place for the time being as the situation in the Middle East continues to unfold. "We are not planning to take any immediate action. I was simply saying that this could be one of the options available as part of an eventual exit strategy," he replied when asked whether gasoline prices would be normalized first. Unlike gasoline, which is used primarily for passenger vehicles, diesel is used mainly in freight trucks and delivery vehicles. As such, changes in diesel prices may have more direct impact on businesses and p

item.title: Prosecutors seek to question Korean ambassador to China over alleged slush fund
item.description: Prosecutors investigating allegations that the family of the late former President Roh Tae-woo concealed a slush fund have asked his son, Ro Jae-hun, currently serving as the country's ambassador to China, to appear for questioning as a suspect, prosecution officials said Wednesday. The Seoul Central District Prosecutors Office recently issued a summons for Ro over alleged violations of the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, among other charges, the officials said. Prosecutors are reportedly coordinating with Ro to schedule his questioning for around the end of this month. The prosecution suspects that part of a slush fund allegedly held by the late president's family was funneled into the East Asia Cultural Foundation and the Roh Tae-woo Center, both chaired by Ro. Roh, who served as president from 1988-93, died in 2021. The alleged existence of the slush fund came to light during the divorce proceedings between Roh's daughter, Roh Soh-yeong, and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won. item.title: Prosecutors seek lengthy prison sentences for pastor, grandmother in fatal abuse of boy
item.description: Prosecutors on Wednesday sought a 25-year prison sentence for a church pastor on charges of fatally abusing an 11-year-old boy suffering from an intellectual disability. The boy died in August after he was strapped with metal chains to a bed at a church in Cheonan, about 80 kilometers south of Seoul, for 38 hours, during which he showed symptoms of high fever and exhaustion, according to the prosecution. At a trial at the Cheonan branch of the Daejeon District Court, prosecutors also sought a 20-year prison sentence for the child's grandmother for allegedly taking part in the crime, 12 years for the pastor's adopted son, and suspended prison terms of six months to a year for the pastor's younger sister and a church member. "The defendants abused an intellectually disabled child merely 11 years of age over a long period of time," a prosecutor said. item.title: Google, KBO team up to improve search experience for baseball fans
item.description: Google LLC said Wednesday it is teaming up with the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) to make the experience of searching for information online better for baseball fans in Korea as the country gears up for the regular season next year. Under the agreement, Google's search engine and artificial intelligence (AI) model Gemini will be introduced through the KBO's social media platforms, such as its official YouTube channel and Instagram, as well as live broadcasts of official matches. Google, on the other hand, will help fans search for information related to their favorite teams, such as information on athletes and past game results, integrating its technologies, the U.S. tech giant said. The two sides also plan to pursue various collaborations throughout the baseball season next year while planning to continue their partnership to provide colorful fan experiences based on the AI technology from Google, the U.S. tech giant added. item.title: Korean apparel makers bet on Central America as US tariff shifts squeeze margins: KIS report
item.description: Korean clothing contractors that make apparel for Walmart, Gap and Target are expanding production closer to the United States and building regional yarn and fabric operations as U.S. tariffs erode the cost advantage of their Southeast Asian plants. Korea Investors Service (KIS), a Moody's affiliate, said in a Nov. 24 report that heavy reliance on American buyers has turned U.S. trade policy into a major risk, along with rising wages, currency fluctuations and weak pricing power. While Southeast Asia remains central to their manufacturing footprints, companies are adjusting supply chains to protect duty free access and shorten delivery times. Hansae generated 94.9 percent of its 2025 revenue in the U.S., while Youngone and TP each derived about 60 percent of sales there, KIS said. Because those brands can spread orders across many suppliers, contract manufacturers struggle to pass along higher costs when trade rules or input prices change. Since April 2025, the U.S. tariff framework facing apparel suppliers has shifted repeatedly between country-specific levies, temporary global duties

item.title: Seoul public weddings surge 7.5-fold as couples seek distinctive venues
item.description: Seoul’s public wedding program has grown more than sevenfold over three years as couples increasingly choose parks, traditional Korean houses and cultural venues for personalized ceremonies that avoid the steep costs of conventional wedding halls. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that 563 weddings had been held or scheduled through its More Beautiful Weddings program as of the end of October, up from 75 in 2023, when the initiative began. Demand is continuing to rise, with 661 weddings already booked for 2027 as of October, surpassing this year's total. Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon met with three couples who had held weddings through the program and one couple planning to marry next April during a meeting Wednesday afternoon at Munhak House Seoul in Jung District. The gathering was intended to hear firsthand accounts of the wedding planning process and collect suggestions for improving the program. item.title: The cast and creators of 'SpongeBob SquarePants' look back on 27 years under the sea
item.description: LOS ANGELES — More than 27 years after “SpongeBob SquarePants” began airing on Nickelodeon, fans are still soaking up the enthusiastic sea sponge and his eccentric underwater neighbors. Even the actors, writers and artists who have worked to keep the animated series fresh without losing what made audiences fall in love with it in the first place can't explain why it has lasted so long. “It’s beyond luck. It’s not luck. It’s something crazier that we can’t really put our fingers on,” said Mr. Lawrence, who voices main antagonist Plankton and has written for the series since its earliest days. “I think most of the time I just always pinch myself and just go, I can’t believe not only that we’re working now, but that we hit on something that people are connecting with.” “SpongeBob SquarePants,” which has a new holiday special coming out Friday, remains the No. 1 animated show on linear television in the United States, according to the latest Nielsen animation report. item.title: Lee vows legal revision to punish domestic violence, even without victim's request
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung said Wednesday that his government will seek to revise the law to enable punishment for perpetrators of domestic violence even when their victims fail or refuse to file a complaint against them. The president made the remarks in a post on his X account to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, adding that it was the state's duty to create a society where women can live without fear. In Korea, perpetrators of domestic violence can avoid punishment if victims express a wish not to have them punished. However, the law has come under criticism over concerns that perpetrators may pressure victims into withholding consent to punishment, and that the lack of punishment could lead to more serious violence in the future. Citing a recent series of crimes involving domestic violence, stalking and dating abuse, Lee said the government had failed to "safeguard precious lives despite warning signs and calls for help." item.title: FM Cho calls on new KOICA chief to continue pursuing strategic development aid
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Wednesday called on the new head of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) to pursue strategic, demand-driven grant aid programs. Cho made the remarks during a ceremony to present an appointment letter to Oh Hyun-joo, who was appointed as KOICA president last week, according to the ministry. The strategic approach aims to align the country's grant aid with its foreign policy priorities and partner countries' development needs while improving coordination among government agencies to enhance the effectiveness of aid programs. Congratulating Oh on her appointment, Cho expressed hope that KOICA would strengthen its role as a key partner of the ministry in coordinating Korea's grant aid programs and continue pursuing strategic official development assistance (ODA). Cho also called on the agency to develop "substantive, field-oriented projects that reflect the needs of recipient countries." Oh vowed to work closely with the ministry to help implement the government's foreign policy strategy and development cooperation policy priorities, including effort
