item.title: Gov't reviewing various technologies to prevent AI-assisted cheating: minister
item.description: The government is reviewing various technologies to prevent cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) and other high-tech means, the science minister said Wednesday. Measures under consideration include communication and radio wave detection, watermark insertion on exam papers and behavior recognition using closed-circuit TVs (CCTVs), Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said during an event in Seoul. The ministry is also conducting a technical review on whether it could utilize jamming technology, or deliberate blocking of wireless signals used in special situations such as presidential security, but at a lower output, the minister added. On Seoul's partnership with global big tech firms regarding follow-up investigations of suspected cases of AI-aided cheating, Bae said the government is in the process of discussing the matter with such companies, whom he said "shared the same concern," on the AI-assisted cheating issue. "It is difficult to come up with a perfect solution from a single measure," the policymaker said, adding that the ministry plans to improve short- and long-term anti-chea

item.title: Korea's 1st Embraer C-390 transport aircraft lands at Seoul Air Base
item.description: The Korean Air Force’s first Embraer C-390 Millennium military transport aircraft landed Monday at Seoul Air Base in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, after a delivery flight that included stops in India and the Philippines. Built by Brazilian aerospace company Embraer, the C-390 is Korea’s first military transport aircraft powered by turbofan engines. It will supplement the Air Force’s existing fleet of turboprop transports. The Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) selected the C-390 in December 2023 under a program to acquire three large transport aircraft. A defense acquisition official said the program has a total budget of 883 billion won ($657.4 million), with the acquisition contract valued at 710 billion won. The aircraft arrived on the same day that DAPA and Brazil’s defense ministry held their first joint defense industry committee meeting in Brazil. DAPA said in a press release Tuesday that the two countries signed a letter of intent to expand defense industry cooperation. item.title: S-Oil completes $6.9 bil. Shaheen project, shifts growth engine toward petrochemicals
item.description: S-Oil has completed its 9.26 trillion won ($6.9 billion) Shaheen project, reshaping its business portfolio around a larger petrochemical operation, as the oil refiner looks to secure a new growth engine beyond the volatile refining cycle. The refiner celebrated Wednesday the completion of the project and its 50th anniversary. Key participants included senior government and business officials from Korea and Saudi Arabia, including Korea's Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan and Saudi Aramco President and CEO Amin H. Nasser. Aramco is the largest shareholder of S-Oil. The Shaheen project, located at S-Oil’s Onsan refinery in the southeastern city of Ulsan, is the largest petrochemical investment ever made in Korea. The project includes a thermal crude-to-chemicals facility that converts crude directly into petrochemical feedstock. The project will help S-Oil add about 3.2 million tons of annual petrochemical production capacity, more than doubling the share of petrochemicals in the firm’s overall production mix from 12 percent to 25 percent. S-Oil plans to complete commissioning this year

item.title: Kookmin University design students win multiple honors at Clio Sports Awards
item.description: Students from the Department of AI Design at Kookmin University’s College of Design have earned recognition at the Clio Sports Awards 2026, a leading international competition honoring creativity in sports advertising. “Unseen Marks,” an individual project by Moon Seung-chan, won two gold and two bronze awards, the university said. “Flip for Safety,” submitted by a team of three students — Moon, Seo Eun-sol and Park Si-yeon — was shortlisted in the student design category. item.title: Mom's Touch shifts focus to franchising in Japan
item.description: Mom's Touch is shifting its Japanese business from company-operated stores to franchise expansion, targeting 100 outlets by the end of 2027 after establishing a foothold in the competitive market. The Korean burger, chicken and pizza chain began testing the market with a pop-up store in Shibuya in October 2023 before opening its first overseas company-operated outlet there in April 2024. Located at a site previously occupied by McDonald's Japan for 39 years, the store attracted 100,000 customers and generated 100 million yen ($627,100) in sales within its first 40 days. By its second anniversary, cumulative visitors had reached 1.44 million and sales totaled approximately 1.12 billion yen. Its average annual sales last year were 1.9 times those of a typical McDonald's outlet in Japan and 7.7 times those of a Mos Burger store, based on the companies' 2025 disclosures. Over the past two years, Mom's Touch has invested approximately 20 billion won ($14.5 million) in building its Japanese operations and developing a franchise model tailored to local demand. item.title: Seoul winter festival expands to Han River with 52 days of lights, markets and celebrations
item.description: Seoul will turn its winter nights into an expansive festival stretching from its historic downtown to the banks of the Han River, with 52 days of light displays, Christmas markets, performances and New Year's celebrations beginning Dec. 11. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that the 2026 Seoul Winter Festa will run through Jan. 31, 2027, across Gwanghwamun Square, Cheonggye Stream, Seoul Plaza, Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Bosingak Pavilion and Ttukseom Hangang Park. Last year's festival drew 10.98 million visitors, and organizers are expanding this year's program to include the riverfront while extending festivities through the end of January. Under the theme "Fantasia Seoul," the festival will bring together seven major events, including Seoul Light Gwanghwamun, Gwanghwamun Market, Seoul Lantern Festival, Seoul Plaza Ice Skating Rink, Seoul Light DDP, SeoulCon and the Bosingak New Year's Eve bell-ringing ceremony. item.title: SK Group chief's ex-wife opposes seeking court-recommended compromise for settlement: lawyer
item.description: Roh Soh-yeong, the former wife of SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, disapproves of his request to the Supreme Court to recommend a compromise for their property settlement case, her legal representative said Wednesday. Roh submitted a statement to the top court outlining her stance against Chey's request filed Monday, according to the representative. In his request, Chey voiced a willingness to pay the full 944 billion won ($700 million) in property settlement to Roh, as ordered by an appeals court, apparently stepping back from his appeal against the July ruling. "If Chey is sincere about an early resolution, he should immediately drop his appeal," Roh's representative said. A court recommendation of a compromise has the effect of a finalized ruling if the plaintiff and the defendant both do not raise objections within two weeks. Chey's representatives earlier said they were seeking a compromise recommendation for an "amicable and final end" to the legal dispute. item.title: Banks' household mortgage lending rates hit over 14-year high in Oct.
item.description: Banks' household mortgage loan rates rose for the sixth consecutive month to the highest point in 14 years and seven months in October on rising market interest, central bank data showed Wednesday. The average interest rate on new bank loans stood at 4.64 percent last month, up 0.07 percentage point from a month earlier, according to the data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The average rate on corporate loans increased 0.06 percentage point to 4.55 percent last month, and the rate on new household loans rose 0.06 percentage point to 5.02 percent, topping the 5 percent line for the first time since November 2023. The average rate on household mortgage loans increased 0.1 percentage point to 4.98 percent in October, extending its winning streak that started in May. It marked the highest level since March 2012, when the average household mortgage rate came to 5 percent. Last month, the BOK kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3 percent after consecutive rate hikes in July and August aimed at curbing rising inflation caused by prolonged tensions in the Middle East and robust economic g

item.title: Hyundai Motor Group unveils unified EV charger ahead of 2027 global rollout
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group is preparing to bring a more consistent charging experience to electric vehicle (EV) owners worldwide, unveiling a new home charger designed to work across its Hyundai, Kia and Genesis brands ahead of an international rollout beginning in 2027. The HMG Global AC Charger consolidates designs and user experiences that previously varied by brand and market, the automaker said Wednesday. Hyundai Motor and Kia led product planning, technology development and design, while Hyundai Kefico participated in product development and will oversee mass production, drawing on its expertise in automotive electronics and EV charging systems. Designed primarily for home use, the charger will initially offer 7-kilowatt and 11-kilowatt output options in Korea and support the Type 1 (J1772) charging standard widely used in the domestic market. item.title: Baemin delivery robots set to bring food orders to Seoul apartment doorsteps
item.description: Food deliveries in Seoul could soon reach apartment doorsteps without a human courier entering the building, as Baemin operator Woowa Brothers deploys autonomous delivery robots in residential complexes — including some of the capital’s wealthiest neighborhoods. Woowa Brothers said Wednesday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Tower PMC, a premium residential property management company, to expand its robot delivery service into apartment buildings, with a door-to-door launch targeted for next year. Under the agreement, the companies will introduce Baemin’s delivery robot, Dilly, to residential complexes managed by Tower PMC and develop infrastructure allowing robots to travel from restaurant entrances to individual apartment doors. The partners plan to select pilot sites in Seoul and install systems linking the robots to building entrances, elevators and designated waiting areas. item.title: Hanwha Aerospace wins export rights for KM3 amphibious bridging vehicle
item.description: Hanwha Aerospace secured the right to export the KM3, an amphibious bridging vehicle it builds under license for the Korean military, the company said Wednesday. The defense firm revised its manufacturing license agreement on Nov. 3 with Germany's General Dynamics European Land Systems-Bridge Systems, which developed the M3 system on which the KM3 is based. The revision allows Hanwha to sell the vehicle to some countries in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Nicknamed Suryong, the KM3 drives into rivers and either ferries equipment across or links up with other units to form a floating bridge, allowing tanks, self-propelled howitzers and armored vehicles to cross. Hanwha is the only M3 buyer that also manufactures the vehicle and the first to obtain export rights. The company has been delivering the KM3 to the Korean military since June 2024, and the vehicle recently completed field trials and deployment evaluations. The revision allows Hanwha to sell the vehicle to some countries in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Nicknamed Suryong, the KM3 drives into rivers and either ferries equipment across or links up with other units to form a floating bridge, allowing tanks, self-propelled howitzers and armored vehicles to cross. Hanwha is the only M3 buyer that also manufactures the vehicle and the first to obtain export rights. The company has been delivering the KM3 to the Korean military since June 2024, and the vehicle recently completed field trials and deployment evaluations. item.title: Hyundai Glovis opens Incheon airport logistics center to expand air freight biz
item.description: Hyundai Glovis, the logistics arm of Hyundai Motor Group, has opened its own air logistics hub at Incheon International Airport as it seeks to grow its air freight business, the company said Wednesday. The company held an opening ceremony Tuesday for the Incheon Airport Logistics Center in the airport's second logistics complex. The five-story facility, with a total floor area of 44,420 square meters, broke ground in 2023 and went into full operation this year. It recently received customs approval to handle express import shipments, adding to its export cargo services. The center sits about 3 kilometers from the airport's cargo terminal. The center is equipped with automated systems designed for e-commerce shipments. Its first-floor express import clearance area can process more than 1 million parcels a month. Four high-speed X-ray machines can screen a combined 5,000 items per hour, with scan data sent to Incheon Airport customs in real time. item.title: Busan tourism portal lets travelers tweak itineraries via AI chat service
item.description: Travelers planning a trip to Busan can now ask an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to reshape their itinerary in plain language, such as requesting less walking on the first day, the city and the Busan Tourism Organization said Wednesday. The two upgraded the AI travel recommendation service on Visit Busan, the city's official tourism portal, on Monday. The service, first launched in September 2024, suggests customized courses based on trip length, travel companions and interests. The revamped version runs on generative AI built on a large language model, the type of technology behind chatbots such as ChatGPT. Users can keep chatting to shorten walking routes or add and remove stops without re-entering their trip details. A traveler who receives a two-day itinerary, for example, can type "Make me walk less on the first day" and then "Change lunch to a seafood restaurant," and the AI will apply the second request to the already adjusted schedule. Users can also add or drop places and change the order of visits directly on the itinerary. The schedule is displayed alongside a map showin

item.title: Tech-driven architect Carlo Ratti to direct 2027 Seoul Biennale
item.description: An architect known for exploring how digital technology, nature and human behavior can reshape cities will lead Seoul’s next international architecture biennale, bringing a distinctly technology-driven perspective to one of the capital’s major cultural events. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday it had appointed Italian architect and urban researcher Carlo Ratti as artistic director of the sixth Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism, scheduled for 2027. Ratti is a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Politecnico di Milano, where his work examines the relationship between architecture, urban planning, engineering and digital technology. He also directs MIT’s Senseable City Lab and co-founded CRA-Carlo Ratti Associati, an architecture and design practice established in 2002. His research uses urban data and sensor technologies to examine changes in transportation, the environment and public spaces, with the aim of understanding how cities can adapt to changing conditions. Recent projects include the Essential torch for the 2026 Milan-Cort

item.title: Korea takes regional tourism push to Shenzhen, turning APEC momentum into travel demand
item.description: From regional food specialties to beauty experiences and direct flights, Korea brought its local travel offerings to Shenzhen last week, seeking to turn growing interest in Korean culture into visits beyond Seoul. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization held the 2026 Korea Festival in the Chinese city from Nov. 21–24, joining forces with the Korean Cultural Center in Hong Kong, the Korea Agro-Fisheries and Food Trade Corp. and the Korea Creative Content Agency. The event followed the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, using the gathering's momentum to promote regional destinations and encourage Chinese travelers to explore more of Korea. Shenzhen, home to about 18 million residents and technology companies including Tencent and Huawei, was selected as a target market for its young consumer base, whose average age is 33. item.title: Publishers pitch book rights to Italian buyers in online meetings
item.description: Korean publishers are pitching book rights to Italian and other European buyers through online meetings rather than traveling to Milan for a live showcase, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Wednesday. The ministry and the Publication Industry Promotion Agency of Korea are hosting the Visiting Korean Book Fair in Milano: Online Rights Meetings from Wednesday through Friday at a venue in Jung District, central Seoul. It is the first time the program, launched in 2015 to arrange one-on-one export talks between Korean and foreign publishers, has targeted Italy. The event was originally planned for Milan but moved online amid an unstable situation in Europe and concerns over rallies and a nationwide general strike in Italy. Seventeen Korean publishers, including Dasan Books, are taking part. Green Book Agency will represent 85 titles from publishers unable to attend. On the buying side are 47 Italian publishers and literary agencies plus five film and video producers and distributors. item.title: Seoul exhibition explores bold new possibilities for traditional hanok
item.description: Traditional Korean houses are being reimagined for modern urban life in a Seoul exhibition that brings together 12 award-winning architectural proposals and five completed projects, offering a glimpse of how an age-old building tradition could shape the city’s future. The Seoul Metropolitan Government will host the special exhibition, titled “Future of Seoul Hanok: From Imagination to Practice,” starting Thursday at Bukchon Cultural Center and Baeryeom House in Jongno District, the city government said Wednesday. The exhibition, running until Dec. 6, will showcase winning entries from the second Seoul Hanok Future Award design competition, alongside architectural projects exploring contemporary interpretations of "hanok," or traditional Korean architecture. A total of 70 teams entered this year’s competition, which focused on the Jeiggi-dong 988 area, where traditional markets and narrow hanok neighborhoods coexist. item.title: Yoon & Yang lawyer wins ALB Young Lawyer of the Year award for cross-border IP work
item.description: Kim Yoon-sun, a senior foreign attorney at Yoon & Yang, has been named Young Lawyer of the Year at the 2026 ALB Korea Law Awards for her work on high-profile intellectual property and cross-border cases, the law firm said Wednesday. The awards, organized annually by Asian Legal Business (ALB), a legal publication owned by Thomson Reuters, recognize the work of private practitioners, in-house counsel and law firms in the industry, with winners judged on the significance and complexity of the cases they handle. The Young Lawyer of the Year category honors a partner-level lawyer under 40 who has made a notable contribution to some of the year’s most significant deals or disputes. Kim was selected from a field of 11 finalists for her work on international disputes involving patents, trade secrets and the biohealth sector. She has helped develop legal strategies and coordinate proceedings across multiple jurisdictions in close collaboration with local counsel, contributing to the early resolution of a major U.S. patent litigation and favorable licensing agreements, according to Yoon & Yang

item.title: Global disaster misinfo fuels panic-buying at chain stores
item.description: Photos of bottled water, canned foods and spare batteries have flooded social media as consumers around the world stockpile emergency supplies in response to a wave of doomsday theories about an impending world war. To prepare for the intensifying strain of extreme weather and prolonged conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, countries such as the United Kingdom and Japan have recently advised households to check their cupboards to make sure they have at least three days' worth of essentials, from non-perishable foods to baby formula and first-aid kits. But the guidelines, which seek to prepare people for all kinds of hazards, have been embroiled in online rumour-mongering that has stoked public anxiety and panic-buying. Scores of social media users in the United States, Europe and Asia linked the updates to a spate of tech outages that disrupted flights and banking apps, speculating that another global conflict was just around the corner. item.title: Sejong University team assesses potential, limits of generative AI in crop breeding
item.description: A Sejong University research team has called for rigorous validation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in crop breeding, saying evidence of their effectiveness in real-world applications remains limited despite growing expectations for AI-assisted agriculture. The team’s review, published online Nov. 4 in Molecular Plant, the world’s top-ranked plant science journal, examines the capabilities and limitations of generative AI and other AI-based breeding technologies. Led by Kim Kyung-do, a professor in the university’s Department of Integrative biological Sciences and Industry, the team conducted the study with researchers from the University of Georgia in the United States. The paper, titled “Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges,” was co-authored by Han Ji-heon, a Sejong doctoral student, who served as first author. Kim and University of Georgia professors Scott A. Jackson and Ethan Pickering were co-corresponding authors. “AI should serve as a tool to support breeders’ decision-making rather tha

item.title: Population mobility up slightly in October on base effect
item.description: The number of Koreans who moved to new residences rose slightly in October from a year earlier due to a low base effect, but the downside trend continued, government data showed Wednesday. Around 453,000 people changed residences to other administrative districts in October, up 2.6 percent, or 11,000, from a year earlier, according to the monthly tally from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The ministry attributed the on-year increase to a base effect as the number fell sharply in October last year amid the Chuseok holiday season. This year's Chuseok fell in September based on the lunar calendar that changes from year to year. However, the ministry said the country's population mobility is in a steady decline from a long-term perspective amid a rapidly aging and decreasing population. The monthly figure dropped to 378,000 people in September, marking the lowest level since 1973. By region, Seoul reported a net outflow of 5,560 people, and the southeastern port city of Busan also recorded a net outflow of 768. item.title: Births in Korea jump 12.2% in September, fastest 9-month growth on record
item.description: The number of babies born in Korea rose 12.2 percent in September from a year earlier, with the cumulative nine-month tally increasing at the fastest pace on record, government data showed Wednesday. A total of 25,113 babies were born in September, up 12.2 percent, or 2,731, from a year earlier, rising for the 27th consecutive month, according to the Ministry of Data and Statistics. It marked the largest figure for any September in eight years, while the year-on-year growth rate was the second highest for the month, following the 16.6 percent rise recorded in 2007. For the first nine months of the year, the number of newborns totaled 218,896, up 14.3 percent from 191,593 a year earlier, marking the sharpest year-on-year growth since the ministry began compiling related data in 1981. The recent increase in births came amid a growing number of marriages, a rise in the population in their 30s and more positive attitudes toward having children. As a result, the country's total fertility rate, which refers to the average number of children a woman is expected to have over her lifetime, rose 0.

item.title: Korea, UN agree to set up working group on peacekeeping contributions
item.description: Korea and the United Nations have agreed to establish a joint working group to discuss ways to expand Seoul's contributions to U.N. peacekeeping operations (PKO) following the planned withdrawal of its troops from Lebanon next year, the foreign ministry said Wednesday. The agreement was reached during separate meetings in New York on Monday (local time) between Chang Wook-jin, the ministry's coordinator-general for international organizations and global affairs, and Mohamed Khaled Khiari, U.N. assistant secretary-general for the Department of Peace Operations, and Atul Khare, under-secretary-general for the Department of Operational Support, according to the ministry. The working group will coordinate the safe withdrawal of the Dongmyeong unit from Lebanon and discuss ways to strengthen Korea's contributions to peacekeeping efforts. The unit is scheduled to withdraw next year following the termination of the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate on Dec. 31 under a U.N. Security Council resolution. item.title: Virtual, AI acts crowd K-pop debut week
item.description: Late November is usually a busy stretch for K-pop rookies hoping to make their mark before the year ends, but four of this season's newcomers are joining the race without a human face on screen. The last full week of the month is seeing a HYBE-backed VTuber project, an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated boy group and two virtual idol acts release their first music, a cluster that shows how quickly nonhuman acts are becoming a regular part of the industry's release calendar. Though often lumped together, the four fall into two distinct camps. Virtual idols, a category led by boy band PLAVE, are fronted by real performers who sing, dance and talk with fans through animated avatars. AI idols, on the other hand, have their looks and videos generated by AI with no single performer behind each member, even if human creatives still shape much of the music and direction. That difference has shaped how fans receive them. item.title: A year after Hong Kong's deadly fire, survivors struggle with loss and lingering sense of injustice
item.description: HONG KONG — Yip Ka-kui still sends WhatsApp voice messages to his wife even though they will never be heard. She was one of 168 people killed last November in Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades. Over the past year, the 68-year-old Yip never turned on the television, struggled to step into a supermarket and stopped taking photos outdoors with his camera — all things he used to do with his wife, Pak Shui-lin. He learned to dine alone. Sometimes, he would cry when thoughts of her crept in. The hardest moments came at night, when sleep eluded him hours past midnight. Now living at his eldest son's place within walking distance of their charred apartment at Wang Fuk Court, Yip has preferred mostly to stay at home in recent months because the familiar streets are full of memories. “Sometimes, a feeling would suddenly flood in,” he said. “I can't believe she's no longer here." item.title: PM says Seoul's development aid will focus on helping partner nations grow on their own
item.description: Korea will focus its official development assistance (ODA) on helping recipient nations tackle problems on their own and grow, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Wednesday. Han made the remark during a ceremony commemorating International Development Cooperation Day that marks South Korea's accession in 2009 to the OECD Development Assistance Committee, the first case of a recipient nation joining the grouping of rich countries. "The number of places in need of assistance continues to grow due to conflicts, climate disasters, famine and diseases while at the same time, the financial resources remain limited, leaving us with the task of how to maximize the impact of our support," Han said. "For us to address this together, partner nations must develop the capacity to solve their own problems and grow," she said. item.title: Remains of Korean Army corporal killed in Vietnam War to be returned home
item.description: The remains of a Korean soldier who died while serving in the Vietnam War will return home, marking the repatriation 59 years after his death, the defense ministry said Wednesday. The ceremony marking the return of late Army Cpl. Ahn Gyu-tae will take place at Seoul Airport in Seongnam, south of Seoul, overseen by Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul, according to the ministry. His remains will be transferred home from Hawaii via the Air Force's C-130 aircraft, it added. item.title: UNESCO spotlights Korea's cultural heritage in new global video series
item.description: A new UNESCO video series is bringing Korea’s cultural heritage to a global audience, showcasing ancient temples, historic villages and living traditions in a campaign that has already begun attracting attention through the international organization’s digital platforms. The fourth season of the UNESCO World Heritage Series, titled “Korea: A journey through time,” is being released in installments on UNESCO’s official Instagram, YouTube and other social media channels through Dec. 22, the Korea Heritage Service said Wednesday. The series, supported by the Korea Heritage Service and the World Heritage Interpretation and Presentation Centre (WHIPIC), features six World Heritage sites and three elements of Korea’s intangible cultural heritage. Launched in 2024, the short-form video initiative aims to highlight the outstanding universal value of World Heritage sites and the importance of preserving them, according to UNESCO. item.title: Father Ham Je-doe, who made more than 60 trips to North Korea, dead at 93
item.description: CHEONGJU — Father Ham Je-doe, born Gerard Hammond, an American Maryknoll missionary who spent more than six decades in Korea and devoted himself to humanitarian work in North Korea, died Monday. He was 93. The Diocese of Cheongju announced that Father Hammond, who had been hospitalized at Cheongju St. Mary's Hospital due to age-related illness, died at 7:46 a.m. Monday. Born in Philadelphia in 1933, Hammond graduated from Maryknoll Seminary and was ordained a priest before choosing Korea as his first mission destination in 1960. After arriving in Korea, he served as director of the Sacred Heart Orphanage in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, caring for children. He later spent more than 30 years conducting pastoral work in the Diocese of Cheongju, dedicating himself to evangelization and social service in the region. In particular, while serving as the first pastor of Sudong Catholic Church in Cheongju, he donated an inheritance from his grandparents to secure land for a church and kindergarten. The Sudong Church, built on the site, was designated a registered cultural heritage site

item.title: Retail sales rise 5.7% in October on steady online sales
item.description: Korea's retail sales rose in October from a year earlier on solid sales from online platforms, government data showed Wednesday. Combined sales of 26 major retail companies increased 5.7 percent from a year earlier, according to data by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. Offline retailers reported a 1.4 percent decrease in sales due mainly to sluggish sales in large discount outlets as the Chuseok holiday fell in September this year. Last year, the Korean equivalent of Thanksgiving Day was in October based on the lunar calendar. Revenue at major online retail platforms rose a solid 10.9 percent from a year earlier in October on steady demand for food and delivery services. Online platforms accounted for 60.3 percent of total retail sales in October.

item.title: Changwon court judges voice concern over ruling party's push to impeach chief justice
item.description: Judges at a regional district court voiced deep concern Wednesday over the ruling Democratic Party of Korea's (DPK) push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae. The judges issued a statement taking issue with the impeachment push following a regular general meeting of all judges at the Changwon District Court in Changwon, about 300 kilometers southeast of Seoul. "Seeking to impeach judges over rulings conducted independently under the Constitution and law undermines the constitutional values of judicial independence and separation of powers and shakes the foundation of the judicial system," the statement said. "(We) voice deep concern over attempts to endanger the separation of powers and constitutional order, such as impeaching judges on the grounds of rulings." The DPK announced its decision to seek Cho's impeachment after the Supreme Court on Thursday partially overturned an appellate ruling that sentenced former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo to 15 years in prison for playing a key role in former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid. item.title: Samsung SDI Ulsan plant earns top green management award
item.description: Samsung SDI said Wednesday that its Ulsan plant has won the Grand Prize at the 2026 Green Management Awards, organized by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute (KEITI). The plant received the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Award in the Excellent Green Company category, which recognizes companies demonstrating outstanding environmental management in areas such as carbon neutrality and resource conservation. The Green Management Awards recognize exemplary achievements in environmental management, environmental information disclosure and environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. Samsung SDI's Ulsan plant became the first battery industry facility in Korea to receive Green Company designation in 1999 and has maintained the status for 27 consecutive years, reflecting its long-standing commitment to environmentally responsible operations. item.title: Handong partners with Korea Mediation Institute to promote mediation education
item.description: The Handong International Law School (HILS) and the Handong Institute for Arbitration and Reconciliation (HIAR) have signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Mediation Institute (KMI) to expand academic and practical collaboration and enhance students’ mediation skills. Handong Global University said the agreement was signed on Nov. 11 by HILS Dean Lee Hee-eun, HIAR President Shin Eun-joo and KMI President Moon Yong-ho. HILS and HIAR are affiliated with the university. The partnership aims to draw on the expertise and resources of the three institutions to advance mediation education, promote joint research and help develop mediation practices. Under the agreement, the three institutions will jointly develop and offer courses, lectures, workshops and practical programs in mediation and negotiation. item.title: Hyundai Mobis wins $744 mil. orders from clients in Europe, North America
item.description: Hyundai Mobis has secured about 1 trillion won ($744 million) in orders for electronic regenerative braking and electronic steering systems from major automakers in Europe and North America, strengthening its position as a global supplier of safety-critical automotive components, the auto parts maker said Wednesday. The company won orders for its integrated Mobis Electronic Brake system and electronic power steering system from major customers in the two regions. The components will be supplied for up to eight years starting in three to four years. The orders cover a range of vehicle models, including sedans, SUVs and pickup trucks. Hyundai Mobis did not share the names of the clients under a nondisclosure agreement. Hyundai Mobis said it was selected as a supplier based on its technological competitiveness in braking and steering systems, which are directly linked to vehicle safety. item.title: Global Public Procurement Marketplace kicks off in Seoul
item.description: An event aimed at helping Korean companies connect with overseas procurement markets kicked off its two-day run in Seoul on Wednesday, the Public Procurement Service (PPS) said. The Global Public Procurement Marketplace 2026, co-hosted by the PPS, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and KEPCO KPS, brings together over 110 prospective buyers and more than 330 local companies, the PPS said. This year, PPS has placed particular emphasis on expanding opportunities for domestic companies to enter new overseas public procurement markets, including those of international organizations, and supporting export market diversification. item.title: Korea slashes nationality reinstatement wait times to 9 months for ethnic Koreans living abroad
item.description: The Ministry of Justice has significantly accelerated the nationality reinstatement process for ethnic Koreans living abroad, cutting the average review time by four months — from 13 months down to nine. For applicants experiencing the fastest processing, wait times have been reduced by as much as seven months, offering swift relief to thousands eager to formally reconnect with their homeland. The breakthrough stems from an intensive, three-month processing campaign conducted between August and October, according to the ministry. Facing a growing backlog fueled by a steady rise in applications from ethnic Koreans living abroad, the ministry overhauled its operational capacity. Previously, a single dedicated officer handled the workload, processing an average of roughly 220 cases per month. By deploying four additional specialists to the team, the ministry dramatically scaled up its output, resolving a total of 4,664 cases over the three-month period. This boosted the monthly average to 1,555 cases — more than seven times the previous pace. For overseas Koreans seeking to restore thei

item.title: Late firefighter in Bucheon factory blaze named person of national merit
item.description: A firefighter killed in the line of duty while battling a factory fire in a city southwest of Seoul last month has been registered as a person of national merit, the veterans ministry said Wednesday. The decision was finalized upon approval by a review committee of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs on Friday and his bereaved family was notified earlier this week, according to the ministry. Fire Lt. Kim Jin-seok died from severe injuries sustained while battling a blaze that broke out at a metalworking factory in Bucheon, just west of Seoul, on Oct. 16. Six other firefighters were also injured. Kim's death sparked calls for a review of firefighting protocols amid questions over whether crews should be rushed into containment efforts without properly assessing the scene to minimize on-site risks to personnel. Local authorities have since launched a probe into the incident to determine whether safety protocols were adequately followed. item.title: Korea's consumer goods exports hit record high amid Korean culture boom
item.description: Exports of Korean beauty, food, fashion and cultural products hit a record high amid the global popularity of Korean culture as the country's total exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, customs data showed Wednesday. Shipments of such Korean consumer goods totaled $28.65 billion from January through Thursday, when the country hit the export milestone, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. The figure marked a 21.5 percent spike from the same period last year and already surpassed last year's full-year total of $27.02 billion. Exports of beauty products surged 34.6 percent on-year to $13.65 billion over the cited period on steady demand for Korean cosmetics. This accounted for 47.6 percent of total consumer goods exports. In 2025, exports of beauty products totaled $11.61 billion, accounting for 43 percent of the total. Outbound shipments of Korean food increased 9.3 percent to $10.94 billion, driven by strong sales of "ramyeon," or instant noodles, and marine products. item.title: US ready to slap tariffs on China, EU and others over subsidized production, AP sources say
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is expected to soon announce plans to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and 14 other economies, according to two people familiar with the matter. The U.S. Trade Representative's Office is expected to release the results of a monthslong tariff investigation into the industrial subsidies by the 16 economies in the coming days, according to the people who were not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity. They stressed the timing for the rollout of the tariffs could still change. The White House and USTR did not respond to requests for comment. Plans for the new tariffs are part of an effort to replace broader duties the administration set last year that were subsequently struck down by the Supreme Court. The plans were reported earlier on Tuesday by Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal. item.title: North Korea to consider shutting down Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea condemned Switzerland on Tuesday for sanctioning a North Korean children's camp over the transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine and said it would consider shutting down the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang, state media said. North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's influential sister, Kim Yo-jong, said the Swiss sanctions infringed on the country's sovereignty and demonstrated hostility towards Pyongyang, KCNA state news agency reported. Voice of America reported last week that Switzerland had added North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp to its sanctions list for cooperating with Russia-linked groups to transfer children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. Reuters could not immediately confirm the Swiss measure. The sanctions deny North Korea's obligation to provide all children with opportunities for culture and recreation and leave "an indelible stain" on its international reputation as a country that promotes humanitarianism, Kim Yo-jong said in a statement. item.title: Nvidia board joins Jensen Huang under scrutiny after reinstating embattled CEO
item.description: NEW YORK — Jensen Huang has been under a spotlight for weeks, but after the 11-day period of disorder that included the resignation and reinstatement of the Nvidia executive, the company's board is joining him at the center of scrutiny. The 10-person board voted unanimously to rehire Huang as Nvidia's president, CEO and a fellow board member, writing in an announcement Monday that the decision emerged after discussions with Huang and “input from senior levels of the United States government.” President Donald Trump said he believes his intervention was crucial to the reinstatement. Just six days earlier, the board was singing a different tune. Board members had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation following his admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy . The board did not intend to reinstate him, Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of a quarterly earnings call. “To bow to pressure to bring someone back who has hurt the reputation of the company is crazy,” said Kathleen Day, a lecturer at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. item.title: Shanghai party pledges loyalty to Beijing as top official faces investigation
item.description: BEIJING — Shanghai's senior Communist Party leadership pledged loyalty to Beijing and understanding of the need to "see things through to the end" after their top official was put under investigation, the financial hub's official paper said on Wednesday. Shanghai's party chief Chen Jining, a member of China's elite Politburo, is under investigation, the government unexpectedly announced on Tuesday, making him the fourth member of the top leadership body to be probed since 2025. China's anti-graft watchdog said in a terse statement that it was investigating Chen for "suspected severe violations of discipline and laws," using a common euphemism for corruption. It gave no details. Chinese President Xi Jinping has overseen a sweeping anti-corruption crackdown since assuming party leadership in 2012. A front-page story in the Shanghai party branch's Jiefang Daily said officials had convened a late-night meeting to discuss the probe into Chen. item.title: Federal grand jury indicts Thomas Markle on child sex abuse material charges
item.description: LOS ANGELES — A federal grand jury in Los Angeles on Tuesday indicted the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, on charges that he kept child sexual abuse material — including photos where Markle himself was pictured with prepubescent children, according to prosecutors. If convicted, Thomas Wayne Markle, 82, could be sentenced to up to 40 years in prison, according to a statement shared by top Los Angeles federal prosecutor Bill Essayli. Markle was arrested in early November after federal officials say they found dozens of illicit images, including film negatives, slides and books depicting suspected child abuse, in a storage facility in Los Angeles. Court filings also allege Markle possessed similar material in the Philippines, where he has a home and where some of the lewd photos of the children appear to have been taken. If convicted, Thomas Wayne Markle, 82, could be sentenced to up to 40 years in prison, according to a statement shared by top Los Angeles federal prosecutor Bill Essayli. Markle was arrested in early November after federal officials say they found dozens of illicit images, including film negatives, slides and books depicting suspected child abuse, in a storage facility in Los Angeles. Court filings also allege Markle possessed similar material in the Philippines, where he has a home and where some of the lewd photos of the children appear to have been taken. Markle himself was identified by a witness in at least two photos with a nude, prepubescent girl, according to the indictment. item.title: Bourse operator activates sell-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp fall
item.description: Korea's bourse operator on Wednesday activated a sell-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the market came under heavy selling pressure. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes from 9:09 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). This comes as investors tracked overnight losses in technology stocks on Wall Street. A sell-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index falls 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

item.title: Seoul shares down over 5% late Wednesday morning on tech rout
item.description: Korean shares extended their losses late Wednesday morning, reversing the previous session's rally, as investors tracked overnight losses in technology stocks on Wall Street. After opening a sharp 3.94 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its losses, shedding 277.22 points, or 5.54 percent, to 4,728.81 as of 11:20 a.m., and falling below the psychologically important 5,000 mark. As the market lost ground, the Korea Exchange activated a sell-side sidecar at 9:09 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. On Tuesday, the KOSPI rebounded more than 6 percent as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to the spotlight. Overnight, U.S. stocks closed mixed as Nvidia gave back part of its historic gains from the previous day and concerns over fresh U.S. tariffs weighed on the tech sector. item.title: Pope Francis saw vision of 'gates of hell' after journalists' questions about clergy sex abuse
item.description: VATICAN CITY — As papal news conferences go, the one with Pope Francis on the flight home from his trip to Chile in 2018 was unusual in every way. Turbulence had forced a pause in the questioning, but when Francis returned to his place at the front of the economy section of the papal plane, I picked up where others had left off. I had a sharp exchange with him about the clergy sexual abuse scandal in the South American country. Like other journalists, I challenged him because he had discredited victims of Chile’s most notorious abuser and seemed completely indifferent to their pain. Only now, after reading “The Private Diary of Pope Francis,” did I realize how much the Argentine pope had suffered when he understood the depths of the problem in Chile. item.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury finds
item.description: NEW YORK — A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks as it grew into one of the world’s biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks. But jurors acquitted Huawei of the most serious charge: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy, a result that the company's lawyer said was a “profound rejection” of the government's narrative that it was corrupt from top to bottom and had a corporate culture of cheating, stealing and lying. Prosecutors had used the charge, commonly found in organized crime and drug cases, to accuse Huawei of operating illicitly to poach intellectual property and technological secrets from competitors and partners. The convictions covered allegations that the company did business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions — including Iran and North Korea — and made false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds. item.title: N. Korea's Yongbyon nuclear complex expansion may boost weapons-grade uranium production, says US science institute
item.description: WASHINGTON — North Korea's latest expansion of a uranium enrichment facility at its Yongbyon nuclear complex may be aimed at increasing its production of weapons-grade uranium, a U.S. research institute assessed Tuesday. The Washington-based Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) made the assessment in a report based on satellite imagery of the facility, located some 100 kilometers north of Pyongyang, whose rapid expansion has drawn concern from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). The institute said satellite imagery of the newly built extension indicated that it consists primarily of a large hall without internal dividing walls, raising the possibility that it could accommodate additional uranium enrichment equipment. "Another possibility is that the added hall is designed specifically to make weapon-grade uranium (WGU)," the report said. Other possible purposes include increasing low-enriched uranium production, expanding operational support for existing enrichment facilities or accommodating research and development activities, according to the report. item.title: Biz sentiment drops for the first time in 5 months
item.description: Korea's business sentiment fell for the first time in five months in November due mainly to sluggish sales and rising inventory, a central bank survey showed Wednesday. The Composite Business Sentiment Index (CBSI) for all industries stood at 103.5 in November, down 0.7 point from the previous month, according to data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The reading marked the first on-month decline since June, when the index dropped 1.2 points. The index measures corporate outlooks on overall business conditions, with a reading above 100 indicating that optimists still outnumber pessimists. The CBSI among manufacturers fell 0.8 point on-month to 104.8 in November from a more than four-year high of 105.6 the previous month. The manufacturing index had remained above the 100 mark for four consecutive months from May through August, after first topping the threshold in May for the first time since August 2022, but fell to 99.5 in September. The index among nonmanufacturers also went down 0.7 point on-month to 102.5. The BOK said rising inventory and global oversupply weighed on manufacturing compani

item.title: Seoul Metro labor, management reach last-minute deal to avoid strike
item.description: Labor and management at Seoul Metro reached a last-minute agreement on wages and working conditions Wednesday, avoiding a planned general strike that could have disrupted the morning commute, according to labor and management representatives. All three labor unions at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, reached agreements with management and called off their planned general strike, which had been scheduled to begin with the first trains of the day. The two sides agreed to cap wage increases at 3.5 percent, while management will put on hold its existing restructuring plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire 500 new employees Union 1, 2 and 3 have 9,100, 2,560 and 2,220 members, respectively. With the government setting a 3.5 percent guideline for increases in total labor costs at public institutions, wages were not a major point of contention between labor and management. The two sides had been far apart on staffing issues. Despite the unions' demands, Seoul Metro had maintained that workforce restructuring is necessary to ensure an appropriate staffing level, cit

item.title: Naver to invest $743 mil. in logistics amid intensifying Coupang rivalry
item.description: Naver plans to invest nearly 1 trillion won ($743.7 million) in logistics infrastructure by 2030 as it moves to strengthen its delivery capabilities and take on Coupang in Korea’s increasingly competitive e-commerce market. The tech giant will be launching a new logistics subsidiary this year, with its Chief Operating Officer Kim Bom-jun tapped to lead the unit as its first CEO. The subsidiary will take the lead in designing logistics systems and infrastructure, while Naver will continue to rely on existing partners to operate warehouses and handle deliveries. The move addresses a longstanding weakness in Naver's e-commerce business — delivery speed and consistency — as the company seeks to strengthen its position following a massive data breach last year at rival Coupang. item.title: Disney's 'Hexed' blends vibrant magic with heartfelt family story
item.description: Walt Disney Animation Studios' 65th animated feature, "Hexed," arrives in Korean theaters Wednesday with vibrant visuals, witty creature design and a tender story at its center, even if its plot follows a familiar formula. Co-directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand and Josie Trinidad, the animated feature introduces Billie Doe (voiced by Hailee Steinfeld), an impulsive 16-year-old navigating the awkwardness of suburban life. Everything changes when a magic-suppressing bracelet accidentally unlocks on her wrist, unleashing dormant powers and opening a portal into Hexe, a sprawling realm inhabited by witches. Pulled into this world alongside her overprotective mother, Alice (Rashida Jones), Billie quickly realizes that Hexe is no carefree wonderland. item.title: Motional's CES self-driving demo crucial to reviving market confidence
item.description: Hyundai Motor needs a convincing autonomous driving breakthrough at CES 2027 to restore investor confidence, as mounting earnings pressure and its lagging position in self-driving technology leave the automaker struggling to justify its ambitious future mobility investments. The upcoming CES tech fair in January will be a critical test for Motional, Hyundai Motor Group’s U.S.-based autonomous driving subsidiary. A compelling demonstration of its self-driving technology could help revive market interest in Hyundai’s long-term technology strategy. But anything short of a clear competitive advantage over established players — such as Tesla or emerging Chinese electric vehicle (EV) makers — risks further eroding investor confidence. The pressure is already evident in Hyundai’s share price. The stock closed Monday at 247,500 won ($184), down approximately 68 percent from its June peak of 783,000 won amid fading investor trust in the carmaker’s earnings growth and delayed self-driving transition. item.title: Korea's 4,500-kilometer coastline walking trail celebrates decade of scenic journeys
item.description: Discovering Korea on foot offers an intimate look at the country that high-speed trains and city itineraries simply cannot match. Stretching roughly 4,500 kilometers across 284 courses — nearly three times the length of Spain’s famed Camino de Santiago — the "Korea Dulle Trail" traces the nation’s entire coastline and northern frontier, turning long-distance walking into one of Korea’s signature travel trends. As the trail marks its 10th anniversary this year, the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) is highlighting the route as a bucket-list slow-travel experience and recently named beloved comedian Hwang Je-seong as its new honorary ambassador to promote the trail. Hwang will officially step into the role during an appointment ceremony at Seoul Marina Club & Yacht in Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, Wednesday. Since launching his career in 2007, Hwang has become a familiar, upbeat presence across Korean television and radio, and an engaging storyteller to introduce long-distance walking holidays. item.title: From local comfort food to global franchise: Chinese malatang king's Korea test
item.description: At around 7 p.m. on a recent Monday, more than half of the dozen or so tables were occupied at a Yangguofu Malatang restaurant in Yeoksam, an office-packed area in Seoul's Gangnam District. Vegetables, fish balls, rice cakes and instant noodles lined a refrigerated self-service topping bar, while pickled radish, peanuts and dipping sauces were available nearby. Two employees juggled cooking, payments, serving and clearing tables in the orange-hued restaurant. Yangguofu Group, one of China's largest malatang chains with nearly 7,000 outlets worldwide, has grown its overseas network from just over 20 in early 2023 to more than 200 across 30 countries and territories, as it steps up its global expansion. Yet the company is a much smaller player in Korea, where malatang — which literally translates to “numbing, spicy, scalding-hot” — found a receptive audience in a country fond of spicy food and hot soups. The dish has become popular enough to be proposed for inclusion in the country’s consumer price index basket. Yangguofu entered the Korean market in 2019 and now has 10 outlets,

item.title: As AI cheating fears soar, does college matter that much in Korea?
item.description: As someone who never took the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), I found myself asking a question last week while covering anxiety over cheating with artificial intelligence (AI) — a concern that rocked Korea. “Is college really that important in Korea?” My answer is yes. Korean society does push people hard to go to college — and not just any college but a good one. When I was a high school senior, I decided to travel around the world instead of going to college. After a year of working as a cleaner in Australia to fund the trip, I spent another year touring 24 countries. Over the course of those two years, one of the most common refrains from fellow Koreans I met on the road was, “You have to go to college.” True to that advice, Koreans go to college at one of the highest rates in the world. According to Ministry of Education data released in September, in 2025 Korea again led Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) member countries in higher education attainment among young adults. item.title: Democrats clinch historic House majority of at least 259 seats, the largest since 1990
item.description: WASHINGTON — House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 259 seats in an election sweep unseen since 1990 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities. Democrats have so far gained 45 House seats from where they started on Election Day, five more than the 40 they picked up in President Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018. The 259-seat tally was reached Tuesday after Democrat Victoria Broderick defeated Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais in Tennessee. Three other House races remain outstanding: one in Minnesota and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff. Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority. The milestone in the 435-member House sets up divided government, with the Senate also in Democratic hands and with a Republican president in the White House. Emboldened Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda to address high costs of living while also confronting Trump with a vast oversight agenda for the remainder of his second term i

item.title: Trump gives the Medal of Freedom to Giuliani, a fierce political ally who led New York through 9/11
item.description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday awarded the Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor, to former New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani. Giuliani was hailed for leading New York after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. Trump has called Giuliani, a fellow New Yorker, the “greatest Mayor in the history of New York City, and an equally great American Patriot.” Giuliani, 82, said in a statement he was honored by the award. “I share the credit with all the men and women who worked with me, disagreed with me, and loved me — particularly those who lost their lives in the causes we undertook together,” he said. The event was closed to the press, but Giuliani's son, Andrew Giuliani, described it afterward as a special honor that was tough to put into words. Rudy Giuliani’s public life has undergone a rise and fall in recent years. item.title: Putin says Ukraine hits Russian oil plants despite Trump's requests, promises retaliation
item.description: MOSCOW — Ukraine continues attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from U.S. President Donald Trump to withhold them, Russian leader Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday, pledging to retaliate. Kyiv has said it would stop striking Russian energy targets only when Moscow did the same and while Ukrainian strikes subsided after Trump's mid-October declaration of energy ceasefire they have picked up again since the end of last month. "We see that the Kyiv regime continues to attack our refining facilities, despite the U.S. president's appeal and direct request to refrain from such attacks. But the Kyiv authorities are ignoring this advice," Putin told a meeting of government officials and senior oil executives in the Kremlin. "In this regard, I would like to stress that retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable," he said. He also told the meeting that he wanted additional security measures for energy facilities. item.title: US consumer confidence jumps to highest level in nearly two years
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. consumer confidence increased more than expected in November, touching its highest level in nearly two years, amid optimism over labor market conditions and the overall economy following this month's midterm elections. The sharp improvement in confidence reported by the Conference Board on Tuesday was driven by respondents identifying as Democrats and Independents. Confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. President Donald Trump's Republican Party lost control of Congress to Democrats in the November 3 elections, which were dominated by anger over the rising cost of living, blamed on tariffs on imports and the US-Israeli war with Iran. The Conference Board survey noted that "while consumers continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs, some comments cited hope for the general economy." Economists viewed the surge in confidence as a good omen for the holiday shopping season, though the correlation between consumer spending and confidence is weak. Consumer spending has recorded two back-to-back quarters of robust growth even as confid

item.title: Nvidia's Huang disclosed more affairs to board before reinstatement: reports
item.description: SEATTLE — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly admitted to additional extramarital affairs during a meeting with the company's board before his reinstatement, according to media reports Monday. Huang disclosed relationships beyond those previously reported during an hours-long meeting Sunday, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The billionaire executive expressed remorse over his conduct, but the exact number of additional affairs and the identities of those involved remain unclear. Huang had previously acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife following reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has faced U.S. scrutiny over possible ties to Chinese intelligence. He was subsequently linked to Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, and another company employee. item.title: Nvidia, Anthropic and other AI stocks get back to tumbling and drag the US market lower
item.description: NEW YORK — Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence industry are dragging the U.S. market lower Tuesday after their surge from the day before quickly fizzled. That's even though much of the rest of Wall Street is rising, along with confidence among Americans in the economy. The S&P 500 fell 0.3 percent and is heading toward its eighth loss in the last nine days. Tech stocks once again led the way lower and dragged the Nasdaq composite down a market-leading 1.3 percent, as of 12:41 p.m. Eastern time. Stocks outside of AI held up much better, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 441 points, or 0.9 percent. They're the latest swings for a market that's been mostly sinking since setting its all-time high last month. The primary worry is that prices for AI-related stocks shot too high into a possible bubble and need to deflate. That carries immense consequences for the broader market and workers’ 401(k) accounts because AI companies have grown into Wall Street’s most influential stocks. item.title: US poised to unveil new tariffs targeting S. Korea, 15 other trading partners
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected. The results of the investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 are expected as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during Trump's second term. The duties would partly replace global import taxes struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The administration's tariffs have in part contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November's midterm elections showed 62 percent of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs. item.title: Jensen Huang is back, but Nvidia still has to deal with his baggage
item.description: NEW YORK — Jensen Huang has returned. The next few weeks could determine whether Nvidia’s decision to reinstate him as CEO was the prudent one that cheering employees, shareholders and President Donald Trump made it out to be — or a big mistake. Huang’s supporters argued that he was indispensable, not only to the company but to the entire artificial intelligence industry, at the moment a major engine of the economy. Trump even suggested Huang's return should be celebrated by the “people of the United States — and, indeed, the World!” But he carries some baggage Nvidia still has to deal with. Huang likely violated the company's code of conduct. He acknowledged having an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. And national security issues aside, Huang’s unusual management style, which included striking deals with a mere handshake, would have doomed many other CEOs. It’s not a given that Huang's second go-round will survive congressional investigations, lawsuits and a probe by a law firm hired by his own board. But investors pushed Nvidia shares up 31.5 perce

item.title: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after historic outage, internal memos show
item.description: Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. The November 12-13 outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents. Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption. The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft's engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. It was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jas

item.title: US reaffirms alliance cooperation after Lee names new foreign, unification ministers, spy chief
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. State Department on Tuesday stressed the importance of close cooperation with South Korea following President Lee Jae Myung's nomination of new officials to lead the country's foreign policy, intelligence and inter-Korean affairs. On Monday, Lee nominated Lim Woong-soon, currently the second deputy national security adviser, as foreign minister; former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS); and former lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister. "The United States values the importance of close cooperation in the U.S.-ROK Alliance," a State Department spokesman said in response to a query from Yonhap News Agency regarding the nominations of new Cabinet members and a new spy chief. ROK stands for the Republic of Korea, South Korea's official name. "We continue to advance U.S. and mutual interests with our ally the ROK," the spokesman said. item.title: Why do restaurants keep reusing leftover side dishes?
item.description: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. Reusing food left behind by customers poses serious hygiene risks and can spread diseases, including influenza and hepatitis. Food that other diners have stirred with their chopsticks may be contaminated with saliva. The risk is easy to understand if you think of the respiratory droplets that became a familiar concern during the COVID-19 pandemic. Restaurants caught doing this can face administrative sanctions, including business suspensions, as well as criminal penalties. Another restaurant has been caught reusing food left behind by customers. A district office in Seoul has begun administrative proceedings against a restaurant found to have violated the Food Sanitation Act. The restaurant reportedly put side dishes left uneaten by customers back into storage containers in the kitchen before serving them to other diners. Under the Food Sanitation Act, food service operators are prohibited from reusing, cooking or storing food left behind by customers. Violations can result in administrative sanctions and criminal penalties. Influenza is curre

item.title: "Huna": Egyptian Author Abdelrahman ElGendy on Prison, National Book Award & Being Denied U.S. Visa
item.description:
This year’s annual National Book Awards ceremony in New York City was marked by the notable absence of nonfiction winner Abdelrahman ElGendy, after the Trump administration denied the Egyptian author entry into the United States. ElGendy’s debut, Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming, chronicles his arrest and over six years of imprisonment, alongside his father, following arrest at a protest against the military dictatorship of Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. After his release from prison in Egypt, ElGendy obtained an MFA in the United States but was forced to flee once again — this time from the U.S. to Europe — for fear of being targeted by immigration authorities over his criticism of Israel’s war on Gaza and U.S.-Egypt relations.

“It was a gutting thing to not be able to attend the ceremony. But it was also unsurprising,” ElGendy tells Democracy Now! about being barred from receiving the National Book Award in person. “[I] have labored for so long my whole life to get to this point, only to again and again and again be forced to witness it all from afar and detached from the people I love.”

We speak to ElGendy about the weaponization of the visa process, in both the U.S. and Egypt, “as a form of transnational repression,” his arrest and imprisonment beginning at the age of just 17, and the Egyptian government’s ongoing repression of free speech, including its attempted closure of the independent news outlet Mada Masr, whose lawyers were in court today appealing its shutdown.

“Mada carries so much of the archive of our revolutionary history … so to erase it is to erase an archive,” says ElGendy, whose early writings were smuggled out of prison and first published in Mada Masr. “The current Egyptian military dictatorship [is] a frantic project of erasure of everything that has to do with the revolution, and it’s an insistence on erasing every trace that would allow people to remember that revolution has happened, that this rupture has happened before.”

item.title: "Disaster Waiting to Happen": Iowa Declares Emergency as U.S. Army Detonates 5 Tons of Lead Azide
item.description: The U.S. Army detonated nearly five tons of highly unstable lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa on Wednesday, potentially sending toxic lead dust and other deadly contaminants spewing across communities and farmland throughout the Mississippi River water basin. Residents, who were first informed last week, had been ordered to evacuate or else shelter in place. “The Army has decided to act as it wishes, and it is going against the recommendations of its own experts,” says Pat Elder, who tracks how military activity impacts people and the planet at the Military Poisons project. “There is no reason for this to be done, and it is a disaster waiting to happen.”

item.title: Philippine Forces Train to Secure Luzon Strait with Warships, BrahMos Missiles
item.description: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine forces are practicing how to secure the Luzon Strait through the deployment of warships and a BrahMos missile battery for maritime strike operations this month. The drills are being conducted during an annual territorial defense exercise, which runs through Friday. The exercise is meant to reinforce Manila’s approach to deter a potential Taiwan Contingency Operation spillover to its northern islands. In 2025, former Philippine military chief Romero Brawner Jr. told troops stationed near Taiwan to prepare for a conflict. item.description: A coroner’s jury has determined Kaylee Martha Dallas Crowchild died by suicide in 2022 following transfer to a hospital from the Kenora District Jail in northwestern Ontario, some 1,500 kilometres from her home community of Tsuut’ina Nation in southern Alberta. Following testimony by more than a dozen witnesses, jurors made 21 recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths, with a focus on improving suicide screening and prevention, and Indigenous cultural supports at the jail.

item.title: Kookmin University earns recognition for managing Global Korea Scholarship program
item.description: Kookmin University has been named an “outstanding university” in a government evaluation of institutions hosting Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) recipients, the university said. The results, announced on Wednesday, were based on an evaluation of how 91 universities across Korea manage and support GKS students. Ten universities, including Kookmin, Korea University and Sogang University, were recognized for their outstanding performance. The GKS is a government scholarship program designed to attract talented international students to Korea and support them in pursuing degrees at Korean universities. item.title: Korea's crude oil supply remains stable: industry ministry
item.description: Korea's crude oil supply remains stable despite the ongoing standoff in the Middle East, the industry ministry said Tuesday. The country has secured crude oil for January that's equivalent to over 75 percent of last year's level, up from more than 50 percent a week earlier, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. The crude oil supply for the November-December period stood at the 90 percent level compared with last year's level, and the naphtha supply for the two-month period reached 100 percent, it added. Last week, the country kept its price caps on fuel products unchanged for the fifth consecutive period amid elevated international oil prices and continued geopolitical tensions.

item.title: IU to become 1st Korean female soloist to headline Tokyo Dome
item.description: Singer-actor IU is set to become the first Korean female soloist to hold a standalone concert at Tokyo Dome in Japan as part of her 2027 world tour, her agency announced Monday. EDAM Entertainment unveiled the first batch of tour dates through IU’s official social media accounts, outlining 19 concerts in 10 cities across Asia and Australia from January to May. IU will perform at Tokyo Dome on April 7 and 8. With a capacity of up to 55,000, the venue has long been regarded as a major milestone for K-pop artists seeking to establish themselves in the Japanese music market. The upcoming tour will kick off with two concerts at Rajamangala National Stadium in Bangkok on Jan. 16 and 17, followed by stops in Bulacan in the Philippines, Kaohsiung in Taiwan and Sydney in February. The singer will then head to Singapore and Kuala Lumpur in March, followed by Tokyo, Taipei and Hong Kong in April. The last of the announced shows will take place at Jakarta International Stadium on May 8 and 9. More dates are expected to follow.
