item.title: Botched alerts over Russian aircraft near Ulleung Island spark confusion
item.description: A series of contradictory emergency alerts sent to Ulleung Island residents Tuesday morning raised questions about South Korea’s disaster messaging system after Russian military aircraft approached the island through the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). According to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), several Russian military aircraft entered the KADIZ over the East Sea early Tuesday and approached Ulleung Island before leaving the zone. The Air Force deployed F-15K fighters in response and the Russian aircraft withdrew eastward. The JCS stressed that no violation of South Korea’s sovereign airspace occurred. The KADIZ is a buffer zone established to detect and respond to approaching foreign military aircraft early and is distinct from sovereign airspace. However, the emergency messages that reached residents told a different story and contradicted each other. item.title: More than half of people in 30s remain unmarried in 2025
item.description: More than half of people in their 30s remained unmarried last year amid a trend toward later marriage, census data showed Tuesday. A total of 24.36 million people reported having spouses, accounting for 54.7 percent of the country's total population of 44.57 million aged 15 or older last year, according to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The number of people without spouses totaled 13.88 million, or 31.3 percent, little changed from five years earlier. The data is based on a sample survey conducted as part of the 2025 census. However, the proportion of people without spouses in their 30s rose to 53.1 percent last year from 42.5 percent in 2020. The figure stood at 13.4 percent in the 2000 census. Unmarried men in their 30s accounted for 61.1 percent of the total, while the corresponding figure for women was 44.3 percent in 2025. The ministry said the trend toward delayed marriage continues, while a growing number of people consider marriage unnecessary. item.title: Salaried jobs rise at sharpest clip in 4 years in Q2
item.description: The number of salaried job positions in South Korea rose at the fastest pace in four years in the second quarter of this year, driven by gains in the health and food service sectors, government data showed Tuesday. The number of paid jobs stood at 21.36 million as of May, up 406,000 from a year earlier, the Ministry of Data and Statistics said. It marked the sharpest on-year increase among second-quarter figures since 2022, when the number of paid jobs shot up by 628,000. Wage jobs refer to positions held by employees and are different from the ministry's monthly employment statistics, which count all employed people. For example, when a person works for a company on weekdays and takes a part-time job at a private academy on weekends, he or she is counted as one employed person, while two paid jobs are recorded. By sector, jobs in health and social welfare rose by 161,000, marking the largest second-quarter increase since 2021. Those in accommodation and food services increased by 67,000, the sharpest since 2017, when the ministry began compiling such data. In contrast, manufacturing wage j

item.title: Samsung promotes 131 executives, rewards semiconductor talent in reshuffle
item.description: Samsung Electronics on Tuesday announced its annual executive reshuffle, mostly promoting officials who helped drive record earnings in its lucrative semiconductor business. A total of 131 executives were promoted, down about 20 percent from a year earlier, the tech giant said in a press release. The reshuffle reaffirmed the company's performance-based personnel policy of rewarding those who deliver results, with key talent in the semiconductor business that drove record earnings receiving recognition. Of this year's promotees, more than half came from the device solutions division, which oversees the semiconductor business. The promotions rewarded executives who led the development and expanded production of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips. In contrast, the number of promotions in the device experience division, which oversees its consumer electronics and mobile device businesses, declined from last year. The division posted consecutive quarterly operating losses in the second and third quarters amid rising component costs.

item.title: 8 Sungkyunkwan faculty members named among world's top 1% most-cited researchers
item.description: Eight faculty members from Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) have been named to the Highly Cited Researchers (HCR) 2026 list, underscoring the university’s strong global research capabilities. Compiled by global information and analytics firm Clarivate, the list recognizes researchers whose papers rank among the world’s top 1 percent most-cited publications in their respective fields. The recognition is widely regarded as a key global indicator of research quality and impact. This year, 6,802 researchers from more than 1,280 institutions in over 60 countries and regions were named to the list. In Korea, Seoul National University topped the list with 16 researchers, followed by Sungkyunkwan University and the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology with eight each, Hanyang University with six, the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology with five, Yonsei University with four and Korea University with three. item.title: 54% of bond experts eye rate hike this week: poll
item.description: More than half of bond experts in South Korea are expecting the central bank to raise its key interest rate this week, a poll showed Tuesday. According to the survey of 100 bond market managers by the Korea Financial Investment Association, 54 percent of the respondents forecast the Bank of Korea (BOK) to mark up its policy rate at a rate-setting meeting slated for Thursday. The remaining 46 experts expected the BOK to freeze the key rate, the latest survey showed. Last month, the BOK kept the benchmark rate unchanged after two consecutive rate hikes. South Korea's economy grew faster than expected by 1 percent in the third quarter from a quarter earlier, putting annual growth of 3.6 percent within reach. The survey also showed its bond market survey index (BMSI) stood at 78.7 points for December, down 20.4 points from a month earlier. A BMSI reading below 100 means more experts expect bond market conditions to worsen going forward.

item.title: After SpaceX's volatile debut, ETF managers take more cautious approach toward Anthropic
item.description: Months after SpaceX’s volatile Nasdaq debut inflicted steep losses on several Korean exchange-traded funds (ETFs), fund managers are taking a more measured approach to Anthropic, which also saw its shares swing in their first days of trading, according to industry officials Monday. The artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot set a new record for the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history when it raised $81.3 billion during its Nov. 19 Nasdaq debut, surpassing that of SpaceX. Its shares closed at $97.17 on the first day, 17.1 percent above the $83 offering price. But the stock retreated the following day, falling as low as $83.05 before closing at $88.91. The sharp swings have put the spotlight on a key decision for domestic ETF managers to gauge the fund’s early performance: when to buy into the newly listed stock and how much of their portfolios to allocate to it. item.title: Female duo forges compelling new dynamic in 'Good Partner' Season 2
item.description: When SBS’ "Good Partner" first aired in 2024, few expected a divorce-themed legal drama to become a nationwide phenomenon, peaking at nearly 20 percent in viewership ratings. Now, with the arrival of "Good Partner" Season 2, which premiered Friday and is also streaming on Netflix, critics and viewers alike are praising the drama for proving that its initial success was no fluke, as its second episode has already surged to nearly 10 percent. At the center of the action is Rebom, the premier divorce law firm founded by veteran attorney Cha Eun-kyung (Jang Na-ra). Rather than simply recycling the winning formula of the original, Season 2 expands its narrative scope right out of the gate. Written once again by real-life divorce attorney Choi Yu-na, the series translates actual courtroom cases into gripping, dopamine-fueled television, elevated this time around by fresh generational dynamics, new rivals and deeper personal stakes. item.title: Jeonbuk National University ranks 12th in Korea in QS sustainability rankings
item.description: Jeonbuk National University (JBNU) ranked 12th among Korean universities in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027, released by U.K.-based higher education analytics firm Quacquarelli Symonds (QS). JBNU climbed 21 places to tie for 419th globally, up from a tie for 440th last year. The university attributed the achievement to its continued efforts to integrate environmental, social and corporate governance (ESG) principles into its operations and advance its sustainable development strategy. “We believe this achievement reflects international recognition of our ESG management, commitment to regional development and world-class research capabilities,” JBNU President Yang O-bong said. “We will push ahead with our key initiatives to break into the world's top 300 and develop into a flagship university leading the way toward a sustainable future for humanity and local communities,” he added. item.title: Korea to raise ban for AI cheaters on licensing exams to 10 years, prison term to 5 years
item.description: The government plans to extend the ban on retesting people caught cheating on national technical qualification exams from three years to 10 years and to raise the maximum prison sentence to five years, more than double the current limit, as fears of cheating with artificial intelligence (AI) mount across Korea’s testing system. The Ministry of Employment and Labor announced the measures Tuesday, amid growing suspicions over unusually high scores on national licensing exams and concerns about increasingly sophisticated cheating methods involving smart glasses, miniature cameras and modified calculators. To restore public trust in exam results, the ministry will also make the scores of the top two candidates public, along with average scores and score distributions by subject. The move comes amid growing concerns that traditional exam supervision, which relies heavily on visual checks by proctors, can no longer keep pace with increasingly sophisticated cheating methods. item.title: Paradise showcases Korean cuisine at La Liste 2027
item.description: Paradise participated as an official partner in La Liste Paris 2027 on Monday (local time), showcasing eight contemporary interpretations of traditional Korean dishes at a dedicated pavilion at the French foreign ministry. La Liste, a French-originated global restaurant guide, annually selects the world's top 1,000 restaurants based on evaluations from restaurant guides, media outlets and online reviews. Its annual Paris gathering brings together internationally recognized chefs and gastronomy professionals to celebrate the latest rankings. At a pre-ceremony cocktail reception, Paradise presented its pavilion under the theme "Jang to Table," highlighting the culinary versatility of traditional Korean fermented sauces such as "ganjang," or soy sauce, "doenjang," or soybean paste, and "gochujang," or red chili paste. The project was led by Kang Min-goo, head consultant of Paradise's Culinary Lab and chef-owner of Mingles, the highest-ranked Korean restaurant in La Liste's selection. item.title: Justice minister nominee vows to complete criminal justice system reform
item.description: Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol pledged Tuesday to complete reforms of the criminal justice system following the recent sweeping overhaul of the prosecution service. Lee made the remarks during his parliamentary confirmation hearing after the country launched a newly scaled-down prosecution service last month, stripping prosecutors of their investigative powers. "By making sure the new criminal justice system is stably established, I will do my best to make sure there are no gaps in the protection of the public," he said. Lee added he would ensure that prosecutors focus on fairly exercising their indictment powers and protecting human rights so that there are no shortcomings in the crime response. Last month's reform took place amid criticism that some prosecutors abused their investigative powers and pursued politically motivated investigations. During the hearing, the nominee avoided offering a direct response to questions about whether he planned to instruct prosecutors to drop indictments against President Lee Jae Myung. item.title: ASEAN+3 nations to discuss regional financial cooperation
item.description: Vice finance ministers and deputy central bankers of Korea, China, Japan and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) will gather to discuss ways to strengthen regional financial cooperation, Seoul said Tuesday. The ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies' Meeting will be held in Kyoto, Japan, on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Ministry of Economy and Finance. During the gathering, participants will assess regional economic trends and policy responses, and how to further develop the Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralization (CMIM), a $240 billion currency-swap arrangement established in 2010 as a regional financial safety net. ASEAN comprises Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

item.title: Africa's 1st 'comfort women' statue to be unveiled in South Africa
item.description: A statue of a girl symbolizing the victims of Japan's wartime sexual slavery, euphemistically referred to as "comfort women," will be erected in Africa for the first time, a local activist group said Tuesday. The statue, known as a Statue of Peace, will be unveiled in a ceremony in Cape Town at 4 p.m. on Dec. 1 (local time), according to the Korean Council for Justice and Remembrance for the Issues of Military Sexual Slavery. The statue symbolizes an estimated 200,000 Asian women, mostly Koreans, who were forcibly sent to front-line brothels to serve Japanese troops during World War II. The first Statue of Peace was installed in front of the Japanese Embassy in Seoul on Dec. 14, 2011, to commemorate the 1,000th weekly Wednesday rally by former comfort women and their supporters. With the latest addition, the number of such statues overseas, including those in the United States, Germany, Canada and Australia, will rise to 17. item.title: Lee calls for measures against illegal acts disguised as religious activity
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung instructed the government Tuesday to come up with effective ways to root out illegal acts disguised as religious activity, apparently referring to controversy over a religious sect's alleged collusion with members of the ruling party. Lee gave the instruction during a Cabinet meeting at Cheong Wa Dae without elaborating on the illegal acts. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea has been mired in internal strife after leader Kim Min-seok recently withdrew his accusations that followers of the Shincheonji Church of Jesus, a nonmainstream religious sect, had attempted to sway the party's leadership race in August in favor of his then rival. "I spoke to you a long time ago about the dissolution process for religious cults engaging in crimes or illegal acts disguised as religious activity," the president said. "I think it is time to realistically consider effective measures against this." item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed cloud company linked to Nvidia scandal
item.description: WASHINGTON — The US Commerce Department on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed, the cloud company at the center of the Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist, following criticism from lawmakers and administration officials. Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the US Commerce Department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied. "The Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Commerce why this took so long," Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said in a posting on X. Megaspeed gained the spotlight about two weeks ago after news broke that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy. China has said the spy accusations are "groundless." After the news broke, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly complained that the Commerce Department had not yet placed the company on its Entity List. He also called out Nvidia. item.title: Seoul stocks up nearly 7% Tuesday morning on Huang's return
item.description: South Korean stocks surged nearly 7 percent late Tuesday morning, surpassing the psychologically important 5,000-point mark, as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia. After opening 3.64 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its gains to rise 315.04 points, or 6.69 percent, to 5,023.58 as of 11:20 a.m. As the rally gathered momentum, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. The measure is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise at least 5 percent and remain at that level for one minute or longer. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3.01 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite surged 6.51 percent. Nvidia's board has decided to reinstate Huang, while U.S. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying Huang poses no national security risk. In Seoul, large-cap stocks advanced across the board, with chip shares leading the gain. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics j

item.title: S. Korea briefly issues alert on eastern island after Russian airplanes enter air defense zone
item.description: Several Russian warplanes briefly flew into South Korea's air defense zone over the East Sea before exiting early Tuesday, prompting Seoul to issue an alert on an island and scramble its fighter jets in response, the military said. The South's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) clarified that the Russian planes had not violated South Korea's airspace as previously announced by the interior ministry in a mobile emergency alert. It also corrected an earlier alert issued by a provincial government that erroneously identified the planes as suspected North Korean aircraft. The Russian warplanes entered the air defense identification zone (KADIZ) early in the morning, approaching Ulleung Island before exiting the zone, the JCS said. "We detected the movement before the Russian aircraft's entry into KADIZ and deployed fighter jets to conduct tactical maneuvers in case of contingencies," it said. The defense ministry plans to call in a Russian diplomat from the Russian Embassy in Seoul later in the day to lodge a formal complaint, ministry spokesperson Chung Binna said in a press briefing. item.title: KRX activates buy-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp rise
item.description: South Korea's bourse operator on Tuesday activated a buy-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index rose sharply. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes from 9:06 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 3.64 percent higher, the KOSPI added 263.75 points, or 5.6 percent, to 4,974.62 as of 9:08 a.m. The index rallied as Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia leadership rekindled optimism over the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index rises 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

item.title: N. Korea threatens to close Swiss office in Pyongyang over sanctions on children's camp
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday denounced Switzerland's sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp, which has been accused of involvement in the forced deportation of Ukrainian children, and threatened to close the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang. Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong-un, made the denouncement, as Switzerland imposed sanctions on the camp last week after Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis visited North Korea to open Switzerland's first diplomatic office in Pyongyang in late October. In a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim called the sanctions an "open hostile act" against North Korea and a "serious infringement" upon the sovereignty of North Korea. "I strongly condemn the Swiss authority for its surprisingly mean behavior of committing such ridiculous act just a few days after its delegation voluntarily visited Pyongyang to discuss the development of the relations with our state and committed to dialogue and cooperation," Kim said. "This is an unfaithful and hostile signal. Needless to say, it is a shabby step." The

item.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship in Libya as conflict spreads beyond Europe
item.description: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Libya's eastern-based government said the corvette, the Merkury, had been docked at the Benghazi naval base. Zelenskyy published videos on Monday from Ukraine's SBU security service that he said showed the attack, and another drone off Libya hitting the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Moscow had used to transport weapons. item.title: Consumer sentiment falls for 2nd month in Nov. on stock market correction, high loan rates
item.description: Consumer sentiment fell for the second consecutive month in November due mainly to a stock market correction and higher interest rates, the central bank said Tuesday. The composite consumer sentiment index (CCSI) stood at 103.1 this month, down 2.3 points from October, according to a survey by the Bank of Korea (BOK). A reading above 100 indicates that optimists outnumber pessimists, while a figure below 100 suggests the opposite. "Pessimistic outlooks increased as the stock market correction and rising lending rates weighed heavily on consumer sentiment," the BOK said. The subindex for people's assessment of current economic conditions came in at 78 in November, down 4 points from a month earlier. The index for people's outlook for future economic conditions also fell 2 points to 86 over the same period. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) dropped 15 percent in the first three weeks of November on escalating concerns about profitability of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investment after the U.S. midterm elections. item.title: US takes action to recover over $1.1 bil. in cryptocurrency stolen by N. Korean hackers
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Justice Department said Monday it has filed a civil forfeiture action to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency allegedly stolen by North Korean hackers from Binance last month. The forfeiture action targets more than $1.1 billion in USDC, a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, which authorities identified as proceeds and laundered funds from the Binance hack, the department said in a press release. The move is part of broader U.S. government efforts to help Binance recover more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in a cyberattack around Oct. 29, it said. The department said the United States has so far assisted in freezing, seizing or returning more than $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency from multiple sources in the Binance case. "This forfeiture action is the latest example of our efforts to combat the North Korean government's attempts to profit from the injustices it repeatedly inflicts upon innocent victims," said M. item.title: Jin Air's Busan hub plan faces profitability test
item.description: Jin Air’s plan to develop Gimhae International Airport as its second hub after Incheon International Airport faces a profitability test, as the airline prepares to expand international routes and flight frequencies — primarily to Japan — from Busan next year. The integrated Jin Air plans to increase the number of international routes from Gimhae to 33 from the current 28 and raise weekly flights to 339 from 281, according to the low-cost carrier (LCC). The planned expansion in Busan comes in response to growing local industry concerns ahead of the upcoming launch of the converged Jin Air. Air Busan, whose headquarters is currently located in Busan, will be merged into Jin Air from March 17, and the merged entity’s head office will be based in Seoul. However, it remains unclear whether the increase in routes and capacity will translate into meaningful improvements in profitability for Jin Air. Most of the additional routes are expected to be short-haul destinations, particularly in Japan. Such routes can help increase passenger volumes and aircraft utilization, but they also face

item.title: AI cheating puts Korea's decades-old exam system under scrutiny
item.description: Korea’s decades-old testing system, especially the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), is facing growing scrutiny amid fears of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered cheating. However, even as calls for reform grow, proposed changes face practical hurdles and offer no guarantee of preventing increasingly sophisticated AI-driven cheating. President Lee Jae Myung's call on Friday for a swift overhaul of the national testing system accelerated efforts to move beyond multiple-choice exams and introduce written response and essay-based questions to Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. In August, the National Education Commission presented Lee with a plan to consider introducing absolute grading and written response and essay-based questions to the CSAT. The commission has since sought public input, including through discussions with its citizen participation committee. However, experts warn that changing the exam format alone would do little to stop AI-assisted cheating. "Generative AI can not only select the correct answer from multiple choices but also explain how it arrived at a

item.title: Oil falls around 3% on increased Middle East flows, Libyan pipeline restart
item.description: HOUSTON — Oil prices shed nearly 3 percent on Monday as traders weighed a rise in supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline, offsetting some unease around shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures fell $2.62, or 2.83 percent, to $89.95 a barrel by 1:49 p.m. EDT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were down $2.68, or 3.21 percent, at $80.73 a barrel. Earlier in the session, Brent hit a session low of $88.60 a barrel, its lowest since August 27, while WTI fell to a low of $79.95, its lowest since August 26. U.S. crude oil and product inventories are expected to have risen by about 900,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, a preliminary Reuters poll of five analysts showed on Monday. item.title: 'A handshake with Jensen': why tech fought to save Nvidia's founder
item.description: WASHINGTON — From Steve Jobs to Elon Musk, Silicon Valley has long rallied behind outsized founders seen as inseparable from the companies they built — and in Jensen Huang, the tech world found its latest figure to defend at all costs. The idea is central to the industry's mythology, often distilled as "founder mode" — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than ceding control to executives. The spy scandal that pushed Huang out of Nvidia was treated by a powerful slice of the industry as a threat to that ethos and something to be fought rather than a verdict to be accepted. The campaign to bring him back began within hours of his November 12 resignation, led by investors and executives with deep stakes in the AI boom, several of them with close ties to President Donald Trump. It succeeded on Monday, when Nvidia's board reinstated Huang 11 days after accepting his resignation and six days after its chair told investors the company did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." item.title: NATO to send early-warning system aircraft to Poland after missiles incident
item.description: WARSAW — NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning system aircraft to Poland as part of its response to three missiles landing in the country on the military alliance's eastern flank, a Polish deputy defence minister said on Monday. Three Russian Kh-101 missiles landed in Poland on Friday, prosecutors said, adding to fears that Russia's war in Ukraine could spill into NATO territory. "An AWACS early-warning aircraft will be made available to Poland," Pawel Zalewski told reporters after a NATO meeting in Brussels. "This is a very good system that gives us even deeper... operational awareness which allows us to respond better to this kind of threat." With their distinctive nine-metre-wide radar domes, NATO's 14 Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft have served as the alliance's eyes in the sky since 1982. Based at Geilenkirchen air base in Germany, the fleet has played an important role in surveillance missions along NATO's eastern flank since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. item.title: 1 election official arrested in alleged vote count manipulation case
item.description: A Seoul court on Tuesday issued an arrest warrant for a regional election official accused of concealing and forging a vote count sheet during the June 3 local elections. The Seoul Central District Court issued the warrant for the official, surnamed Lee, citing concerns that the suspect could destroy evidence. Lee was among eight officials -- three from the National Election Commission and five from regional election commissions -- accused of manipulating voter turnout figures or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. item.title: PM Han discusses ways to strengthen energy cooperation with Qatari minister
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook held a meeting with Qatari Minister of State for Energy Affairs Saad bin Sherida Al Kaabi on Monday to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation in renewable energy. item.title: Nvidia bears face $12.2 billion hit on Huang's surprise return
item.description: Nvidia short sellers were staring at about $12.2 billion in paper losses on Monday, their biggest one-day hit since at least 2019, according to ORTEX, after the chipmaker's shares soared on Jensen Huang's surprise return as CEO. The losses, calculated at a share price of $168.50, would erase more than $10.5 billion in paper gains from last week. Short sellers, however, remain up about $14 billion since October 29, ORTEX said. The chip giant shares were last up 33 percent at $167.14 after Huang was reinstated less than two weeks after resigning over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump had called for his return. Short sellers "are still well ahead since late October, so this hurts but it hasn't undone the trade," said Peter Hillerberg, co-Founder of ORTEX. "Some will be covering, but with only just over 1 percent of the float short, this looks like a reaction to the news rather than a squeeze."

item.title: Trump says he assured Nvidia that Huang posed no national security threat
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he reassured the Nvidia board that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO would not pose a risk to U.S. national security. Trump said he had been in touch with the board since Huang stepped down November 12 following revelations about his extramarital affairs with subordinates and with Chinese national Alice Huang, a suspected spy of no relation. Trump, who counts Huang as among his closest friends in Silicon Valley, had pushed for his reinstatement despite the revelations in an extraordinarily public intervention by a U.S. president into a company's decision-making. "The board decided to do what we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know is there a national security problem?" Trump said in an interview with CNBC after the board's decision to reinstate Huang as CEO was announced. "And after a lot of research... we said, 'No, it's not a problem.'" item.title: Fresh reports indicate Russia may deploy a nuclear weapon in space
item.description: Russia could launch a nuclear weapon into space via satellite before the end of this year, according to fresh media reports from Monday, which echoed stories that surfaced last year. The German government said it is taking the reports "very seriously." However, there is currently no "immediate threat," government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said in Berlin on Monday. He recalled that on November 3, the National Security Council had addressed a "changed security situation in space." The details of that meeting are classified, however. There is no reason "to spread undue anxiety here and now over hypothetical questions," Kornelius emphasized. Earlier, German public broadcasters WDR and NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung broadsheet had reported on Moscow's alleged plans, citing Western intelligence agencies and military sources, including the Bundeswehr and the German Federal Intelligence Service (BND). item.title: Seoul to offer up to $370,000 for reporting college entrance exam cheating
item.description: South Korea will offer rewards of up to 500 million won ($370,888) for reporting cheating on the annual college entrance exam, the anti-corruption agency said Monday, as authorities step up efforts to crack down on cheating aided by artificial intelligence (AI). The government will offer 100 million won for each tip-off that leads to the detection of a cheating case, up to a maximum of 500 million won, according to the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC). Those who confess to cheating and report accomplices will also receive the full reward, while facing reduced penalties for their own misconduct, the commission said. "The measure is aimed at safeguarding the fairness and credibility of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by encouraging the public to report cheating," it said. The commission is accepting reports of cheating through Jan. 19 as part of a two-month campaign. SK hynix's American depositary receipts (ADRs), traded on the Nasdaq, jumped 20 percent, or $20.71, to finish at $124.28, according to market data. item.title: Wall Street roars back as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia as CEO
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes rallied sharply on Monday, led by a nearly 7 percent jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2 percent, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump's call for Huang's return. Huang resigned as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. "Huang’s return marks one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive," said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. Huang resigned as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. "Huang’s return marks one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive," said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. "Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw." The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion in m
item.author: reuters@koreatimes.co.kr (KoreaTimes)

item.title: US lawmakers criticize Nvidia decision to reinstate Huang as CEO
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. lawmakers from both parties sharply criticized Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, saying Congress should tighten restrictions on China's access to the company's advanced AI chips and scrutinize the circumstances surrounding Huang's return. Democratic U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, who is set to chair the Banking Committee starting in January, called the decision to reinstate Huang "reckless," adding Nvidia's board still owes Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls. The Banking Committee is responsible for approving legislation on export controls. "Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," Warren said. Huang will testify on December 3 before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee in a public hearing, the panel's Republican Chair Tim Scott said Monday, as lawmakers probe allegations about Huang's ties to a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

item.title: AI-generated song's chart success draws mixed reactions
item.description: There may be no real person behind the voice singing the song, but the music itself remains. A song created using artificial intelligence (AI) has reached the top of Korea's largest music streaming platform. As AI-generated music wins over listeners and climbs to No. 1 on the charts, it is once again drawing attention to broader debates about the future of the music industry. “The Adult I Dreamed Of” by MEOMURU reached No. 1 on Melon's Top 100 chart on the afternoon of Nov. 13. It was the first AI-generated track to top the chart and maintained its position for more than a week, as of the afternoon of Nov. 20. Released in June, the song began gaining traction on music charts after spreading through social media as background music for short-form videos. Its success attracted even greater attention because it topped a chart featuring other recent hits, including A2O LITE's “Neon,” RESCENE's “With” and ILLIT's “You're Under Arrest.” MEOMURU is an AI music project created by Glorywave, a production team consisting of composers and producers Lee Yong-seok, also known as Mart

item.title: Traditional Korean paper gains recognition as tool for preserving world heritage
item.description: Hanji, the traditional Korean paper, is gaining attention as researchers document its potential for restoring some of the world's most treasured cultural artifacts. The National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage said Tuesday it had published a reference book titled “Our Paper, Hanji: A Reference Guide to Lightweight Hanji,” documenting the physical properties and characteristics of hanji used in cultural heritage conservation and restoration. The publication defines lightweight hanji as paper weighing less than 15 grams per square meter and includes samples produced by six artisans recognized as holders of national or provincial intangible cultural heritage. The book combines actual paper samples with scientific assessments, allowing researchers and restoration specialists to compare how production techniques and working conditions influence the material's characteristics. Hanji has long served as a material for preserving and restoring cultural heritage, with its qualities shaped by generations of papermaking expertise and craftsmanship. item.title: PM vows to thoroughly investigate suspected cheating in past state-run exams
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Tuesday the government will look thoroughly into suspected cheating cases in past state-run exams and take every possible measure against offenders. Han made the remark at the start of a meeting of the government's task force on ensuring exam fairness, instructing ministries in charge of respective exams to look into whether cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) and other high-tech means had occurred in past exams. "We should closely examine problems raised in the press, reports of suspected cheating and unusual score patterns, and take all possible measures, including stripping licenses and criminal punishment, if cheating is actually confirmed," Han said. Exam cheating has been one of the hottest topics in Korea in recent weeks, following the confession earlier this month by the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam that he cheated with the help of AI and that he also used the same method on a certified public accountant exam. The revelations sparked massive concerns that AI-assisted cheating could be more widespread than previ

item.title: [FORUM] Trust built on transparency, predictability key to achieving 'Korea premium'
item.description: Korea's capital market needs more transparency, predictability and access to gain more trust from foreign investors and attract them, in a broader goal to narrow the longstanding discount on Korean stocks and build a “Korea premium,” experts said. Domestic and overseas financial experts, investors and business leaders discussed tasks to achieve that goal at the 2026 Korea Times Forum Tuesday. Under the theme “Capital market advancement: Giant leap toward era of Korea premium,” the forum examined measures to curb unfair trading, delist struggling companies and expand English-language disclosures. It also explored how companies can increase shareholder value by raising dividends, canceling treasury shares and strengthening the role of their boards. In a rare joint appearance, the forum brought together the chairs of all five major Korean financial groups — KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori and NH NongHyup. item.title: Musinsa wins Shanghai regional headquarters status, expands China ambitions
item.description: Korean fashion platform Musinsa has secured official recognition as a multinational corporation regional headquarters in Shanghai, gaining access to expanded government support as it deepens its investment in China and seeks to bring more domestic fashion brands to the market. Musinsa China received the certification at a Nov. 18 ceremony hosted by the Shanghai municipal government, the company said Tuesday. The designation recognizes Musinsa's continued investment and business expansion in China, where it has been building retail infrastructure and distribution channels to help Korean fashion labels reach local consumers. Shanghai's regional headquarters certification program is designed to attract international investment and improve the business environment for foreign companies, with recipients selected through an assessment of their business scale and operational capabilities. Under the designation, Musinsa China will be eligible for policy support in areas including financial management, import and export customs procedures, talent recruitment and intellectual property protection. item.title: KT, Army Training and Doctrine Command partner on next-gen battlefield system
item.description: KT has signed an agreement with the Army Training and Doctrine Command to jointly develop the military branch's next-generation combat operations system, the telecom operator said Tuesday. The memorandum of understanding was signed at KT's Gwanghwamun Building West in central Seoul. Senior officials from both sides attended. The system, known as KCCS-Army, is designed around the Army's operating environment and mission needs. Command and control systems link commanders with units in the field so they can share battlefield information and direct operations. Under the agreement, KT will share and advise on advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and 5G. The two sides will jointly identify research and development tasks, including combat experiments. KT will also help identify key technologies and new weapons systems for the future Army. Both sides will look for ways to apply private-sector technology in the Army's operating environment. item.title: 1,000 graduating design students to showcase works at DDP
item.description: About 1,000 graduating design students from across the country will showcase their senior projects to industry leaders and working designers at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) in central Seoul next week. The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Design Foundation, which runs the plaza, will hold the 2026 DDP Next Design exhibition from Dec. 1-5. The show brings together 1,000 graduation works from 64 departments at 50 universities, a larger lineup than last year's. The foundation said the event pairs graduation exhibitions with presentations to companies and career mentoring. It is part of the city's strategy to nurture young designers. On Dec. 3, 10 students chosen through a screening will present their work and vision to design company leaders at a "design busking" session. Under the theme "Whose tomorrow does my design change?" they will explain the problem they found and how they tried to solve it through design. item.title: City libraries open warm winter spaces to encourage household energy savings
item.description: Seoul is inviting residents to turn down their home heating and head to nearby libraries this winter, pairing an energy-saving campaign with hundreds of reading and cultural programs across the city. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that 214 libraries, including Seoul Metropolitan Library, will participate in its Off & Library campaign from Dec. 1 through Feb. 28, 2027. The initiative, titled Libraries Are Hot, encourages residents to switch off their heating temporarily and spend time reading or enjoying cultural activities in warm public spaces, reducing household energy consumption during the coldest months. Now in its fourth year, Seoul Metropolitan Library's seasonal climate campaign has featured separate summer and winter editions, promoting libraries as places to escape extreme temperatures while encouraging everyday energy conservation. item.title: Bae Yong-joon, Park Soo-jin return to Korea after four years in Hawaii
item.description: Actor Bae Yong-joon, one of the original stars of the Korean wave, and his wife, actor Park Soo-jin, have reportedly returned to Korea with their two children after spending approximately four years in Hawaii. Local media outlet OSEN reported Tuesday that the celebrity couple returned to Korea earlier this year and have since settled in Seoul. Bae and Park, who have largely stepped away from the entertainment industry, married in 2015 and have a son and a daughter. The family reportedly moved to Hawaii in 2022. According to the report, the couple decided to return to Korea after discussing the matter with their children, with Park reportedly particularly keen to move back. The family is reportedly living in an apartment in southern Seoul's Seocho District, while both children attend an international school in Korea. The couple made headlines in June when they were spotted vacationing in Singapore with another celebrity couple, actors Park Shin-hye and Choi Tae-joon. Bae particularly drew attention for his long, gray hair, a departure from the image many fans remember from his acting days.

item.title: 2 chronicles of Korea's Three Kingdoms to go on joint display for 1st time
item.description: Two foundational chronicles of Korea’s ancient kingdoms will go on joint display in the country for the first time, offering visitors a rare look at how the history of Baekje and other early states was recorded and preserved. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that Hansung Baekje Museum will open a special exhibition, “Samguk Sagi and Samguk Yusa: Recording Baekje,” on Friday, running through Feb. 21. The exhibition marks the reopening of the museum's permanent galleries and brings together the two landmark historical works, “Samguk Sagi” and “Samguk Yusa,” alongside restored woodblocks and historical editions. A major highlight is the complete Oksan Seowon edition of “Samguk Sagi,” a National Treasure comprising nine volumes and 50 books printed around 1573. Oksan Seowon, a Confucian academy in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, is lending the entire collection to highlight the historical value of documentary heritage and the importance of its preservation. item.title: [FORUM] Experts call for changes in corporate behavior to tackle 'Korea discount'
item.description: Korea's corporate governance reforms must translate into tangible changes in corporate decision-making in order for the country to overcome its longstanding market discount, experts said Tuesday. The remarks came during the 2026 Korea Times Forum, where participants discussed ways to strengthen the country's capital market and improve its global competitiveness. During a session titled "Capital market reform to eliminate Korea discount," panelists examined structural weaknesses holding back the market and measures to attract more long-term investment. item.title: HD Hyundai's Global R&D Center earns national building safety certification
item.description: HD Hyundai’s Global R&D Center has earned a national safety certification for its facility management, the shipbuilding and heavy industry conglomerate said Tuesday. The company received the Space Safety Certification from the Korea Safety Certification Institute on Monday at a ceremony at the center. The center is located in Pangyo, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, a technology hub south of Seoul often called Korea's Silicon Valley. The certification is the country's only voluntary safety evaluation program for companies. The institute runs it under the supervision of the National Fire Agency. The program assesses a building's safety comprehensively, from design and construction to operation and maintenance, and certifies facilities that meet its standards. Certification is valid for three years. During that period, the facility does not have to undergo one of the two comprehensive fire safety inspections normally required each year. The center earned the certification this month after about nine months of document reviews, on-site evaluations and improvement measures that began in Februa

item.title: Lawmaker referred to prosecutors over alleged corruption, bribery
item.description: Police on Tuesday referred independent lawmaker Kim Byung-kee to prosecutors over various corruption allegations, such as taking bribes. Kim, formerly of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), faces allegations of accepting tens of millions of won in exchange for legislative favors for cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb and a transport system company. He is also suspected of overlooking allegations that a former DPK lawmaker took 100 million won ($74,400) in bribes ahead of the 2022 local elections, and accepting a hotel voucher from Korean Air, among other allegations. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's public crimes unit sent the cases to the prosecution, recommending multiple charges, including acceptance of bribes and obstruction of business. Kim quit the DPK in January after stepping down as the party's floor leader the previous month over the mounting allegations.

item.title: Hyundai, Kia's Europe sales fall 1.7% in October amid Chinese competition
item.description: Combined vehicle sales by Korea's Hyundai Motor and its affiliate Kia in Europe fell 1.7 percent in October from a year earlier amid stiff competition from Chinese automakers, industry data showed Tuesday. Hyundai and Kia sold a combined 80,005 vehicles in Europe last month, down from 81,358 a year earlier, according to data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA). "Hyundai recently discontinued production of the i10, a mass-market model, in Europe to make way for the Ioniq 3. However, the new model has yet to gain traction among local customers," a company spokesperson said. In addition, gains made by Chinese carmakers in Europe weighed on the monthly results, he said. Hyundai Motor's sales fell 18.8 percent on-year to 33,245 units, while Kia's rose 15.7 percent to 46,760 units. Hyundai Motor's sales fell 18.8 percent on-year to 33,245 units, while Kia's rose 15.7 percent to 46,760 units. item.title: State honors revoked for 8 military officers behind state violence cases
item.description: The defense ministry said Tuesday it has revoked state honors and medals awarded to eight military officials behind state violence cases, including one involving forced conscription of university students who resisted former President Chun Doo-hwan's authoritarian rule in the 1980s. The Cabinet passed a motion Tuesday to annul 10 state honors conferred on eight military officers over their "unconstitutional" acts, according to the ministry. The move comes as the government has sought to strip those accused of state violence of their commendations as part of efforts to preserve constitutional value and set the prestige of state honors straight. Among them is late Gen. Park Jun-byung, who led a cover-up scheme by forcibly drafting university students in the early 1980s in an attempt to suppress student activists who resisted Chun's dictatorship. item.title: Seoul shares rebound over 6% on Huang's return
item.description: Korean shares rebounded over 6 percent Tuesday, recovering from a two-day rout, as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia. The Korean won was trading higher against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) added 297.49 points, or 6.32 percent, to end at 5,006.03 after reaching as high as 5,065.74. The KOSPI reclaimed the psychologically important 5,000-point mark for the first time in three sessions. As the rally gathered momentum, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. It marked the first activation of a buy-side sidecar on the KOSPI since Nov. 10. The measure is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise at least 5 percent and remain at that level for one minute or longer. Overnight, technology stocks on Wall Street surged after Nvidia's board decided to reinstate Huang, triggering a relief rally in battered artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. item.title: EU unveils 22nd Russia sanctions package as war nears sixth year
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen unveiled the 27-member bloc's proposed 22nd package of Russia-related sanctions as the Kremlin's war against Ukraine nears its grim fifth anniversary. The package includes bans on 60 Russian banks that will be removed from the SWIFT system and punitive measures to crack down on crypto and payment networks. Third countries that aid Russia in evading sanctions will also be targeted. An energy services ban will be expanded, denying European companies from helping Russia with its energy infrastructure, especially its refineries, which Ukraine has been attacking. The ban will also cover electricity services. More than 70 tankers of Russia's shadow fleet will be added to its blacklist. The package includes a proposed ban on Russian ex-combatants visiting Europe. In a written statement unveiling the package Monday, von der Leyen said this move is in response to the escalation in so-called non-conventional kinetic activities conducted by Russian operatives in Europe. "They cannot be allowed to wander freely across our countries," she said. The fo

item.title: Seoul to overhaul public restrooms across 8 major tourist zones
item.description: Seoul will add more public restrooms, renovate aging facilities and tighten hygiene standards across eight major tourist districts and 10 traditional markets to make navigating the city easier for foreign visitors. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday the initiative will focus on helping travelers locate clean, accessible facilities nearby. The eight designated tourist districts are Itaewon; Myeong-dong, Namdaemun, Bukchang-dong, Da-dong and Mugyo-dong; Dongdaemun Fashion Town; Jongno and Cheonggye; Jamsil; Gangnam MICE; Hongdae Culture and Arts; and Goto and Sebitseom. As part of the initiative, the city will expand multilingual restroom information through QR codes installed on street facilities, digital information boards and bus and taxi stops. Visitors will be able to scan codes to view maps showing nearby public restrooms, building on English-language restroom information introduced on Visit Seoul, the city's official tourism platform, in early November. The city also plans to increase the number of publicly accessible restrooms from 148 to 200 by 2027, encouraging partici

item.title: Banks to issue stablecoins, digital asset platform operators' stake capped at 20%: regulator
item.description: Banks will be allowed to issue stablecoins, and platform operators of digital assets must hold their stake at below 20 percent, the financial regulator said Tuesday. Also, digital asset platform operators as well as digital asset brokering and management firms are subject to regulations applied to financial institutions, according to the proposal for the comprehensive enactment regulating digital assets such crytpo currencies. According to the government proposal, a consortium, more than half owned by a bank are able to issue stable coins, and fintech firms are allowed to join the consortium as well. Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies pegged to another asset, typically the U.S. dollar, to maintain a stable value, and their adoption has been growing globally. The Bank of Korea has been cautious over stablecoins as they can be used as a channel for bypassing foreign exchange and capital regulations, and could undermine the effectiveness of monetary policy. The central bank has insisted that banks become the main issuers of stablecoins, or if stablecoins are issued through bank-led consortia,

item.title: Justice minister nominee sidesteps question on dropping charges against president
item.description: Justice minister nominee Lee Yong-chul did not make clear whether he would direct prosecutors to drop charges against President Lee Jae Myung during his confirmation hearing Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned him about his role concerning a special counsel tasked with investigating how the pending criminal cases against the president were brought. Under a law that took effect Thursday, the special counsel and relevant prosecutors will examine whether prosecutors abused their authority in bringing the charges forward before the president was elected in June 2025. The inquiry will cover the prosecution’s handling of 12 cases, including six involving allegations against the president stemming from his 2010-2018 tenure as Seongnam mayor and Gyeonggi Province governor from 2018 to 2021. If appointed, the nominee could direct the special counsel on how to handle the pending cases in light of the special prosecutors’ findings. Opposition lawmakers questioned whether his long-standing ties to the president could undermine his ability to make a fair and objective decision. The nominee and the pr

item.title: Handsome street food vendor who resembles Cha Eun-woo reveals surprising backstory
item.description: Outside a convenience store in Gwangmyeong, Gyeonggi Province, customers flock to an unassuming street food stall without even a sign. Some wait up to two hours to get their hands on bungeoppang, a popular Korean fish-shaped pastry filled with sweet red bean paste. Behind the griddle is Lee Jae-jin, a young man whose resemblance to singer and actor Cha Eun-woo has earned him the nicknames "Gwangmyeong's Cha Eun-woo" and "Bung Eun-woo," a playful combination of bungeoppang and the celebrity's name, on social media. Monday's episode of SBS' "Master of Living" introduced the story of Lee, who has been making and selling the pastries for two years. While his good looks initially attracted attention on social media, the quality of his pastries has also helped spread the word. Lee cooks the batter until it turns golden brown and crispy, generously filling each pastry with sweet red bean paste from head to tail. He learned how to make bungeoppang at a renowned shop near Hyochang Park, widely regarded as one of Seoul's three best bungeoppang vendors. The program also revealed an unexpected detail

item.title: [FORUM] Korea needs stronger shareholder powers, Kosdaq chair says
item.description: Korea should give shareholders binding votes on executive compensation policies and lower barriers to shareholder proposals and lawsuits to help achieve a “Korea premium,” Kosdaq Market Committee Chairman Kim Woo-chan said Tuesday. Delivering a keynote speech at the 2026 Korea Times Forum, titled “Capital market advancement: Giant leap toward era of Korea premium,” Kim called for stronger shareholder powers to help translate recent governance reforms and market gains into lasting improvements in the nation’s capital market. Kim, who is also a professor at Korea University Business School, said his remarks reflected his personal views, not those of the Korea Exchange. Kim outlined priorities for further reform: executive compensation, shareholder proposals, derivative lawsuits, shareholder meetings and collaborative investor engagement. “Still in Korea, shareholders have less control,” he said, addressing executive compensation. item.title: [FORUM] Korea emerges as regional leader in corporate governance reform: ACGA chief
item.description: Korea has staged one of the most decisive turnarounds and become a regional leader in corporate governance, said Amar Gill, secretary general of the Asian Corporate Governance Association (ACGA), Tuesday. "It has moved in a remarkably short period from a market long characterized by stalled reform and structural discounts to one where policymakers have delivered a coherent sequence of changes that better protect minority shareholders," Gill said during his keynote speech at the 2026 Korea Times Forum at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. Korea ranked fifth in this year's edition of ACGA's CG Watch, which evaluates Asia's corporate governance (CG) landscape. Korea moved up three places from 2023 and nine places from 2018. The only other market to have seen a similarly significant improvement in its ranking, according to Gill, is Japan, which climbed from seventh in 2018 to second this year. "Japan and Korea are providing leadership in the region on value-up type of program," Gill said. CG Watch evaluates 12 Asia-Pacific markets across seven categories: government and pub

item.description: A senior North Korean official has held talks with China's top envoy to Pyongyang and reiterated her country's commitment to cementing relations with Beijing, the Chinese Embassy in the North said Tuesday. Ryu Un-hae, vice minister at the Ministry of External Economic Relations, met Chinese Ambassador Wang Yajun at the embassy in Pyongyang on Monday, taking stock of progress in bilateral ties following the summits between North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September 2025 and again in June, according to the embassy. item.title: Infertility leave of absence to go into effect next month
item.description: Civil servants undergoing fertility treatment will be entitled to one year of infertility leave of absence, extendable by up to an additional year, officials said Tuesday, a move partly aimed at tackling the country's ultralow birth rates. The change was made possible as revisions to the decrees on the appointment of public officials and local public officials were approved at a Cabinet meeting, the Ministry of Personnel Management and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety said. The revisions will go into effect Dec. 3. So far, those undergoing fertility treatment have used sick leave instead. Under the revised decrees, those receiving assisted reproductive technology or equivalent infertility treatment are entitled to up to one year of infertility leave, which can be extended by up to another year in unavoidable cases. Applications for the leave should be approved in principle, officials said. "We will build a child rearing-friendly public service environment where having and raising children does not become a burden," said Park Sung-hee, director general of the Personnel Innovation B

item.title: Riot Games to fund conservation of rare Goryeo Buddhist painting held in US
item.description: Riot Games, the U.S. developer behind global hit games, including League of Legends and Valorant, will fund the conservation of a rare 14th-century Korean Buddhist painting held by the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco, the company said Tuesday. The painting, "The Buddha Amitabha with the Eight Great Bodhisattvas," dates from the Goryeo Kingdom, which ruled the Korean Peninsula from 918 to 1392. Amitabha, the Buddha who presides over the Pure Land paradise, sits cross-legged on a high pedestal. Below him stand eight bodhisattvas, enlightened beings who help others reach salvation, four on each side. Only about 10 paintings of this type survive worldwide, including works at the National Museum of Korea and a temple in Japan. The San Francisco painting was collected by Avery Brundage, a former president of the International Olympic Committee, who donated it to the museum in 1972. The painting has been brought to Korea for the work, which is expected to take about two years. When it is finished in 2028, the painting will go on public display in exhibitions in Korea and abroad. The project i

item.title: Korea Tourism Organization donates 10,000 coal briquettes to Wonju households
item.description: The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) has donated 10,000 coal briquettes to help low-income households in Wonju, Gangwon Province, stay warm this winter, the state-run agency said. The organization gave the briquettes Monday to the Bapsang Community Briquette Bank, a charity that supplies heating fuel to households in need. About 30 employees from the organization and its subsidiary, KTO Partners, delivered briquettes by hand the same day to homes in the city's Wonin-dong neighborhood. Coal briquettes, known in Korean as "yeontan," are cylindrical blocks of compressed coal with holes running through them. Gas and oil heating have largely replaced them, but they remain an important source of heat for many elderly and low-income households in older neighborhoods because they are cheap. Volunteers often carry them by hand to homes along narrow alleys and steep hillsides that delivery trucks cannot reach. The 10,000 briquettes, including those delivered Monday, will be handed out gradually to local residents through the charity, the organization said. The program aims to ease heating costs fo

item.title: Seoul exports outdoor library model to El Salvador, Indonesia
item.description: Seoul has launched pilot versions of its popular outdoor library in El Salvador and Indonesia, exporting one of its signature civic programs overseas, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday. The newest branch opened Saturday, spanning 1,500 square meters at Bustanussalatin Park in Banda Aceh, Indonesia. It follows an 1,800-square-meter space launched Oct. 31 at Cuscatlan Park in San Salvador, the capital of El Salvador. Both locations will operate pilot programs on weekends for eight weeks through the end of the year. The Seoul Outdoor Library was launched in 2022. It turns public spaces such as Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Stream into open-air reading areas with bookshelves, beanbag sofas and cultural programs. It has drawn more than 10 million visitors. The overseas sites are part of the Seoul ODA Challenge. This official development assistance program shares the city's policies with foreign cities to help them tackle urban problems. This year it covers three projects in four cities. item.title: Discover Seoul Pass tops 400,000 sales in 1st decade
item.description: Sales of Seoul’s flagship tourist pass for foreign visitors have topped 400,000 cards over its first decade, the Seoul Tourism Organization said Tuesday. The agency announced the milestone at an anniversary event at the Pullman Ambassador Seoul Eastpole hotel celebrating 10 years of the Discover Seoul Pass. Roughly 110 representatives from 60 partner attractions, sales agents and pickup centers attended the gathering. The pass is sold only to foreign tourists. It combines free admission and discounts at major attractions in one physical or mobile pass. item.title: North Korean vessel to be returned soon on humanitarian grounds: Seoul
item.description: A North Korean fishing boat found near Ulleung Island in the East Sea earlier this month will be sent back to the North soon, Seoul's unification ministry said Tuesday, as most of those aboard the vessel are believed to want to return home. The ministry is "taking necessary steps, in consultation with relevant agencies, to send it back to the North on humanitarian grounds," a ministry official told reporters. The boat was found adrift Nov. 3 in international waters north of the southeastern island. Seven North Koreans were aboard. One of them is believed to have expressed a wish to stay in the South, with the request said to have been granted. Authorities have finished questioning the crew. The timing of the return will depend on the weather. Once a date is set, Seoul will contact the North through the United Nations Command, since the two sides have no working communication channel. Such vessels are generally repatriated by letting them sail back from the waters where they were rescued. item.title: Supreme Court confirms Japanese company should compensate late forced labor victim
item.description: The Supreme Court has confirmed a court ruling that ordered Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to pay compensation to a late Korean victim of Japan's wartime forced labor, legal sources said Tuesday. The late Kim Han-soo, who was conscripted into forced labor at a Mitsubishi shipyard in Nagasaki in 1944, had filed the suit against the Japanese company in 2019, seeking 100 million won ($75,000) in damages. Kim, who died in October last year, was one of many Koreans mobilized for forced labor during Japan's colonial rule of the Korean Peninsula from 1910-45. The Supreme Court upheld the appellate court ruling that ordered the company to pay 100 million won in compensation to Kim, which marked a reversal of a lower ruling that the statute of limitations had already passed. In overturning that ruling, the appeals court had deemed that the base year for calculating the statute of limitations should be 2018, when the top court confirmed the right of forced labor victims to seek compensation for damages.

item.title: Seven years after Goo Hara's death, law bearing her name takes effect
item.description: Seven years have passed since the death of Goo Hara, a member of K-pop girl group Kara. Her legacy continues to resonate beyond the entertainment industry, with a law bearing her name taking effect this year and bringing meaningful change to Korean society. Goo was found dead at her home in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul, on Nov. 24, 2019. She was 28. Police found no evidence of foul play, citing a handwritten note found at the scene, among other evidence, and decided not to conduct an autopsy. Following her death, a family dispute over her inheritance sparked a nationwide debate. Her older brother, Goo Ho-in, argued that it was unfair for their biological mother, who had been absent during most of her childhood, to inherit her estate. Under the Civil Act at the time, however, it was difficult to restrict a parent's inheritance rights solely on the grounds of failing to fulfill parental duties. item.title: Middle schooler identified as suspect behind fake bomb threat at department store
item.description: A middle school student has been identified as the suspect behind a fax message claiming an explosive was planted at a store of Shinsegae, a major department store chain, sources said Tuesday. The message was sent to police Sunday evening, prompting a search of all 13 Shinsegae branches across the nation, as the note had not specified a branch. No explosives were found. The case was assigned to Seoul's Guro Police Station, but the third-year middle school student was tracked down at his home in Ulsan, some 310 kilometers southeast of Seoul, on Monday through collaboration with the local police, according to the sources. The student reportedly admitted to sending the message. Police determined no explosives had actually been planted. Similar incidents have occurred in the past. In August 2025, an online post claimed an explosive was planted at Shinsegae's main branch in Seoul's Myeongdong district, forcing the evacuation of some 4,000 customers and staff members. The suspect in that case turned out to be a first-year middle school student living on the southern island of Jeju.

The next few weeks could determine whether Nvidia’s decision to reinstate him as CEO was the prudent one that cheering employees, shareholders and President Donald Trump made it out to be — or a big mistake. Huang’s supporters argued that he was indispensable, not only to the company but to the entire AI industry, at the moment a major engine of the economy. item.title: Jensen Huang saga exposes Korea's Nvidia dependence
item.description: Shares of Korea’s major tech firms roared back Tuesday after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to the top post, with the market’s sharp reversal demonstrating how Nvidia’s fortunes have become a powerful force shaping valuations of Korean corporate heavyweights. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix opened sharply higher on the benchmark KOSPI, gaining 8.85 percent and 11.71 percent, respectively, as Huang’s return to the helm fueled a rally in major chip stocks on the Nasdaq overnight. Hyundai Motor and Naver, which also maintain close ties with Nvidia, joined the rebound after recent losses. On the Nasdaq the previous day, Nvidia shares surged 31.5 percent following Huang’s return, while other artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks also rallied. Micron rose 19 percent and Oracle gained 12.3 percent. item.title: Asian stocks rally after Wall Street rebound as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: HONG KONG — Asian stocks advanced after a rally on Wall Street as Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia’s CEO, while U.S. futures edged higher and oil prices fell. Taiwan’s Taiex led gains in Asian markets, climbing more than 9 percent, driven by gains of nearly 10 percent for chip-related stocks Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. and Mediatek. The Kospi in Seoul advanced 6.5 percent to 5,014.41 as Samsung Electronics rose 7.5 percent and SK Hynix gained 8.6 percent. Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 3.9 percent to 58,654.40. Computer chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron climbed 10.5 percent and testing equipment maker Advantest surged 14.1 percent. “We are seeing a reaction to the rally in US tech stocks overnight on the announcement that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA as the CEO,” said Neil Newman, managing director and head of strategy at Astris Advisory Japan. “It is obviously a big surprise and a knock-on effect will be through Asia,” Newman said. item.title: SME exports account for 23.9% of Korea's shipments in January-October
item.description: Exports by small and midsized enterprises (SMEs) accounted for nearly 24 percent of Korea's total outbound shipments in the first 10 months of the year as the country's exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, customs data showed Tuesday. Korean SMEs exported $222.3 billion worth of goods in the January-October period, accounting for 23.9 percent of the country's total exports of $930.2 billion, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. The figure represents a 35.1 percent increase from $164.5 billion recorded in the same period of 2011, when the country first achieved $500 billion in annual exports. After nearly 15 years, Korea's annual exports surpassed the $1 trillion mark Thursday, making it the fourth country in the world to achieve the milestone after the United States, Germany and China. The number of exporting SMEs rose 22.2 percent to 96,286 in the January-October period of 2026 compared with the same period 15 years earlier. Nearly 300 SMEs exported $100 million or more worth of goods during the 10-month period, the customs data showed.

item.title: Air Force deploys early warning, forecast system for space weather observation
item.description: The Air Force said Tuesday it has deployed an early warning and forecast system to better observe changes in "space weather" in a bid to help enhance stable military operations in space. Space weather refers to changes in the space environment caused by solar activities, such as flares near sunspots. The Air Force held an event to mark the deployment of the early warning and forecast system for space weather in Gyeryong, some 145 kilometers south of Seoul, attended by some 60 personnel, according to the armed service. The Air Force has sought to develop systems to observe and analyze any changes in space weather in advance to better prepare the military for potential disruptions in its operations. For instance, an explosion near the sunspots may interfere with the ionosphere in the Earth's upper atmosphere, thereby disrupting aviation radio communications or causing errors in navigation systems. The newly deployed systems are designed to prevent such disruptions by informing the military of such changes in a timely manner ahead of military operations. Earlier this month, the Air Force depl

item.title: China investigates Politburo member Chen Jining, Xinhua says
item.description: BEIJING — Shanghai's party chief Chen Jining, a member of China's elite Politburo, is under investigation, China's state-run Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday, marking the fourth member of the top leadership body to be probed since 2025. Chen is being investigated for "suspected severe violations of discipline and laws," Xinhua said. The phrase is a common euphemism for corruption. Before the unexpected announcement of the Chen probe, three Politburo members from the 24-member body formed in 2022 — He Weidong, Zhang Youxia and Ma Xingrui — had already been purged. The investigation of Chen marks a further escalation in President Xi Jinping's widening anti-graft campaign, which has thinned the party's senior leadership ranks and depleted the military's top command. Chen, 62, had an unusual rise through China's official ranks. An environmental scientist by training, he earned a doctorate from Imperial College London and rose through China's elite Tsinghua University to become its president.
