item.title: No. of ministries, gov't agencies set to relocate to Sejong reduced to 31
item.description: The number of government agencies set to be relocated to the central administrative city of Sejong by 2031 will be reduced to 31, set to affect 5,460 public servants, the interior ministry said Tuesday. The change of plan was included in a notice released by the ministry. Originally, the government had planned to send a total of 44 ministries and agencies to Sejong, about 110 kilometers south of Seoul, starting next year. Of the 31 subject to the relocation, 22 agencies, including the media watchdog Korea Media and Communications Commission, will move their offices to leased-private buildings by next year. Nine agencies that require special facilities, such as the Board of Audit and Inspection and the National Police Agency, will relocate to a newly constructed building by 2031, the ministry added. The estimated cost for the relocation was about 1.65 trillion won ($1.2 billion), according to the notice. item.title: Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say
item.description: BOSTON/NEW YORK — Nvidia's board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday. The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment, these people said. Nvidia said on Monday that after talks with senior U.S. officials, its board "is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. The abrupt U-turn, just days after the board vowed to look elsewhere for a successor, has also drawn U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration into Nvidia's corporate governance. item.title: Nat'l Assembly speaker discusses bilateral ties with Japanese PM
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik met with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during a visit to Tokyo on Tuesday to discuss ways to expand bilateral cooperation and called for Tokyo's support in reviving a long-stalled parliamentary dialogue forum. It marked the first time that a Korean parliamentary speaker has held talks with a Japanese prime minister since December 2023 when then Speaker Kim Jin-pyo met with then Prime Minister Fumio Kishida in Tokyo. "Thanks to the leadership of the Korean and Japanese leaders, the two countries are enjoying their friendliest relations ever," Cho said, noting that "shuttle diplomacy" between their countries' leaders has been restored. Cho requested Takaichi's support for resuming the "Future Dialogue between the Parliaments of Korea and Japan," a parliamentary dialogue forum last held in 2018. He also expressed hope for greater economic cooperation in advanced industries, supply chains and energy, and asked Takaichi to help ensure Korean companies can operate without difficulties in Japan. item.title: Korea, Brazil launch dialogue to boost defense industry ties
item.description: Korea and Brazil have held their inaugural dialogue on defense industry cooperation, Seoul's state arms agency said Tuesday, as Seoul looks to expand arms exports into Latin America. The first meeting of the joint defense industry committee took place in Brazil on Monday (local time), led by officials of Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and Brazil's defense ministry, DAPA said in a release. The committee's launch came as a follow-up step after the two countries agreed to bolster defense industry ties at a summit between President Lee Jae Myung and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Seoul in February. Korea views Brazil as a strategic partner in its push to diversify arms exports to the Central and South American regions. Seoul plans to purchase three Brazilian-made Embraer C-390 Millennium tactical airlifters for its Air Force to boost its troop transport and aerial refueling capabilities under the second phase of its large transport aircraft acquisition program. item.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, vows to be 'a better CEO'
item.description: Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to Nvidia's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday, less than two weeks after he resigned as CEO following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China. "I'd be a better CEO the second time around," the 63-year-old, clad in his trademark black leather jacket, told cheering employees who packed an atrium and crowded the balconies above. US President Donald Trump — instrumental in Huang's comeback — heaped praise and fellow tech icon Elon Musk hailed his return. Nvidia shares surged 31.5 percent, propelling a broader Wall Street rally. Huang's swift reinstatement at the helm of the chipmaker he co-founded more than three decades ago is the story of a stunning comeback, one that underscores his sway over Washington, markets, the AI industry and geopolitics. "Jensen is bigger than Elvis for tech investors," said Eric Schiffer, chairman of Los Angeles-based private equity firm Patriarch Organization. item.title: Lee's new security team faces strains with US, tensions with North Korea
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung has appointed a new foreign policy and security team as Seoul tries to get stalled negotiations with Washington on nuclear-powered submarines back on track, while managing the risk of an accidental clash along the increasingly fortified border with North Korea. On Monday, Lee nominated Lim Woong-soon, currently deputy national security adviser, as foreign minister; former presidential secretary for political affairs Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister; and former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as director of the National Intelligence Service. National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac remains in his post. The appointments come amid friction with Washington over intelligence sharing. The presidential office said the government would continue to strengthen the U.S. alliance and pursue peace on the Korean Peninsula. Submarine talks stalled South Korea and the U.S. held their first meeting in June on Seoul’s plan to acquire nuclear-powered submarines and its bid for broader authority to use nuclear material. item.title: SKT's AI Care senior aid app wins trade ministry honor at Michelin Star Awards
item.description: SK Telecom’s AI Care program, an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered elderly care service, has won the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy Award as one of 10 honorees at the 2026 Michelin Star Awards, the mobile carrier said Tuesday. The awards combine corporate social responsibility initiatives with the format of the Michelin Guide, allowing members of the public to participate in identifying outstanding social contribution programs. Organized by the Federation of Korean Industries and supported by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the awards were held for the first time this year. AI Care advanced from an initial pool of 113 programs to 20 finalists following an expert review, securing a place among the final 10 through public voting, held from Oct. 26 to Nov. 8, and a committee evaluation. item.title: MBC's beloved book show to return after 25 years
item.description: A beloved television show in Korea that helped turn reading into a nationwide pursuit is returning after 25 years, hoping to reconnect with young audiences in an age of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital distraction. MBC’s “Let’s Read Books Returns,” a three-part revival show of its 2001 hit reading campaign reality show, premieres Wednesday at 9 p.m. Original host Kim Yong-man will join comedian Seo Kyung-seok and education YouTuber Mimiminu. Produced in cooperation with the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education, the reboot will visit elementary, middle and high schools to explore students’ reading habits and concerns. The hosts will introduce selected books and lead quizzes involving students and teachers, according to MBC. The original show aired between 2001 and 2003, with hosts meeting readers around the country. During the two years, the program introduced 25 books which became bestsellers. The show also helped in launching the Miracle Library project in 2003, bringing a children’s library to Suncheon, South Jeolla Province. The show’s popularity drew viewershi

item.title: [FORUM] AI rout puts Korea's corporate value-up drive back in spotlight
item.description: Korea's stock market rally earlier this year, buoyed by the artificial intelligence (AI) supercycle, initially drew investors' eyes to the broader market’s growth potential. But as the market enters a correction, stakeholders are looking more closely at companies outside the AI boom to assess whether they can generate sustainable returns and close the country's longstanding valuation gap. "The AI curtain has been lifted. Now, the low-PBR [price-to-book ratio] companies are much more visible and shareholders are starting to increase their voices," said Kim Seo-ha, managing director and partner at consulting firm BCG Korea. Companies outside the AI and semiconductor sectors are consequently facing greater scrutiny over their valuations, with pressure from shareholders and the government to improve corporate value likely to intensify. "The market should reward companies that make genuine efforts [to improve their corporate value] and therefore can highlight the rest of the market, instead of just riding the AI cycle," said Peter S. Kim, global investment strategist of KB Financial Group.

item.title: Korean won climbs against US dollar on foreign inflows
item.description: The Korean won strengthened against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, as foreign investors turned net buyers of local stocks. The won was quoted at 1,342.4 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 3.5 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in morning trading, the won rose to a high of 1,348.7 per dollar, but pared some gains. The won's rise came after the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) jumped, following strong gains on Wall Street after the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia. Foreign investors purchased a net 725 billion won ($543 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the KOSPI surging 6.32 percent to close at 5,006.03.

item.description: The finance ministry said Tuesday it plans to place greater emphasis on easing economic polarization in next year's economic policy while fostering new growth drivers to sustain economic momentum. The Ministry of Finance and Economy reported key outlines of its 2027 economic policy plan to President Lee Jae Myung at a Cabinet meeting. The 2027 economic policy plan is scheduled to be announced next month, with a focus on realizing "growth for all" by ensuring that every citizen can equally enjoy the opportunities and benefits of economic growth. item.title: Final talks between Seoul Metro labor, management in deadlock ahead of planned strike
item.description: Labor and management at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, remained at odds in their final negotiations Tuesday, a day before unionized workers threatened to launch a strike. If the negotiations fail, the company's three labor unions plan to launch an indefinite general strike starting with the first trains Wednesday, potentially disrupting the morning commute. Seoul Metro's three labor unions are demanding a 3.5 percent wage increase, the scrapping of planned workforce reductions and additional hiring. Seoul Metro and Union 1 began their fourth round of collective bargaining and wage negotiations at 10 a.m., but the talks were quickly adjourned without an agreement. Union 1 is also demanding that the company scrap a plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire an additional 1,313 on-site safety workers this year to address staffing shortages. Other demands include state funding for public services and a requirement that all field operations be carried out by two-person teams. Seoul Metro also held separate negotiations with Union 3 at 11 a.m. and Union 2 at 1:30 p.

item.title: ICE Out of NJ Demands Freedom for Junior Marte & Other Former Delaney Hall Hunger Strikers
item.description:
Democracy Now! has obtained exclusive audio from inside Delaney Hall, the controversial immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey, operated by the for-profit prison company GEO Group. The audio was recorded over the summer during a labor and hunger strike organized by immigrant detainees. Junior Marte, an asylum seeker and father from Venezuela, was one of the organizers. He describes conditions inside the facility, including abusive treatment, medical neglect and prolonged legal limbo.

“We are here unjustly, wrongfully accused of being criminals. Yet immigration officials refuse to review our cases, because they know that we are all innocent people,” Marte says in the message.

The hunger and labor strike lasted for a month, with an estimated 300 detained immigrants participating in the protest. Jenny Garcia, campaign coordinator at the American Friends Service Committee of New Jersey, says that since the strikes, GEO Group and ICE have taken “every opportunity to retaliate against the strikers, the families visiting outside, and the protesters.”

item.title: "Only Path Forward Is to Abolish": Outcry After Masked ICE Agents Arrest Family at Seattle Airport
item.description:
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson and other officials in the state have denounced the violent arrest of a father and daughter by ICE agents on Saturday as they were boarding a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Video of the arrest shows masked plainclothes agents dragging a woman off the jetway as she screams for help. Both Alaska Airlines and the Port of Seattle said ICE carried out the operation without their knowledge. ICE said Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, originally from Mexico, was targeted for overstaying his tourist visa, and that his daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, would be charged with assault for allegedly throwing hot coffee at an agent — although witnesses dispute that account.

“This is one of, unfortunately, many thousands of detentions that is happening not only in Washington state, but across the country,” says Josefina Mora-Cheung, director of organizing for the immigrant justice group La Resistencia. “The only path forward is to abolish ICE.”

ICE said Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, originally from Mexico, was targeted for overstaying his tourist visa, and that his daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, would be charged with assault for allegedly throwing hot coffee at an agent — although witnesses dispute that account.
“This is one of, unfortunately, many thousands of detentions that is happening not only in Washington state, but across the country,” says Josefina Mora-Cheung, director of organizing for the immigrant justice group La Resistencia. “The only path forward is to abolish ICE.”

item.title: Too Big to Fire? Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia; Questions Loom Over AI Boom & U.S.-China Relations
item.description:
Nvidia stock prices surged over 30% on Monday as the chip maker reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Huang had stepped down earlier in November amid reports he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI boom, and the leadership turmoil had erased trillions in value from the U.S. stock market. President Donald Trump acknowledged he had encouraged the company’s board to bring Huang back.

“The fact that our markets are so over-indexed on the AI trade, that something like three-fourths of gains in the [S&P 500] this past year have been AI-related, is unsustainable,” says Aya Ibrahim, senior fellow for economic and national security at the AI Now Institute.

We also speak with organizer and researcher Tobita Chow, who says Huang’s “spy scandal” that led to his ouster is part of a larger effort by anti-China figures in the U.S. national security establishment to escalate tensions between the countries.

“The national security leadership in both parties in D.C. has been greatly frustrated with President Trump, who has over the past year pursued policies to maintain very warm relations with Xi Jinping,” says Chow, who notes that Secretary of State Marco Rubio is one of the “chief” frustrated China hawks in the administration.

item.title: POSCO International acquires US gas field for $550 mil.
item.description: POSCO International, the trading arm of POSCO Holdings, said Tuesday it has completed the acquisition of a U.S. shale gas field for $550 million as part of its growth strategy. The shale gas asset, owned by Chord Energy and located in Pennsylvania's Appalachian region, holds reserves equivalent to 1 million tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG), the company said in a press release. "This acquisition marks a significant milestone in the company's energy business in the United States, in line with POSCO Group's Triple Core growth strategy," POSCO Group Chairman Chang In-hwa said. "It will help enhance profitability by generating synergies with the group's LNG value chain, spanning production to sales." The company expects the shale gas asset to generate an average annual operating profit of 100 billion won ($74 million) through 2040 as it expands production. Under its Triple Core strategy, POSCO Group has been expanding its overseas energy resource investments, while also investing in a steel plant being built in the United States by Hyundai Motor Group and lithium resources in Argentina and

item.title: Korea's foreign ministry expresses regret to Russia over warplanes' KADIZ entry
item.description: The foreign ministry said Tuesday it has conveyed its regret to Russia over the entry of Russian military aircraft into the country's air defense zone and called for measures to prevent a recurrence. About five Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the East Sea earlier in the day and approached the edge of Korea's territorial airspace near Ulleung Island, according to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS). "We conveyed our regret to Russia through diplomatic channels and called for measures to prevent a recurrence," the ministry said in a press release. The ministry sent the message to the Russian Embassy in Seoul but stopped short of summoning the Russian ambassador, diplomatic sources said. The defense ministry called in Nikolai Marchenko, a military attache from the Russian Embassy in Seoul, to lodge a formal complaint over the incident. The JCS issued an alert for residents of the eastern island as the aircraft appeared close to entering Korean airspace. The Air Force also scrambled fighter jets in response, though no violation of the count

item.title: Seoul Metro labor, management hold final talks ahead of planned strike
item.description: Labor and management at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, began final negotiations Tuesday, a day before unionized workers threatened to launch a general strike. If the negotiations fail, the company's three labor unions plan to launch an indefinite general strike starting with the first trains Wednesday, potentially disrupting the morning commute. Seoul Metro's three labor unions are demanding a 3.5 percent wage increase, the scrapping of planned workforce reductions and additional hiring. Seoul Metro and Union 1 began their fourth round of collective bargaining and wage negotiations at 10 a.m., but the talks were quickly adjourned without an agreement. Union 1 is also demanding that the company scrap a plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire an additional 1,313 on-site safety workers this year to address staffing shortages. Other demands include state funding for public services and a requirement that all field operations be carried out by two-person teams. Seoul Metro also held its separate negotiations with Union 3 and Union 2 at 11 a.m. and 1:30 p.m., res

item.title: POSCO International secures 1st US shale gas assets in $550 mil. deal
item.description: POSCO International has completed its $550 million acquisition of a shale gas field in Pennsylvania, marking the company's entry into U.S. natural gas production and its first overseas energy asset acquisition since POSCO Group announced its Triple Core growth strategy in July. The group's trading and energy subsidiary said Tuesday that it had acquired all of U.S. energy company Chord Energy's stake in the Appalachian shale gas assets in Pennsylvania. The acquisition comes about two months after the companies signed a definitive agreement on Sept. 14. item.title: Why Nvidia couldn't afford to lose Jensen Huang | About That
item.description: Nvidia's board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, stating the decision followed consultation with multiple stakeholders — including the U.S. government. Andrew Chang breaks down how the CEO of a trillion-dollar tech company returned just 11 days after being forced to step down following reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia on Monday said it is reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately. Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25% in premarket trading. The company's move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board's decision just days earlier to rule out his return. Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of AI processors, steering its chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties along the way. He resigned on November 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies. The board said it was satisfied with Huang’s candor and leadership ability and, after receiving input from senior U.S. government officials, saw no national security risk in his return.

item.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
item.description: BERLIN — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow. "We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting -- Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia -- happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Zelenskyy said. "We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner." European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks. item.title: Boy and elderly survivor pulled from rubble after Russian attack near Kyiv
item.description: Rescuers pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a residential building in the town of Dymer in Ukraine's Kyiv region as the death toll from Sunday's Russian attack reached 11, officials said on Monday. The survivors, who were trapped for 22 hours, were identified only as Davyd and Valentyna, emergency service spokeswoman Viktoriia Ruban said, without providing their full names. Doctors were treating the boy, who was rescued from the wreckage on Sunday, and his parents were with him, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday in a post on Telegram. He said four other injured people were also in hospital. Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said earlier on Monday that rescuers had pulled another body from the rubble, raising the death toll to 11. The youngest of those killed was 11 years old, the Kyiv regional prosecutor's office said. Rescuers were combing the rubble of a residential building, after retrieving several bodies overnight. item.title: UK police evacuate 12,000 people from concert after 'unknown substance' release
item.description: LONDON — British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from a concert venue in Manchester after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital. Police declared a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during a performance by U.S. rapper Don Toliver. The ambulance service for the North West England area said it assessed more than 50 people who reported "eye and respiratory symptoms," while attendees were quoted by the BBC as reporting a "horrible smell" and seeing people choking. Police said on Monday they had started an investigation to find out what the substance was and how the incident came about, after the ambulance service earlier reported the substance was believed to be tear gas. Tear gas is a chemical irritant that temporarily incapacitates people by burning their eyes, nose and throat. item.title: Iran says will use 'all available means' to counter US blockade
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran said Monday it would use all means at its disposal to counter a US naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter US aggression," said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray. The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies. In response, the US imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. item.title: Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair: NYT
item.description: NEW YORK — Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China's top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant's former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. item.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya, Zelenskyy says
item.description: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship was one of Russia’s newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 invasion of its neighbor , the Ukrainian leader said in a post on X. Russian officials made no immediate comment. The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spiderweb in June last year, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked near air bases across Russia. The 36-year-old, best known for the hit series "Reply 1988," allegedly crashed into a cleaning vehicle in Seoul in the early hours of Nov. 14, while drunk driving. He has since issued a public apology and withdrawn from public appearances. item.title: 'Sumbakkokjil' producer serves Korean ghost lore to K-pop's global fandom
item.description: By pairing K-pop idols with Korean horror, "Sumbakkokjil" has grown from the first original program on Mnet Plus, CJ ENM's global K-pop platform, into its flagship, drawing fans around the world who tune in for their favorite acts and stay for the scares. "Sumbakkokjil" — the Korean name for the game of hide-and-seek — drops K-pop acts into abandoned buildings and other darkened sets. Group members must avoid being caught by an unidentified seeker for 4,444 seconds. In its first season, they hunted for keys before the chase began, while season two required them to collect "dead pieces" to escape. Rather than the typical showcase of singing and dancing, the show focuses on how idols react to the scares and how they look out for one another. Its second season, which wrapped Friday, made it the platform's first original to run for more than one season. The season and its related content was watched in 213 regions and drew more than 100 million cumulative views, and CJ ENM credits it with bringing in over 320,000 new sign-ups. "We didn't expect it to be such a hit," producer Ahn Hye-rin

item.title: SK chair offers to pay full $701 mil. to settle divorce dispute
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won on Monday asked the Supreme Court to propose a settlement in his divorce-related property dispute, offering to pay the full 944 billion won ($701 million) awarded by a lower court to his former wife, Art Center Nabi Director Roh Soh-yeong. Chey’s representatives said the offer was intended to bring the long-running dispute to an end, but it does not mean the case is over. If the Supreme Court proposes a settlement, either party may object within two weeks of receiving the decision. item.title: Korean, Mongolian FMs discuss cooperation on critical minerals, trade
item.description: The top diplomats of Korea and Mongolia discussed bilateral cooperation on critical minerals, trade, technology and other key issues during their talks in Seoul on Monday, the foreign ministry said. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg at his ministry as the two countries seek to expand cooperation following Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit to Ulaanbaatar in July. During the meeting, Cho called for accelerating joint efforts to sign a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA), noting that the agreement, if inked, would serve as an institutional foundation for expanding bilateral trade and investment, according to the ministry. Cho also noted the need for the two countries to leverage a rare metals cooperation center in the Mongolian capital for expanding cooperation across the entire critical minerals value chain. The center opened last December as part of Seoul's official development assistance project for the country. He also asked the Mongolian government to help ensure that Korean businesses can operate in the country

item.title: Nearly 3,000 people petition gov't to prevent cheating on college entrance exam
item.description: Nearly 3,000 people have signed a petition demanding the government take proper steps to prevent cheating on the national college entrance exam, a student-led advocacy group said Monday, amid controversy over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating. The group, composed mainly of high school and college students, said it conducted two rounds of signature campaigns starting last Monday and a total of 2,964 people had joined the petition. Most of the signatories were students who had sat for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday amid confusion over the government's announcement of haphazard measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating. The measures had been rolled out after the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted to cheating using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative AI. In the petition, the group said it demands the education ministry and relevant authorities clearly outline procedures for filing appeals and the criteria for invalidating scores in cases of cheating, among other measures.

item.title: 2-term lawmaker nominated to lead interior ministry
item.description: Rep. Han Jun-ho, tapped to lead the interior ministry, is a two-term lawmaker of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) who formerly worked as a news anchor. Born in 1974 in the southwestern city of Jeonju, Han graduated from Yonsei University with a degree in mathematics before joining local broadcaster MBC as a newscaster in 2003. He left MBC in 2018 and worked at the presidential office under then President Moon Jae-in as a communications official. Han was elected as a lawmaker for the DPK in the 2020 general elections before winning his second term in the 2024 elections. He currently serves as a ranking member of the parliamentary science, ICT, broadcasting and communications committee. "As a two-term lawmaker and a former journalist, (Han) racked up legislative experience in various sectors, such as land, transport and artificial intelligence (AI)," Lim Kwang-hyun, presidential chief of staff, said. "He is expected to robustly secure public safety and inject vitality into region-led growth."

item.title: Kim Myung-min returns as ruthless jungle boss in 'Tristes Tropiques'
item.description: For veteran actor Kim Myung-min, returning to the big screen after a seven-year absence did not feel like a long wait at all. "To be honest, I didn't realize it had been seven years until I saw it in news reports," Kim told The Korea Times at a cafe in Seoul, Monday. "Back when I was younger, even two or three years felt like forever. Now that I am in my 50s, time flies at the speed of light." Kim stars as Master in director Park Hoon-jung's upcoming action noir "Tristes Tropiques," whose French title translates to "sad tropics." The movie marks Kim's first movie appearance since 2019 and his first project since the 2024 ENA drama "Your Honor." It also reunites him with Park nine years after they worked together on the 2017 crime thriller "V.I.P." Set in a dense rainforest, the story follows a group of young assassins raised by Master, the supreme ruler of a killer organization specializing in jungle warfare. item.description: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo is a three-term lawmaker and a close political ally of President Lee Jae Myung with North Korea expertise. Born in 1967, he studied political science at Hanyang University. Before entering politics, he worked as a researcher at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and as a policy adviser to the Ministry of Unification. He also taught as a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. He won election to the National Assembly three times, serving from 2012 to 2024. Hong served as floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea from September 2023 to May 2024 when Lee was party chair. item.title: Critic-turned-presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister
item.description: Kang Yu-jung, the senior presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister Monday, is a cultural specialist who worked for nearly two decades as a film and literary critic and columnist. Kang, 51, first gained prominence in 2005 when she swept three prizes in that year's newspaper literary contests, winning in film criticism from the Dong-A Ilbo and in literary criticism from the Chosun Ilbo and the Kyunghyang Shinmun. As a critic and columnist, Kang regularly appeared on television programs about film and wrote for daily newspapers. She also published several books on cinema and taught at Korea University and Kangnam University. Her interest in the arts extended beyond criticism. Last year, she received a special award at the Korea Dance Awards in recognition of her support for dance and her contributions to developing and popularizing the art form. Kang entered politics in the 2024 general election, winning a proportional representation seat with the Democratic Alliance of Korea, a coalition party led by the Democratic Party of Korea. item.title: Korea's exports forecast to exceed $1 tril. for 2nd straight year in 2027
item.description: Korea's exports are expected to exceed $1 trillion for the second consecutive year in 2027 on continued global demand for semiconductors, a state-run think tank said Monday. The Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade (KIET) forecast that Korea will post $1.32 trillion in exports in 2027, up 14.1 percent from this year's estimate of $1.16 trillion. The trade surplus is expected to rise to $455.9 billion next year from $377.8 billion this year. The KIET said exports are expected to expand 33.9 percent on-year in the first half of 2027, driven by increasing investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, while they are forecast to contract 0.7 percent in the second half due to a base effect and a correction in memory chip prices. As strong semiconductor exports are expected to boost domestic demand, the KIET projected Asia's fourth-largest economy will grow 3.5 percent next year. However, the KIET highlighted lingering uncertainties over U.S. trade policies, global AI investments and further developments in the war in the Middle East as possible downside risks. The KIET p

item.title: G-Dragon turns heads with long, flowing hair
item.description: BIGBANG's G-Dragon drew attention with a dramatic new hairstyle at the 2026 MAMA Awards, appearing onstage with long, silky, straight hair that seemed to get in his way as he delivered his acceptance speech. The K-pop star appeared alongside fellow BIGBANG members Taeyang and Daesung at Kyocera Dome Osaka in Japan on Saturday, where the group received the Music Visionary of the Year award. While the award marked a significant moment for the veteran K-pop group, G-Dragon's striking hairstyle became a highlight of the ceremony. Sporting long, flowing locks that framed his face and fell around his shoulders, the singer struggled to keep his hair out of the way while speaking. "We like to joke around a lot," G-Dragon said, adding to the lighthearted atmosphere. item.title: Unification minister, Mongolian FM vow closer cooperation for peace on Korean Peninsula
item.description: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young on Monday asked Mongolia to support peace on the Korean Peninsula, citing its friendly ties with the two Koreas, during a meeting with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg, the ministry said. Chung noted Mongolia's efforts to promote regional peace and thanked Battsetseg for the warm welcome he received in June when he visited the country to attend the 11th Ulaanbaatar Dialogue on Northeast Asian Security. Describing bilateral relations as entering an "age of gold," he expressed hope that the two countries will keep deepening mutual ties. Battsetseg also vowed to continue close cooperation with Seoul in its push for peaceful coexistence on the peninsula, according to the ministry.

item.title: Seoul stocks lose 3.3% as AI rout tests gov't rescue plans
item.description: Korean stocks fell 3.31 percent Monday, as a sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI)-related shares deepened, though bargain hunting after steep losses and government preparations to activate a stock market stabilization fund helped limit the decline. The benchmark KOSPI closed at 4,708.54, down 3.31 percent, its lowest finish since Jan. 13. The index opened 2.77 percent lower and plunged as much as 5 percent intraday, briefly slipping to 4,586.8. A sell-side sidecar was triggered at 11:33 a.m. The index pared losses in afternoon trading to finish just above the 4,700 mark. Institutional and other corporate investors helped cushion the decline as foreign and retail investors continued to sell, according to analysts. The decline followed Friday's sharp sell-off on Wall Street, where Nvidia, Sandisk, Micron, AMD and Broadcom each tumbled more than 10 percent, sending the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 10.73 percent. The losses extended across Korea's AI supply chain. SK hynix fell 2.52 percent to close at 1,085,000 won ($807.05), while Samsung Electronics dropped 3.06 percent to 17

item.description: Park Jong-bok, former CEO of Standard Chartered (SC) Bank Korea, has been named the sole candidate to lead the Korea Federation of Banks, setting him up to become the next head of the banking lobby, the federation said Monday. item.title: S. Korea commemorates 16th anniv. of victory against N. Korea's 2010 shelling of border island
item.description: The Marine Corps on Monday held a ceremony to mark the 16th anniversary of South Korea's victory in an artillery attack in 2010 by North Korea on a border island that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The ceremony was held at Daejeon National Cemetery in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul, on the occasion of the 16th anniversary of the North's artillery attack on Yeonpyeong Island on Nov. 23, 2010. North Korea's shelling of the island marked its first attack on a civilian area in the South since the 1950-53 Korean War. During Monday's event, Vice Defense Minister Lee Doo-hee said the South Korean military will maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure its victory against any enemy threats. "Our military will immediately respond to any enemy threat or provocation and maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure absolute victory," Lee said in his commemorative address. "To achieve this, we will push to restructure the military system so that the Marine Corps will be enhanced to a quasi-fourth service," he added. item.description: A court on Monday held arrest warrant hearings for eight National Election Commission (NEC) officials accused of manipulating voter turnout numbers or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. Three officials from the NEC headquarters appeared at the Seoul Central District Court in the morning, refusing to answer reporters' questions before entering the courtroom. Hearings for the remaining five officials from regional NEC offices were set to be held later in the afternoon. The court was expected to decide whether to issue the warrants later in the day at the earliest. Requests for the warrants were filed Wednesday by special counsel Lee Tae-han's team on suspicions that the election officials entered false voter turnout figures while voting was under way or forged vote count sheets during the race for the education superintendent of Gyeonggi Province, with some of them allegedly involved in multiple cases. item.title: Factional feud, impeachment fight test Kim Min-seok's DPK leadership at 100 days
item.description: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok heads into his 100th day in office on Tuesday, as party support slips amid a deepening factional feud, in stark contrast to the turnaround he promised. Kim pledged during his leadership campaign to raise the DPK’s support by at least 10 percentage points within three months. But a Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put the DPK’s support at 36 percent, down from 41 percent in a survey conducted from Aug. 11–13, just before Kim took office on Aug. 17. Under the circumstances, Kim’s leadership will face another test as he tries to reunite the DPK and win over centrist voters while the party’s hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae — a move that could rally its base and alienate moderates. “It appears the voters still don’t feel they can count on the ruling party to settle problems under Kim’s leadership,” said Jung Jae-hwan, a political science professor at Inha University. “The move to impeach the chief justice will test whether Kim can keep the party focused on voters’ everyd

item.title: GS E&C joins hands with 3 firms to speed up data center construction
item.description: GS E&C has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with LS Electric, LG Uplus and Honeywell to shorten the time needed to bring data centers into service by coordinating engineering work from procurement through final testing. GS E&C announced Monday that the four companies had signed the MOU in Seoul. The construction company said rising demand for data centers amid the expansion of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry has made meeting customers' project schedules more important than ever. The partners will coordinate across four stages: procurement preparation, design, system installation and integrated commissioning. They will review power, design, construction, controls and operational requirements early in the process to avoid duplicated work and address operational needs before construction begins. The aim is to minimize potential delays during construction and commissioning so facilities can begin serving customers sooner. item.title: Min Hee-jin's label cites SPEED anniversary gift to reject NewJeans copying claims
item.description: Min Hee-jin's independent label ooak records on Monday cited a gift from Japanese record label Toy's Factory, home to 1990s J-pop girl group SPEED, in rejecting online claims that NewJeans copied the Japanese act. Min recently shared on social media a direct message and a gift box from Toy's Factory, sent to mark SPEED's 30th debut anniversary. In the message, a company representative said the label's president had wanted to send Min a commemorative gift. Min responded by posting a photo of the box with a thank you message, which Toy's Factory's official social media account later reshared. In a statement Monday, ooak records said the exchange dismissed what it described as "groundless claims" that NewJeans had copied SPEED. The company characterized the gift as a gesture of respect from the Japanese label and evidence of a friendly relationship between the two sides. The message shared by Min, however, did not directly address the allegations. item.title: 5 CSAT examinees face criminal complaints over smart device cheating
item.description: The education ministry was set to file criminal complaints Monday against five people caught cheating with smart devices during last week's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), a senior ministry official said. The ministry previously announced that 111 suspected cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during the annual college entrance exam held Thursday amid growing public concerns over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on national exams. Of those cases, five involved the actual use of devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, according to the ministry. Complaints have already been filed against some of the five test-takers, and the process for all five will be completed before the day's end, Shin Jin-yong, head of the ministry's University Admissions Policy Division, said in a media briefing. The ministry also plans to indefinitely keep open its CSAT cheating reporting center on its website, Shin said, adding there are no restrictions on the scope of reports and that individuals can report suspected cheating not only in this year's CSAT

item.title: Family of late LEET top scorer appears before police in cheating probe
item.description: A family member of the late top scorer of this year's law school entrance exam appeared before police Monday as investigators step up a probe into allegations that he cheated on the test. The late Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student, was found dead Thursday after facing suspicions of cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Despite his death, police have pressed ahead with the investigation on suspicion of fraud and other charges, after a group of lawyers earlier filed a police complaint. Earlier in the day, a family member of Lee appeared before the financial crime unit under the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Police were expected to ask Lee's family member for cooperation in turning over evidence, such as his mobile phone. Lee's academic achievements came under widespread scrutiny following the recent admission by the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI. item.title: Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin's son takes mother's surname after turning 19
item.description: The son of Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin, a member of Samsung's founding family, has legally changed his surname to his mother's after reaching adulthood, following a court-approved application he filed himself. According to legal sources Monday, the Seoul Family Court approved a petition filed by Lee's son, Dong-hyun, to change his surname from Lim, his father's family name, to Lee. Presiding Judge Park Mi-hwa of the court's Family Division 21 granted the request last month. Dong-hyun reportedly filed the petition after becoming a legal adult in August. During its review, the court also sought the opinion of his father, Lim Woo-jae, a former adviser to Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Under Article 781, Paragraph 6 of Korea's Civil Act, a child's surname and ancestral family origin may be changed with court approval if deemed necessary for the child's welfare. Such requests can be filed by either parent or the child. Under Family Litigation Rules, courts may hear the opinions of the parents and children aged 13 or older when reviewing such petitions. item.title: 'Cats' unveils international cast for 8-city Korea tour
item.description: The international touring production of “Cats” will visit eight Korean cities beginning in December, bringing a 29-member cast whose performances combine singing with the demanding physical work of transforming into felines. The tour opens at Daegu’s Keimyung Art Center on Dec. 18 and continues through April 11, 2027, concluding at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul, according to a press release announcing the cast and itinerary, Monday. The principal performers have traveled with the production since its South African opening in December 2025, followed by the musical’s Mumbai premiere and engagements in Hong Kong and Singapore. Cindy-Ann Abrahams will play Grizabella, the faded glamour cat. A semifinalist on “South Africa’s Got Talent” in 2013, Abrahams won a best actress honor at the Cape Town Theatre Awards for the role, according to the release. Dylan Janse van Rensburg will portray the rebellious Rum Tum Tugger. His previous musical theater credits include Joseph in “Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat” and Melchior in “Spring Awakening.

item.title: Korea's gender wage gap remains widest among OECD members
item.description: Korea continued to have the widest gender pay gap among OECD countries in 2025, with women's median earnings 27.8 percent lower than men's, data showed Monday. According to the latest OECD data, women's median earnings in Korea stood at 72.2 percent of men's last year. The gap was the largest among 13 OECD countries that have released figures for 2025, exceeding Japan's 20.1 percent and the United States' 17.9 percent. The figures for Korea cover full-time employees and compare median monthly earnings. They do not adjust for differences in occupations or job assignments. Korea has recorded the widest gender pay gap among OECD members every year since 2000, although the disparity has gradually narrowed. The gap fell from 37.2 percent in 2015 to 31.5 percent in 2020 and 29.3 percent in 2023. It narrowed further to 29 percent in 2024 and 27.8 percent last year. The wage disparity also varied significantly across income levels, with Korea recording one of the widest gaps among OECD countries at both ends of the wage distribution. item.title: Ex-Justice Minister Kang tapped as spy agency chief
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service (NIS), Monday. Lee also tapped Lim Woong-soon, his second deputy national security adviser and a former ambassador to Canada, as foreign minister, and Hong Ihk-pyo, a former presidential secretary for political affairs and former floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), as unification minister. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the Cabinet reshuffle largely focused on the security and diplomacy sectors during a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul. He said the changes would bring in new leadership to protect Korea’s interests as the international landscape shifts. “Kang is the most suitable person to reinforce democratic oversight of the NIS, based on her strong belief in the neutrality of powerful organizations. She is also expected to resolve new security threats, such as cyberattacks, through international cooperation,” the chief of staff said. item.title: Korea ready to deploy market stabilization fund if conditions warrant: finance minister
item.description: Korea will decide whether to deploy its stock market stabilization fund based on how market conditions evolve, Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il said Monday, a day after the government began preparations. Lee said the government would continue to monitor the market before deciding on the timing and size of any deployment. “We are reviewing the steps needed in case market conditions warrant activating the fund,” Lee said at a press conference. “We will decide on the details as we assess how the situation evolves.” Lee said the review was intended to ensure the fund could be deployed smoothly if needed, given how long it had been idle. Asked whether the government would expand the fund, he said authorities would assess market conditions at the time of any deployment before deciding on its size. His remarks came as growing doubts about the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI) and returns on AI investment dented investor confidence. item.title: NC raises 2026 sales forecast on Lineage Classic success
item.description: Korean game developer NC raised its sales forecast for this year to 2.8 trillion won ($2.09 billion) in a Nov. 11 regulatory filing after sales through September surpassed the lower end of its previous full-year guidance, as Lineage Classic and casual mobile games bolstered its results. Third-quarter sales rose 91 percent from a year earlier to 687 billion won, while the company returned to operating profitability, posting an operating profit of 120 billion won. Sales for the first nine months rose 83 percent to 2.01 trillion won, above the previous guidance floor of 2 trillion won. Lineage Classic generated 159 billion won in sales in the third quarter, bringing its cumulative sales to 428 billion won in about eight months after launch. NC said the number of paying players remained stable. Sales from casual mobile games rose from the previous quarter to 172 billion won, accounting for 25 percent of total sales. item.description: A senior Qatari official has described Korea as an "essential" partner in Qatar's efforts to diversify its industries in the post-oil era during a bilateral policy meeting in Doha, Seoul's foreign ministry said Monday. item.title: Daily share buyback limit to be lifted for 3 months amid market rout
item.description: The country's financial regulator said Monday it will lift the daily share buyback limit for listed firms for three months, as part of efforts to stem market volatility. According to the Financial Services Commission (FSC), the daily limit for the purchase of own shares by publicly traded companies will be fully lifted from Tuesday. On Sunday, the financial authorities announced a set of measures to limit market jitters caused by rising fears over artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments. They also said around 10 trillion won ($7.42 billion) worth of a stock stabilization fund is in store to be activated when necessary. If the market rout deepens, the fund will go into operation, marking the first time since 2008. Also, the authorities stressed that market monitoring will be enhanced and illegal short selling will be strictly banned. The country's benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index dipped as low as more than 5 percent, before recovering to some degree as AI optimism faded over valuations and rising debt.

item.title: Jongno District deploys AI crosswalks to give slower pedestrians more time
item.description: Jongno District in central Seoul is upgrading its intersections with artificial intelligence (AI), pavement-level LED lights and automated voice alerts to help pedestrians — especially children and older adults — cross streets more safely. The district office said it will begin operating pavement-mounted pedestrian signals and voice guidance devices at 123 locations from Dec. 1 with an AI-powered system that automatically extends crossing time. The pavement-level pedestrian signals illuminate the tactile pavers, a kind of ground surface indicator to assist disabled pedestrians, at crosswalks to help people detect when it is safe to cross. Voice guidance devices use infrared sensors to detect pedestrians and issue audible warnings when they attempt to cross against the signal, as well as announcing when the light turns green. The installations target roads with at least four lanes, prioritizing areas with heavy pedestrian traffic and a history of accidents. item.title: Trump hosts gala for meme coin investors as his token plunges to record lows
item.description: NEW YORK — US President Donald Trump has made hundreds of millions from his $TRUMP meme coin, but at a Sunday dinner for the token's biggest holders, he said his motive for supporting the cryptocurrency was to boost the economic competitiveness of the United States. “I’m doing it for the United States... If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 but has fallen to a record low of under $1. The private dinner this year was more low-key than the initial event last year, attendees said, with a smaller crowd and far less money at stake this time. Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP coin from September 30 to November 16. Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16. item.title: US Forces Korea deploys Apache, Blackhawk helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan
item.description: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) recently deployed its helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan, the first time such assets have been sent outside the Korean Peninsula for exercises, the USFK said Monday. The 2nd Infantry Division's 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade deployed the AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, the UH-60 Black Hawk multirole utility helicopters and the CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters to the Combined Arms Training Center (CATC) at Camp Fuji, located in Shizuoka Prefecture, the USFK said in a social media post. It said the "historic first" deployment of the choppers was aimed at strengthening its readiness in the Indo-Pacific. The AH-64 Apache serves as a heavily armed attack helicopter designed to hunt and destroy enemy tanks and armored vehicles with missiles and rockets, while the UH-60 Black Hawk is a core asset primarily tasked with airlifting troops into combat zones, transporting supplies and evacuating wounded soldiers. The CH-47 Chinook is a heavy-lift transport helicopter used to move large numbers of troops, heavy artillery and bulk supplies across the battlefield.

item.title: PPP files petition with Constitutional Court over special counsel bill
item.description: Lawmakers of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) filed a petition with the Constitutional Court on Monday, arguing that their rights to vote on legislation were violated by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)'s unilateral passage of a special counsel bill. The PPP's move came after the DPK-controlled National Assembly railroaded the bill earlier this month that mandates a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. PPP lawmakers had boycotted the vote in protest. The PPP claimed that its lawmakers were not given sufficient time to review and deliberate on the details of the bill before its passage and said it filed a competence dispute against National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and DPK Rep. Seo Young-kyo, chair of the parliamentary legislation and judiciary committee. item.title: New Incheon airport chief tasked with fast-tracking capacity expansion
item.description: Incheon International Airport Corp.'s (IIAC) new CEO Park Nam-chun faces the task of accelerating capacity expansion at the country’s main aviation hub, as passenger traffic is expected to outstrip existing infrastructure in the coming years. Park officially took office Monday as the airport operator’s 11th chief for a three-year term, with expanding airport facilities expected to be among his top priorities. The Incheon airport plans to add a third passenger terminal and a fifth runway to raise its annual passenger-handling capacity from 106 million to 131 million. Park’s key challenge will be to move the projects from planning to construction and operation as quickly as possible, with passenger demand nearing the airport’s existing capacity. The airport handled 74.07 million international and domestic passengers last year, the highest annual figure since its opening in 2001. The figure is expected to climb further, as international travel demand continues to expand at a rapid pace. item.title: KB Financial's new chairman sets sights on turning banking giant into global platform
item.description: Lee Jae-keun, the new chairman of KB Financial Group, set a goal Monday to turn Korea’s largest financial group from a “leading bank” into a “leading platform.” His plan calls for closer cooperation among the group’s 11 affiliates and greater use of data and artificial intelligence (AI), as KB seeks to move beyond its reliance on banking and compete with major platforms in global markets. At his inauguration ceremony at KB Kookmin Bank headquarters in Yeouido, Seoul, Lee said the advantages that once made KB a domestic market leader were no longer enough to ensure its future growth. “KB became the country’s leading bank through its sheer scale — its extensive branch network and large deposit and lending businesses,” he said. “But as AI and digital technology drive down the cost of reaching customers, the competitive edge built on scale alone is quickly disappearing.” KB Financial has delivered record earnings under outgoing Chairman Yang Jong-hee, reporting net profit of 5.79 trillion won ($4.3 billion) in the first nine months of this year, up 13.1 percent from a

item.title: Seoul launches green bio hub to connect startups with investors, global markets
item.description: Seoul is expanding its ambitions in biotechnology, transforming its food startup center into a platform designed to connect promising agricultural and food technology companies with major corporations, investors and global distribution networks. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it had relaunched the Seoul Food Startup Center as the Seoul Green Bio Hub, broadening its focus from food manufacturing and distribution to technology-driven businesses built around agricultural and biological resources. Green biotechnology applies biological technologies to agricultural and other biological resources to create new products and commercial opportunities in sectors including food and agriculture. item.title: Korea conducts evacuation drills in Latvia amid political uncertainty
item.description: Korea has conducted mock drills to practice evacuating and protecting its nationals in Latvia amid deepening political uncertainty in the Baltic country, Seoul's foreign ministry said Monday. The drills involving a rapid response team took place at the Korean Embassy in Riga on Friday, it said, as Latvia has experienced political uncertainty since its ruling coalition collapsed in May following a dispute over drone incursions, with the newly formed government holding a narrow parliamentary majority. Embassy staff, National Fire Agency officials and civilian experts participated in the drills, sharing information on the situation in Latvia and safety guidelines on how to respond to incidents and accidents, and checking communication lines. "The drills ... were very helpful in checking a coordination mechanism between the foreign ministry and the overseas diplomatic mission in case of a crisis, and strengthening the embassy's readiness posture for protecting citizens abroad," Korean Ambassador to Latvia Kim Jong-han said.

item.title: Industry minister urges petrochem sector to rev up restructuring
item.description: The industry minister said Monday the petrochemical sector should accelerate its restructuring efforts to enhance its competitiveness. In August last year, 16 petrochemicals companies drew up business reorganization plans. Two restructuring schemes were approved by the government earlier this year, but a business reorganization plan for the Ulsan industrial complex has not been finalized. In a meeting with heads of major petrochemicals companies, such as LG Chem Ltd. and GS-Caltex Corp., Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan urged petrochemicals companies to draw up their final restructuring plans. "All companies should share the responsibility for the future of the sector," Kim said, adding that all discussions should be done before the end of the year. Kim said all necessary measures will be provided to help the sector take a leap forward to remain competitive. The local petrochemical sector has been facing a prolonged oversupply leading to low prices, especially amid the economic slowdown. item.description: SUWON, Gyeonggi Province — Audiences gasped and applauded as Japanese magician Taiju Fujiyama pulled eggs out of an apparently empty pocket, performing Edo Tezuma, a traditional Japanese form of magic preserved for roughly 300 years. The performance was part of the 2026 Suwon Japan Week, organized by the Japanese Embassy in Korea to showcase traditional culture and arts. The event began on Friday and runs through Nov. 26 in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, in line with the city’s 2026-2027 Visit Suwon Year. This year's program features a range of cultural activities, including traditional Japanese clothing experiences and traditional candy-making demonstrations. item.title: Seoul, Daesang turn tofu byproduct into healthier traditional snacks
item.description: Seoul is turning a byproduct of tofu production into a selling point for healthier snacks, teaming up with food company Daesang to launch two products that pair traditional flavors with waste-reducing food innovation. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it introduced Seoul Yakgwa and Seoul GO Guma Bar, marking its first collaboration with a private company to incorporate upcycled food ingredients into products under its Seoul My Soul city brand. Food upcycling involves transforming ingredients and byproducts that might otherwise be discarded during food production into new food products, helping reduce waste and make better use of resources. Seoul Yakgwa reimagines "yakgwa," a traditional Korean honey pastry, using soybean pulp left over from tofu production, an ingredient rich in protein and dietary fiber. Rather than deep-frying the pastries, the product is oven-baked for a softer texture, while allulose is used to reduce sugar content. item.title: HD KSOE wins $228.6 mil. order for 2 LPG carriers
item.description: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (KSOE) said Monday it has secured a 308.4 billion-won ($228.6 million) order for two liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carriers. HD KSOE, the shipbuilding subholding company of HD Hyundai, said its affiliate, HD Hyundai Samho, will build the vessels for an Asian client and deliver them by the first half of 2030. With the latest contract, HD KSOE has secured orders worth $22.1 billion for 201 vessels so far this year, achieving 94.9 percent of its annual order target.

item.title: Chinese man gets suspended sentence for stealing 100 BTS concert wristbands to resell
item.description: A Chinese man in his 40s has received a suspended prison sentence for stealing 100 admission wristbands at a BTS concert venue in Busan with the intention of reselling them at inflated prices. According to legal sources Sunday, the Busan District Court sentenced the man, identified only as A, to 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, on charges of aggravated theft. The man was charged with stealing 100 admission wristbands from an event booth set up at the Busan Asiad Auxiliary Stadium in Yeonje District, Busan, at around noon on June 12, along with two unidentified accomplices. According to the court ruling, A arrived at Incheon International Airport the day before the theft and met with two accomplices to plan the resale of BTS concert tickets at inflated prices. However, the concert organizer had introduced measures to prevent ticket scalping, requiring attendees to present identification matching their mobile tickets before receiving admission wristbands. item.title: 15 years, 164 awards: How Global Korea Award tracked changing Korea
item.description: In 2012, The Korea Times established the Korea Multicultural Youth Awards to encourage students from multicultural families who struggle with cultural differences and language barriers. Rebranded as the Global Korea Awards last year, the program marks its 15th anniversary this year. Over that span, it has recognized 152 students and individuals and 12 volunteer groups, teachers and institutions, distributing 164 awards in total. The Ministry of Gender Equality and Family has sponsored the program since its founding, and the grand prize winner receives the minister’s award. Among the honors is the Semoon Chang Award for students with outstanding foreign language skills, created in 2015 with column fees donated by Chang Se-moon, a former Korea Times columnist and retired economics professor at the University of South Alabama. GKL said Monday that its report received the Platinum Award in the sustainability report category of the 2025/26 LACP Spotlight Awards, organized by the U.S.-based League of American Communications Professionals (LACP). The annual competition evaluates corporate annual reports and sustainability reports from around the world, attracting about 500 companies and organizations each year. item.title: Sungkyunkwan University team develops ultrasensitive vitamin C sensor using AI
item.description: A Sungkyunkwan University research team has developed an ultrasensitive sensor capable of detecting even trace amounts of vitamin C by using artificial intelligence (AI) to optimize sensor fabrication conditions. The team was led by Park Jin-sung, a professor in the Department of Bio-Mechatronics Engineering, according to the university. Other researchers included Park Daeil, Choi Do-eun, Jo Won-jun, Kim Chi-hyun and Park Joo-hyung. Rather than conducting numerous trial-and-error experiments, the team used AI to identify promising fabrication conditions based on a relatively small dataset and then verified the sensor's performance through actual experiments. item.title: CJ ONE offers foreign tourists free coupon package for Korea trips
item.description: Foreign tourists visiting Korea can now score discounts on everything from pastries and convenience-store snacks to beauty treatments and duty-free shopping through a free coupon package from CJ ONE, a major Korean retail and lifestyle rewards platform. item.title: Buick opens Electra E7 orders, targets Korea's premium SUV market
item.description: General Motors’ (GM) premium brand Buick said Monday it had opened preorders for the Electra E7, its first model in Korea, with prices starting at 43.6 million won ($32,500). The initial ordering period, which began on Monday, is reserved for customers who previously registered for advance reservations, while orders from the general public will open Wednesday. The Electra E7 is a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) combining a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated gasoline engine with an electric motor, delivering a maximum electric driving range of up to 126 kilometers and a total driving range exceeding 1,000 kilometers. Customers can choose between two lithium iron phosphate battery options, with capacities of 19.7 kilowatt-hours and 31.7 kilowatt-hours, offering certified electric-only ranges of 80 kilometers and 126 kilometers, respectively. The vehicle supports multiple driving modes, including EV, power-retention and intelligent hybrid modes, as well as DC fast charging and vehicle-to-load technology, which allows its battery to power external electrical devices. item.title: S. Korea monitoring troop activities after N. Korean vessel marked 'coast guard' spotted near NLL
item.description: South Korea's military said Monday it is monitoring North Korean troop movements near the maritime border following a media report of a North Korean vessel marked "coast guard" spotted near the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the Yellow Sea. Earlier in the day, a local newspaper reported the vessel marked "coast guard," the first North Korean ship seen bearing those words, was spotted last week near the de facto maritime border between the two Koreas. The vessel was equipped with what appeared to be 76-millimeter caliber naval artillery, the report said, noting it appeared to be monitoring Chinese fishing boats nearby. "Our military is closely monitoring and following the activities of North Korean forces," Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) spokesperson Capt. Jang Do-young told a press briefing. "The activities of North Korean vessels in the front-line maritime areas are under real-time monitoring of our military's surveillance systems," Jang said, without elaborating on the role and purpose of the spotted vessel. item.title: Lawmakers propose measures aimed at preventing covert filming using smart glasses
item.description: A group of lawmakers proposed on Monday a revision to rules aimed at mandating smart glasses to include functions that signal to others when photos are taken or videos are recorded, amid growing concerns of covert filming using such devices. The proposed amendment also aims to set guidelines so that users of smart glasses notify people nearby before taking a photo or recording a video. Violators could face fines of up to 10 million won ($7,424). "We plan to prepare guidelines to protect people's privacy from the recording phase, to prevent cases where people belatedly discover themselves being covertly filmed using smart glasses online," said ruling Democratic Party Rep. Lee Ju-hee, the lead sponsor of the bill. The move comes as concerns grow over smart glasses being used for spy cams and cheating at national or corporate exams. Currently, widely used devices, such as Meta AI glasses, feature a bright white LED light that lights up or blinks during capture, but lower-priced models are said to either lack such a feature or make it hard for others to detect whether recording is taking pla

item.title: Son Yong-seok named Hankook Ilbo CEO
item.description: The Hankook Ilbo, the sister company of The Korea Times, said Monday that it has named Son Yong-seok, chief of its advertising business headquarters, as the paper’s new CEO and publisher. Son will begin his term on Dec. 1. Son is the first photojournalist to head a major Korean news outlet. A graduate of the Department of Korean Language and Literature at Chung-Ang University, Son joined the Hankook Ilbo in 1990. He later served as chief of the photo desk and head of the AD strategy headquarters. He also served as president of the Korea Press Photographers Association and currently chairs the Advertising Council of the Korea Newspaper Association. In a related reshuffle, Lee Tae-gyu, chief of the news content headquarters, will concurrently serve as editor. Park Il-keun, chief editorial writer, will lead the advertising business headquarters. Lee Sung-chul, who has served as CEO since December 2022, has been appointed an adviser.

item.title: Seoul Metropolitan Library to be renovated into multipurpose cultural space
item.description: The Seoul Metropolitan Library, housed in the former city hall, will be renovated into a multipurpose cultural space by 2029, city officials said Monday. The renovation project coincides with the 100th anniversary of the building's construction in 1926. A state-designated cultural heritage site, the building was converted into a public library in 2012. A public design competition will open Tuesday for the renovation of the library's four floors and an overhaul of its third-basement-floor archive, with the five floors spanning 7,556 square meters. To create a more spacious and open atmosphere, the city plans to relocate part of the library's current book collection from the upper floors to an underground storage area and install lower, more flexible bookshelves. The renovation will also add a kids' lounge for families and an open lecture hall for talks, educational programs and small gatherings. While the building's exterior and windows will be preserved in accordance with cultural heritage protection rules, the interior will be redesigned so citizens can freely spend time enjoying books

item.title: Immigration detainee denied video call with dying father, rights watchdog says
item.description: Korea's rights watchdog said Monday it recommended that an immigration detention center minimize restrictions on detainees' freedom of communication, after it found that a facility violated a detainee's right to pursue happiness by not allowing a video call with a dying father. The National Human Rights Commission of Korea, which made the recommendation last week, called on the center to guarantee that detainees can use their personal mobile phones to the extent necessary in urgent and serious humanitarian cases, such as when a family member is critically ill or dying. The complainant, a foreign national held at the center, brought the case to the commission in November 2025. The detainee claimed that they were refused after asking staff for permission to use a personal mobile phone to see their critically ill father one last time over a video call. The father died that day, and the complainant said the refusal deprived them of the most basic human right to pursue happiness. The center said it had never received the request and would have considered necessary measures if it had. It adde
